top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: Beijing confirmed that Xi Jinping will make a state visit to the United States from Wednesday, with talks with Trump in Washington on Thursday, their second summit in six months. The same day, Chinese state media said the country's former top general, Zhang Youxia, had been expelled from the Communist Party, and the party set its big autumn meeting for late October. Elsewhere it was a day of results and rulings: Russia's ruling party was awarded a record 355 Duma seats in an election with no anti-war party on the national ballot, and a Seoul court jailed five former commanders over the 2024 martial law bid. The Middle East stayed tense rather than moving, with Iran's Revolutionary Guards issuing new threats and the Houthis pressing forward in Yemen. With nearly 130 leaders now gathering in New York, this week's summit and the UN meetings will show whether any of that tension eases.

stories.headline: China confirms Xi Jinping will make a state visit to the US from Sept 23 to 25
stories.summary: China's Foreign Ministry confirmed on Sept 21 that President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from Sept 23 to 25 at President Donald Trump's invitation. The two are expected to hold talks in Washington on Thursday, their second summit this year after Trump's visit to Beijing in May, with trade and tariffs, artificial intelligence, Taiwan and the Iran war expected to feature. Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the reciprocal visits within six months of 'historic, milestone significance'.

stories.headline: China expels its former top general Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli from the Communist Party, state media say
stories.summary: State news agency Xinhua reported on Sept 21 that Zhang Youxia, who had been the senior vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission and China's highest-ranked general, and fellow officer Liu Zhenli have been expelled from the Communist Party, saying their cases involved 'exceptionally large sums of money'. The defence ministry announced in January that both were under investigation for 'serious violations of discipline and the law'. The details come from Chinese state media and have not been independently verified.

stories.headline: United Russia takes a record 355 of 450 Duma seats in a vote without anti-war parties, election officials say
stories.summary: Russia's election chief Ella Pamfilova said on Sept 21 that preliminary results gave Vladimir Putin's United Russia 355 of the Duma's 450 seats, above its previous record of 343. Near-complete returns put the party on 57.83 per cent of the party-list vote, up from 49.8 per cent in 2021, with turnout given as 59.3 per cent. The three-day election was tightly controlled and no party critical of the Kremlin or the war in Ukraine was on the national ballot; the anti-war Yabloko party won no national seats but crossed the 5 per cent threshold for Novgorod's regional parliament.

stories.headline: Houthis push for strategic heights in Yemen after a report that Trump called off US strikes at the last minute
stories.summary: Houthi fighters were pushing on Sept 21 to seize high ground that would cut the Red Sea coast off from remaining areas held by Saudi-backed forces, after a media report that President Donald Trump called off US airstrikes on the group at the last minute. Washington has so far rebuffed Saudi requests to join the fight. The Houthis said on Sept 19 that they had fired on Riyadh; Saudi Arabia has not commented, and the battlefield claims have not been independently verified.

stories.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they would use new weapons against new targets if the US attacks again
stories.summary: A spokesman for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Sept 21 that there would be 'significant changes in our defence and our counteroffensive' in the event of a new US attack, adding that Iran would 'introduce new weapons with new capabilities' and that its targets 'will not necessarily be the same as before'. The statement is a warning from one party to the conflict, not evidence of new capabilities. Almost seven months into the war, the two sides remain in a stalemate.

stories.headline: UN expert says US strikes on alleged drug boats breached international law and could be crimes against humanity
stories.summary: A report by UN Special Rapporteur Ben Saul concludes that US airstrikes on vessels alleged to be trafficking drugs breached international law and could constitute crimes against humanity. It counts at least 68 strikes in the Caribbean and Pacific since September last year, killing more than 220 people, and argues that the targets had not staged an armed attack that would trigger a right of self-defence. US Southern Command said two days earlier that its latest strike killed four 'narco-terrorists' on a vessel it said was confirmed to be trafficking drugs.

stories.headline: CNN, MS NOW and Politico say they will sue over their White House ban
stories.summary: The three outlets said in a joint statement on Sept 21 that they are pursuing legal action to 'protect our First Amendment rights' after their reporters were denied entry to the White House on Sept 19. President Trump announced the ban on Sept 18, accusing them of writing 'fiction or lies' about his administration, and responded on Truth Social that he was targeting 'fake news' rather than the free press.

stories.headline: Five former South Korean military commanders jailed for up to 18 years over the 2024 martial law bid
stories.summary: A Seoul court on Sept 21 sentenced former Defence Counterintelligence Command chief Yeo In-hyung to 18 years and former Capital Defence Command head Lee Jin-woo to 15 years for their roles in ex-president Yoon Suk Yeol's short-lived martial law declaration in December 2024; prosecutors had sought 30 years for both. Former army chief Park An-su received 10 years, former Defence Intelligence Command head Moon Sang-ho 12 years and former special warfare commander Kwak Jong-keun nine.

stories.headline: Anwar says he reminded the Pardons Board to weigh public confidence before Najib's move to house arrest
stories.summary: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Sept 20 that he had reminded the Pardons Board to consider how former prime minister Najib Razak's conditional pardon, which moves him from jail to house arrest, could affect public confidence and Malaysia's international reputation. He rejected suggestions that he had paved the way for the decision, saying every prisoner has the right to appeal; the board is chaired by the King, Sultan Ibrahim.

stories.headline: Indonesia says it is doing 'everything' but is still struggling to contain forest fires as Malaysia steps up haze measures
stories.summary: Indonesian authorities said on Sept 21 that dozens of aircraft and thousands of personnel are fighting large forest and peatland fires but are struggling to contain them, citing the size of the territory and the difficulty of extinguishing peat. Neighbouring Malaysia has stepped up its own efforts against the resulting haze.

stories.headline: Australia says its export controls are 'robust' after a report that F-35 parts were diverted to Hong Kong
stories.summary: Australia said on Sept 21 that it protects classified defence technology and has 'robust' export controls, responding to a Politico report that a shipment of F-35 parts, including a canopy with radar-resistant technology, was unexpectedly diverted to Hong Kong after leaving Australia. A US House committee is examining how the diversion happened.

stories.headline: Ireland's data watchdog fines Google 403 million euros over location data
stories.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission, acting as Google's lead regulator in the European Union, said on Sept 21 that it had fined the company 403 million euros (about S$590 million) for unfair processing and excessive retention of users' location data between May 2018 and February 2020, in breach of GDPR. Google was given six months to bring its processing into compliance; the company said it has updated its policies since 2019 and added tools for managing location data.

stories.headline: German car workers hold nationwide protests over job cuts
stories.summary: The IG Metall union said protests would take place at more than 280 sites across Germany on Sept 21, with tens of thousands of workers expected, to press government and management to protect jobs and plants. The industry is under pressure from Chinese competition, weak domestic demand and US tariffs; Volkswagen plans to cut 100,000 jobs by the end of the decade, and Mercedes-Benz and BMW are also downsizing.

stories.headline: Denmark, Greenland and the US to sign a Greenland security deal on Sept 22
stories.summary: Denmark said the agreement, due to be signed on Sept 22, places Arctic security under NATO's shared responsibility, and both Copenhagen and Nuuk said it respects Greenland's sovereignty. President Trump has described the deal as giving the US 'permanent control' over Greenland's security, a characterisation Denmark and Greenland have not confirmed.

stories.headline: Three detained in South Africa over one of nine recent killings of women east of Johannesburg
stories.summary: South African police described the detention of a man and two women as a 'breakthrough' in the death of Jabulile Ntimba, whose body was found in Dawn Park last week, the most recent of nine cases in the area in which women's bodies were left by roadsides. The suspects were due in court on Sept 21; police have not said the nine cases are linked.

stories.headline: New air traffic control failure delays flights at several UK airports
stories.summary: Britain's air traffic control provider NATS said a failure on Sept 21 delayed flights at airports including Manchester, Glasgow and Belfast, with Gatwick and London City warning of some disruption. It came less than two weeks after a separate NATS system problem halted flights across the country.

stories.headline: China's Communist Party sets its fifth plenum for Oct 26 to 29
stories.summary: The Politburo, meeting on Sept 21, set the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee for Oct 26 to 29 in Beijing, state news agency Xinhua reported. The session will study issues concerning 'full and rigorous party self-governance', the agency said earlier.

stories.headline: Textile factory fire in Foshan, southern China, kills eight
stories.summary: A fire that broke out at about 3.12pm on Sept 20 in a two-storey building in an industrial park in Foshan, Guangdong province, killed eight people and injured one, Chinese state media reported on Sept 21. It was put out in about an hour.

stories.headline: UN rapporteur says Russia has stepped up repression of critics abroad
stories.summary: The UN Special Rapporteur on human rights in Russia told the Human Rights Council in Geneva on Sept 21 that Moscow has intensified surveillance, intimidation and reprisals against critics overseas since 2022, calling it one of the most prolific perpetrators of 'transnational repression', including attempted assassinations, assaults and poisonings.

stories.headline: US proposes an AI incident-notification channel with China as Bessent and He Lifeng wrap up pre-summit talks
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Vice-Premier He Lifeng ended a day of talks in New York on Sept 20 with the US side proposing a mechanism for the two countries to notify each other of AI-related incidents that rise to a national-security level, for Presidents Trump and Xi to consider at their White House summit on Thursday, Sept 24. Bessent called it a 'very successful engagement' and said more transparency between 'the No. 1 and the No. 2 AI powers' was important; Chinese state media described the exchanges as 'frank, in-depth, and constructive'. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said teams are still working through which 'non-sensitive' goods could see mutual tariff cuts, and neither official reported progress on the flow of critical minerals.

stories.headline: Iran's foreign minister heads to the UN as Tehran says Hormuz stays shut and Trump floats a meeting with Pezeshkian
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi left Tehran on Sept 20 for the UN General Assembly with a stopover in Qatar, Iranian state media said, hours after Iran's central military command warned that it had information the US was preparing to resume strikes. Al Jazeera reported that President Trump told Fox News his options on Iran included further military action, economic pressure or a deal, and that he would be open to meeting President Masoud Pezeshkian in New York. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until Washington met what Iran calls its commitments under an earlier agreement. Qatar's foreign ministry said its officials were carrying proposals between capitals and had heard US assurances that Washington wants a deal.

stories.headline: Merz calls German state election results a 'disaster' as the Left Party wins Berlin and the AfD leads in the north-east
stories.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he would stay on after two state elections on Sept 20 went badly for his Christian Democrats. In Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, projections first showed the CDU scraping in with its worst result there and later put it below the 5 per cent needed to stay in the state parliament, the BBC reported; the far-right AfD was on course to top the poll, though other parties refuse to govern with it. In Berlin the Left Party took 25.3 per cent, ahead of the CDU on 19, the AfD on 16 and the SPD on 12.1, with counting still under way late on Sunday, and its lead candidate Elif Eralp repeated a pledge to nationalise private housing associations that hold a large share of the city's homes. The votes came two weeks after the AfD's win in Saxony-Anhalt. Update, Sept 21: the AfD finished as the strongest party in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, more than doubling its 2021 result, and the CDU's showing there was its worst in any state election since 1949, The Straits Times reported; Merz faces calls to resign after less than 17 months in office.

stories.headline: Zelensky says he and Trump have agreed to meet in New York
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sept 20 that he had spoken with US President Donald Trump and that the two agreed to meet in New York during the UN General Assembly, a meeting he said 'could change a lot'. 'There is diplomatic momentum,' he wrote on X, thanking Trump for this month's visit to Kyiv by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and referring to ideas for de-escalation steps and security guarantees. CNA reports that Trump's UN schedule includes a bilateral meeting with Ukraine's leader.

stories.headline: Afghan officials say Pakistani airstrikes killed at least three people in the north-east
stories.summary: Taliban deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat said airstrikes on Sept 21 hit at least one house in Kunar province, killing three members of one family and injuring four, and that two locations in Paktika's Barmal district were also bombed without casualties. Pakistan's military did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and the account has not been independently verified. The strikes follow an attack on a police facility in north-west Pakistan days earlier that killed at least 16 people, and come after nearly three months of relative calm between the neighbours. Islamabad accuses Kabul of harbouring militants who attack across the border, which the Taliban government denies.

stories.headline: Three South Korean officers injured in an explosion inside the Demilitarised Zone
stories.summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said on Sept 21 that three military officers were hurt by 'an explosion of unknown cause' during an operation south of the Military Demarcation Line inside the DMZ. Two were evacuated by helicopter and the third was to be moved by road before being airlifted; the military gave no details of their injuries. It was not clear whether the blast came from a North Korean mine, a South Korean mine or another device.

stories.headline: North Korea says no new sanctions will block its development, rejecting a monitoring group's report
stories.summary: A North Korean foreign ministry spokesperson, quoted by state news agency KCNA on Sept 21, accused the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team of fabricating a report to portray what Pyongyang calls normal economic cooperation as illegal, and said the country would not tolerate efforts to curb its ties with other states. The 11-member monitoring group said in a Sept 16 report that North Korea continued to send workers abroad in breach of UN Security Council resolutions, earning an estimated US$450 million to US$800 million in 2025 for its weapons programmes. The statement is a North Korean state-media claim.

stories.headline: Two New Zealand navy ships transited the Taiwan Strait last week, Wellington confirms
stories.summary: New Zealand's Defence Force said on Sept 21 that the frigate Te Mana and the oiler Aotearoa passed through the Taiwan Strait on Sept 18 as part of a three-month Indo-Pacific deployment. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon called the transit 'a routine activity' and said he did not expect a backlash from China, which claims the waterway and had not commented. Separately on Sept 21, Australia and New Zealand signed Plan Tasman, a pact to deepen cooperation between their navies on training, engineering and operations.

stories.headline: Anthony Loke to attend APEC transport meeting in Beijing before returning to handle his Cabinet resignation
stories.summary: Malaysia's Transport Ministry said on Sept 21 that Anthony Loke will go ahead with an official visit to China for the 12th APEC Transport Ministers' Meeting in Beijing on Sept 21 and 22, where he is due to sign two memorandums of understanding on transport cooperation and aviation safety, and will then join Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's delegation in Shanghai. Loke, the Democratic Action Party's secretary-general, offered to resign from the Cabinet on Sept 19 after former prime minister Najib Razak was granted a conditional pardon allowing house arrest; Anwar has said he will meet Loke on his return. The ministry said its operations would continue without disruption.

stories.headline: Australia forecasts deaths will outnumber births from the 2060s as population growth slows
stories.summary: The Australian government forecast on Sept 21 that deaths would exceed births for the first time in the 2060s, and that population growth would slow to 0.9 per cent a year over the next four decades from 1.4 per cent over the past 40 years, as fertility declines and net migration is cut. It warned that an ageing population will raise demand for health and aged care and tighten the labour supply.

stories.headline: Facebook and Instagram recover after a brief outage
stories.summary: Meta's Facebook and Instagram were disrupted for thousands of users from about 8.55am Singapore time on Sept 21, with reports to Downdetector peaking at more than 17,000 for Facebook and more than 5,000 for Instagram before falling sharply about an hour later. Downdetector's figures are user-submitted reports, so the number actually affected may differ. Meta had not commented.

stories.headline: White House weighs an outside commission with a veto over NIH research grants, US media report
stories.summary: White House officials have discussed creating an external commission able to veto grants awarded by the National Institutes of Health, according to anonymous sources cited by Politico, The New York Times and The Washington Post over the weekend. The Post reported that budget director Russell Vought has accused the agency of funding 'woke' research. The plan has not been announced. Research!America president Russ Paulsen said in a Sept 20 statement that 'adding more bureaucrats would slow medical progress to a grinding halt'.

stories.headline: Explosions at a Syrian army weapons depot near Aleppo injure at least four
stories.summary: A series of explosions early on Sept 21 at a Syrian army site near the town of al-Eis, south of Aleppo, injured at least four people, the state news agency SANA reported, citing the head of civil defence operations in Aleppo. The governor urged residents to stay indoors and roads to the site were closed; an Al Jazeera correspondent reported further blasts after the first. The cause has not been stated. Similar depot explosions have occurred in Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.

stories.headline: Typhoon Dujuan nears Japan's eastern coast with warnings of heavy rain and landslides
stories.summary: The Japan Meteorological Agency said Typhoon Dujuan, the 25th of the season, was expected to pass near the Boso Peninsula in Chiba, east of Tokyo, from the evening of Sept 21, and warned of heavy rain, strong winds and landslides, with bands of intense rain possible across the Kanto-Koshin and Tokai regions. The storm has already closed sections of highway during a five-day holiday period.

stories.headline: Australia to bid for a UN Security Council seat from 2029
stories.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese launched a campaign in New York on Sept 21 for one of the two non-permanent Security Council seats available to Australia's regional group from 2029. Australia's last two-year term on the council ended in 2014. Albanese said his relationships with other leaders would help the bid and that the country 'punches above our weight'.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang dismisses AI extinction warnings as 'doomsday narratives'
stories.summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang rejected warnings that artificial intelligence could lead to humanity's extinction within the next decade, the BBC reported. '2030 is not going to be the end of the world. There is 0% chance that's going to be the end of the world,' he said in an interview.

stories.headline: Seven Ethiopian armed groups form an alliance to remove Abiy's government
stories.summary: Seven armed groups announced on Sept 20 that they had formed the 'Ethiopian Peoples' Forces Alliance for Survival' with the aim of replacing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government with an inclusive transitional administration, Al Jazeera reported. Members include the Amhara Fano National Movement, which has fought federal forces in the Amhara region. The former adversaries said they would settle their differences; the federal government's response was not included in the report.

stories.headline: Japan's over-65s reach a record 29.6 per cent of the population
stories.summary: Government estimates released on Sept 20 put Japan's population aged 65 or older at a record 36.24 million, up 20,000 from a year earlier and 29.6 per cent of the total - the highest share among countries with more than 40 million people. Those aged 75 or older make up 17.7 per cent. The elderly population is projected to reach 39.45 million, or 36.3 per cent, by 2045.

stories.headline: ICE officer shoots and wounds a man in Austin, Texas
stories.summary: An Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer shot a man in the torso during a brief foot pursuit shortly before 1pm on Sept 20 in Austin, city officials said; he was taken to hospital in serious but stable condition. Austin Police Chief Lisa Davis gave the account at a press conference. ICE, the Department of Homeland Security and the Texas Department of Public Safety had not commented by the time of the reports.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Negeri Sembilan's ruler dismisses the state's executive council members
stories.summary: The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan has revoked the appointments of state executive council members with immediate effect, a palace statement said, on the grounds that their actions and statements on Sept 15 breached the oath of office they signed on Aug 7. Menteri Besar Ismail Lasim is to propose new candidates so that the state administration continues to function, in line with the state constitution.

stories.headline: Trump lines up two days of meetings as nearly 130 leaders gather for the UN General Assembly
stories.summary: President Trump is due in New York on Monday afternoon, US time, for two days at the UN General Assembly that will include bilateral meetings with the leaders of Ukraine and the United Kingdom and with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani. The US ambassador to the UN said his address would highlight how the administration has 'confronted complex problems head-on'. Nearly 130 heads of state and government are attending, with the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine dominating the agenda and the UN itself under financial strain after US funding cuts.

stories.headline: France to summon Iran's ambassador after Tehran shuts a French language centre
stories.summary: France's foreign ministry said on Sept 20 it would summon Iran's ambassador and take 'appropriate measures' after Iranian authorities sealed a French language centre affiliated with its embassy in Tehran, which Iran accused of posing a security threat. Spokesman Pascal Confavreux called the closure 'unjustifiable and unacceptable', citing an assault on two French embassy staff in July. Iran has accused France of cultural interference; the two foreign ministers are due to meet at the United Nations this week.

stories.headline: Trump administration has prepared sanctions on the entire International Criminal Court, sources say
stories.summary: Two sources familiar with the matter said the Trump administration has drawn up sanctions against the International Criminal Court as an institution and plans to announce them soon, The Straits Times reported from wire copy. Washington has already sanctioned individual ICC judges and prosecutors and wants the court to drop arrest warrants for Israeli leaders and a past probe into US troops in Afghanistan. The plan has not been officially announced and the report rests on unnamed sources.

stories.headline: Iran's economy shrank 10.1 per cent in the spring quarter, official data shows
stories.summary: Iran's gross domestic product contracted 10.1 per cent year-on-year between late March and late June, the first quarter of the Persian calendar, the Statistical Center of Iran said on Sept 20. The period covers the early months of the war that began with US-Israeli strikes in late February and Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The figure is the Iranian government's own; the economy was already strained by sanctions, high inflation and a falling currency.
stories.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Statistical Center of Iran)

stories.headline: Macron and Carney pledge closer France-Canada ties at a meeting off Canada's Atlantic coast
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced closer ties on Sept 20 at a joint news conference in Saint Pierre and Miquelon, the small French territory off Newfoundland. 'We both believe that our countries are two great, independent nations who want to remain so,' Macron said; Carney said history remembers 'those who defend their sovereignty'. Both governments have strained relations with Washington.
stories.source: CNA, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Qatar's prime minister calls the fallout of the Iran war an 'earthquake' and urges a regional security framework
stories.summary: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, told a Qatar Economic Forum event in New York on Sept 20 that the region needs a 'framework in which sovereignty is respected' and in which no state threatens another, warning against 'cycles of escalation'. Al Jazeera also reported him saying Doha is working to revive talks between Iran and the United States. Qatar has been the channel for Iran's conditions for ending the war.

stories.headline: Russia vows to 'intensify' strikes on Kyiv after the Moscow drone attack as exit poll shows ruling party winning
stories.summary: Russia's defence ministry said on Sept 20 that it would 'continue and intensify' strikes on what it called military targets in Kyiv, accusing Ukraine of trying to disrupt the final day of Russia's parliamentary election. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said the overnight attack involved some 1,600 drones, 450 of them aimed at the capital, which would make it the largest on Moscow since 2022; the figure is a Russian claim and is not independently verified. Regional officials reported two dead, and President Zelensky said a key oil facility and a logistics site were hit. An exit poll by a state-run pollster put United Russia on 49.4 per cent in what AFP described as tightly controlled elections.

stories.headline: South African investigative journalist reported missing in Djibouti
stories.summary: The family of Micah Reddy, Africa editor of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists, said on Sept 20 that he had not been heard from since Saturday while on a reporting trip to Djibouti, where he arrived on Thursday. The Committee to Protect Journalists said it was 'increasingly alarmed' that neither Reddy nor his fixer, Kooki Mahmoud, could be reached, and that their reporting was not focused on Djibouti. Djiboutian authorities had not commented.

stories.headline: Eighteen suspects in the 2021 killing of Haiti's president are flown to the US for trial
stories.summary: A military aircraft took 18 suspects in the assassination of President Jovenel Moise from Haiti to the United States on Sept 20, said Jason Reding Quinones, the US attorney for the Southern District of Florida, who called it 'the next major phase' in the case. In May a Miami federal jury convicted four South Florida men of plotting the killing by hiring mercenaries to attack Moise at his Port-au-Prince home.

stories.headline: Trump says his planned triumphal arch in Washington will double as a military complex
stories.summary: President Trump said in a social media post on Sept 20 that he is updating plans for his proposed triumphal arch in Washington at the 'strong request' of the US military and for 'national security purposes'. He said the complex would 'house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers' on its roof and plaza. The arch was first proposed in April; the Pentagon has not publicly detailed any such request.
stories.source: BBC, The Straits Times, CNA, Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Thousands march in France against a police use-of-force bill critics call a 'licence to kill'
stories.summary: Protesters marched in Paris and other French cities on Sept 20 against a bill, approved by the National Assembly in July and now before the Senate, under which a law-enforcement officer who uses a weapon is presumed to have acted lawfully. Rights groups and left-wing politicians including Mathilde Panot of France Unbowed joined the marches. Supporters say the measure protects officers; opponents say it removes accountability.

stories.headline: Trump tells Fox News the Houthis have agreed not to fight the US and that 'big things' are coming on Iran
stories.summary: Fox News reporter Trey Yingst said President Trump told him on Sept 20 that Washington is 'in constant communication with the Houthis and that they've agreed not to fight the United States', even as the Iran-allied group steps up attacks on Saudi Arabia and seizes territory from Yemen's Saudi-backed government. Yingst said Trump described himself as in 'deciding mode' on Iran and said 'big things will be happening in the not-so-distant future'. The remarks are reported second-hand by Fox News; the Houthis have not confirmed any understanding with Washington.
stories.source: The Straits Times (AFP, citing Fox News), Ukrinform

stories.headline: Trial opens in Hong Kong over the 2023 murder of socialite Abby Choi
stories.summary: The trial of Abby Choi's former husband and his family members on charges including murder and preventing lawful burial was due to begin at Hong Kong's High Court on Sept 21 with jury selection, the South China Morning Post reported. Choi, a model and socialite, was found dismembered in a rented village house in February 2023; police have pointed to a property dispute as a possible motive. The trial is expected to run until December.

stories.headline: Iran warns any new US attack would bring sustained retaliation against American bases
stories.summary: Iran's military central command said on state media on Sept 20 that it had information a new attack by the United States and its allies was being prepared, and that any such strike would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests, with Washington's regional allies treated as parties to the conflict. It gave no details of the information. The warning follows Houthi-claimed missile and drone strikes on Riyadh and the Saudi port of Yanbu on Sept 19, which Saudi Arabia has not commented on, and a US State Department security alert about possible escalation and airspace closures.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Layoffs are the number to know today: 4,620 people were retrenched in the second quarter, the most since late 2020, and fewer of them found new work within six months, even as overall hiring kept growing. On the commute, rules taking effect on Wednesday make loud audio and feet on bus seats a finable offence. The deposit scheme for drink containers is catching on, with about 33 million bottles and cans returned since April and a new automated sorting plant running in Tuas. The courts were busy, led by a coroner's inquiry into last year's Hougang flat fire and a long jail term for a serial sex offender. Separately, seized luxury goods from the S$3 billion laundering case sold for well above their estimates. The lighter talk is about neighbours and life choices. Watch Wednesday: the bus rules start and the next COE results land the same day.

stories.headline: Vivian Balakrishnan to deliver Singapore's statement at the UN General Assembly on Sept 26
stories.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Sept 21 that Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan will be in New York from Sept 22 to 28 for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly and will deliver Singapore's national statement at the general debate on Sept 26. He will host several events, including the ministerial meeting of the Global Governance Group of small and medium-sized states, and attend a high-level meeting of the Global Alliance for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution.

stories.headline: About 33 million bottles and cans returned under the deposit scheme so far as a new Tuas sorting plant is unveiled
stories.summary: Around 33 million drink containers have been returned since the Beverage Container Return Scheme began in April, through about 1,300 reverse vending machines that refund the 10-cent deposit. A new 2,000 sq m counting and sorting facility at Cora Environment in Tuas, shown to the media this week, takes in around 1,200 large bags of flattened containers a day and uses magnets and infrared sorting to separate six material types without manual sorting; The Straits Times reports it has handled 27.5 million containers in under two months.

stories.headline: Seized luxury goods from the S$3 billion money laundering case sell for more than S$1.1 million at auction
stories.summary: All 337 lots of handbags and jewellery in the first auction of assets seized in the case were sold, fetching more than S$1.1 million in total, with some going far above their estimates; a Chrome Hearts pendant estimated at S$1,000 to S$1,500 sold for S$11,000. A limited-edition Louis Vuitton bag made with artist Yayoi Kusama drew 81 bids, the most of any item. The sale, managed by Deloitte for the police with proceeds going to the Consolidated Fund, came days after properties linked to the case drew no bids.

stories.headline: 41 rare artefacts from the National Library of China to go on show in Singapore from Dec 7
stories.summary: A six-month exhibition on the Four Great Classical Novels opens at the National Library on Dec 7 with 41 artefacts on loan from the National Library of China, including two top-graded cultural relics and a rare edition of Water Margin, shown alongside items from Singapore's own collection.

stories.headline: Man, 53, arrested within four hours over a shop break-in along East Coast Road
stories.summary: Police said they were alerted at about 1.40pm on Sept 19 to a case of housebreaking and theft at a shop along East Coast Road, and identified and arrested the man within four hours of the report using police camera images and surveillance footage. He was due to be charged on Sept 21.

stories.headline: Kopitiam founder Lim Bee Huat sues a contractor over alleged defects at two Whitley Road bungalows
stories.summary: Lim, who is in his 70s, is suing Tiandi ACMV Engineering for breach of contract, alleging that defects from renovation work have made the two adjoining bungalows unfit for his family to move into, Lianhe Zaobao reported; he told the High Court on Sept 14 and 15 that the houses were unsuitable for habitation. The contractor denies responsibility and says the problems were caused by a separate contractor Lim engaged. The amount of any compensation is for the court to decide.

stories.headline: Engineer reportedly loses about S$80,000 to an 'online store' investment pitched by a Facebook friend of three years
stories.summary: A 49-year-old man told Shin Min Daily News that he lost about S$80,000 after a Facebook user he had chatted with for about three years persuaded him to invest in an online store. The account is the man's own, as reported by Shin Min, and has not been tested in court.

stories.headline: Retrenchments hit a post-pandemic high of 4,620 in Q2 as vacancies fall, though employment keeps growing
stories.summary: The Ministry of Manpower's second-quarter labour market report, released on Sept 21, shows 4,620 workers were retrenched, up from 3,830 in the first quarter and the most since the fourth quarter of 2020, or 2.0 per 1,000 employees. MOM attributed the rise to restructuring in outward-oriented sectors such as manufacturing, information and communications, and financial services, and said it has not established how much AI adoption is contributing. The share of retrenched workers who found a job within six months fell to 54.9 per cent from 60.7 per cent, and vacancies dropped to 68,600 in June from 73,300 in March, still 1.48 per unemployed person. Total employment grew by 11,400, a 19th straight quarter of growth, though resident employment growth slowed to 2,200 from 5,400; unemployment held at 1.9 per cent overall and 2.9 per cent for residents. Acting Manpower Minister Jasmin Lau pointed workers to career conversion programmes.

stories.headline: Bus passengers who play loud audio or put their feet on seats face fines of up to S$500 from Sept 23
stories.summary: The Land Transport Authority said on Sept 21 that new rules on bus passenger conduct take effect on Sept 23, bringing penalties in line with those on the rail network. Playing music loudly, putting feet on seats and similar disruptive acts will carry fines of up to S$500, while more serious offences such as causing obstruction or danger at interchanges and terminals, or soiling a bus or interchange, will carry up to S$5,000. Authorised staff of the four public bus operators, such as ticket inspectors and interchange staff, can issue notices; bus drivers will not, but can advise passengers to stop, ask them to alight, and call the operations control centre or the police. LTA said operators will exercise discretion, particularly for commuters with physical or mental health conditions. The regulations were passed in Parliament in October 2025.

stories.headline: Coroner's inquiry opens into the 2025 Hougang flat fire that killed a family of three
stories.summary: An inquiry opened on Sept 21 into the deaths of Lee Choon Geak, 62, his wife Seow Siew Choo, 56, and their daughter Grace Lee, 18, in a fire on Jan 9, 2025, in a third-floor flat at Block 971 Hougang Street 91. The court heard that the fire started at a wall socket in the master bedroom and spread through combustible items nearby, and an SCDF officer testified that firefighters had great difficulty opening the main door because of the items piled inside. A police investigator said the Housing Board learnt of the family's hoarding in February 2024 and that its officers were refused entry on two visits that year. The investigator told the court that no foul play was suspected.

stories.headline: Man, 21, gets 14 years' jail and 15 strokes of the cane for sexual offences against girls and other crimes
stories.summary: A 21-year-old was sentenced on Sept 21 to 14 years' jail and 15 strokes of the cane after pleading guilty to nine charges, including sexual assault involving penetration, statutory rape, aggravated outrage of modesty, rioting and causing hurt with a dangerous weapon, with 29 other charges taken into consideration. He committed the offences when he was between 15 and 17, against victims aged 13 to 16, and prosecutors said several were committed while he was on bail.

stories.headline: Two men arrested in Singapore over child abuse material after a tip-off from Italian police
stories.summary: The Singapore Police Force told Mothership that two men, aged 27 and 33, were arrested for possessing and gaining access to child abuse material after Italian authorities shared information about a Telegram group used to distribute it. Police in Italy arrested 17 people in their investigation into the Italy-based international network. The men's nationalities, and whether they knew each other, were not disclosed.

stories.headline: Two women arrested after police seize more than 900 suspected counterfeit items from Scotts Road shops
stories.summary: Officers from the Criminal Investigation Department raided two retail shops in a shopping mall along Scotts Road on Sept 16 and seized more than 900 trademark-infringing goods, including luxury bags, watches, apparel, footwear and accessories, the police said. Two women, aged 39 and 54, were arrested for their suspected involvement in selling counterfeit goods. Possessing goods with falsely applied trademarks for trade carries a fine of up to S$100,000, a jail term, or both.

stories.headline: Batam customs detain a Singaporean woman over 40 etomidate vape cartridges
stories.summary: Indonesian customs officers in Batam detained a Singaporean woman, identified only by her initials, after she arrived on the last ferry from Singapore at Harbour Bay Ferry Terminal on the night of Sept 3, allegedly carrying 40 vape cartridges containing etomidate, The Straits Times reported on Sept 21. Etomidate, the substance in the vapes known in Singapore as Kpods, is classed as a narcotic in Indonesia. Officers reportedly became suspicious because of the way she was walking.

stories.headline: Police warn that fake 'device locked' pop-ups bearing the SPF logo have re-emerged
stories.summary: The police said on Sept 20 that victims have again been seeing pop-up alerts carrying the Singapore Police Force logo which claim their device has been 'locked' for visiting illegal websites and demand payment of a fine within hours, with a countdown timer and a threat of permanent locking and prosecution. Victims who entered bank card details later found unauthorised foreign-currency charges, often larger than the supposed fine. The police said they do not remotely lock personal devices or demand payment through such alerts, and advised calling the ScamShield helpline on 1799 when unsure.

stories.headline: Solar power saved Singapore about S$123.8 million in fuel imports during the Hormuz price spike, report estimates
stories.summary: The Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air estimates that solar generation spared Singapore US$97 million (S$123.8 million) in power-related fossil fuel imports over five months earlier this year, nearly all of it avoided gas purchases, after prices jumped with the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. The same report estimates that reliance on imported fuel still cost Singapore an extra US$8.1 billion in the six months after the US-Iran war began. These are the think-tank's modelled estimates, not official figures; it recommends more solar, battery storage and regional grid links.

stories.headline: When condo defects surface years later, who pays?
stories.summary: The Straits Times examines why management corporations struggle to recover repair costs when cracks, seepage or loose concrete appear long after completion: responsibility is disputed among developers, architects, engineers and contractors, and developers often set up a company for a single project and wind it up soon after, leaving no one to sue. The piece follows lawsuits by the MCSTs of Foresque Residences, where an alleged problem surfaced about 10 years after completion, and Canberra Residences, whose MCST alleges defects remain unresolved despite a 2020 settlement. The claims are allegations before the courts.

stories.headline: Tollyjoy to wind down its baby-care brand after 55 years
stories.summary: Home-grown baby and mother-care company Tollyjoy, founded in 1971, said in a Sept 15 social media post that it will 'soon be taking our final bow and winding down the brand', calling it 'a bittersweet moment' and thanking the generations of families who used its products. It said customers can buy remaining stock from retail partners at farewell prices. The company also sells products under the Little Precious label. The Straits Times and CNA reported the closure on Sept 21.

stories.headline: Man jailed three months for secretly recording nude video calls with his ex-girlfriend
stories.summary: A 44-year-old South Korean man was sentenced to three months' jail after pleading guilty to one of three charges, which included filming a person without consent and an offence under the Films Act, Mothership reported, citing Shin Min Daily News. He had recorded video calls with his then girlfriend without her knowledge, and the recordings were later discovered by a new partner. The court barred publication of details that could identify the victim.

stories.headline: Stefanie Sun and JJ Lin turn up for Kit Chan's sold-out homecoming concert
stories.summary: Kit Chan brought her Atrium Live Tour to a sold-out Singapore Indoor Stadium on Sept 19, with fellow Singapore singers Stefanie Sun and JJ Lin among the local entertainment figures in the audience, CNA reported. Chan also paid tribute during the show to musicians including David Tao and the late Leslie Cheung.

stories.headline: Jurong tenants complain about an upstairs neighbour's daily cello practice
stories.summary: Four tenants living below a cello player told Shin Min Daily News that she practises almost every day, usually from 1pm and at times until 5pm, and that they cannot rest at home. The report carries the player's response as well.

stories.headline: Singaporean who moved to Thailand at 26 explains why he would not move back
stories.summary: In an Instagram video posted on Sept 18 that has been widely shared, Alden Lee, 40, said he would 'absolutely' not return to live in Singapore after more than a decade in Thailand, and spoke to Mothership about his reasons.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: Nothing that happened on Monday changed the shape of any of the three wars; the day's movement was mostly political. Russian election officials handed Putin's party a record 355 of 450 Duma seats in a vote that kept anti-war parties off the national ballot, a talking point for the Kremlin rather than a change at the front, where the last reported attack was a routine-sized drone raid. Around Iran the pattern was threat without action: the Revolutionary Guards promised new weapons and new targets if the US strikes again, and the Houthis kept advancing in Yemen after a report that Trump cancelled strikes on them. Gaza was not quiet despite the ceasefire: Palestinian medics told Al Jazeera that Israeli fire killed three people, a child among them, and Israeli troops detained dozens in a West Bank town after Sunday's shooting of an Israeli man. The real test comes in New York this week, where Zelensky expects to meet Trump and Iran's foreign minister is due at the UN.

theatres.name: Russia-Ukraine War
theatres.status: No new strikes were reported through the evening of Sept 21 after an overnight drone attack on a routine scale (Ukraine's Air Force says 147 of 172 drones were downed; Ukrainian claim, not independently verified). Russian election officials awarded United Russia a record 355 of 450 Duma seats in a vote with no anti-war party on the national ballot.

timeline.event: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, opening the largest land war in Europe since 1945.

Ukrainian drones kill five people in a residential area of Russia's Rostov region and three more in the Belgorod, Kursk and Moscow regions, regional governors say; four others are reported killed in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. Moscow's regional governor calls it 'one of the most massive drone attacks in recent memory' and Russia's defence ministry says it intercepted 822 drones overnight.

Russian drones and missiles kill two people and wound 14 at ArcelorMittal's steel plant in Kryvyi Rih, which partially halts production, and burn down stalls at Kyiv's Pochaina second-hand book market. Zelensky says Ukrainian cities were hit by more than 1,550 attack drones, nearly 1,560 guided bombs and 62 missiles over the past week, and renews his appeal for air defence.
A Spanish F-18 on NATO air-policing duty shoots down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from Moldova, about 24km north of Galati - the fourth drone downed over Romania this year.
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and President Vladimir Putin exchange messages reaffirming bilateral ties to mark Korean Liberation Day.

Six people are killed and four injured, including a 14-year-old, in Ukrainian missile strikes on Russia's Belgorod region overnight, acting governor Alexander Shuvaev says on Telegram. A woman is also killed by a drone strike on a home in the Astrakhan region, its governor says. The claims have not been independently verified.
Russian forces attack port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, Ukrainian authorities say.
Ukrainian energy company Naftogaz says Russia attacked its facilities 13 times over the past week.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the bloc plans its most far-reaching sanctions package against Russia in the autumn, without giving timing or detail.
Documents reported by The Straits Times show Binance gave Russian authorities client details later used to charge a Russian over donations to Ukraine.
Russia's defence ministry says air defences intercepted 205 Ukrainian drones over Russia and Crimea between Sunday night and Monday morning. Kyiv has not commented on the figure.
A separate overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port city of Odesa damages a civilian vessel and injures four people, Ukrainian authorities say.
Moldova's foreign ministry condemns a violation of its airspace by an unidentified aerial object that later exploded on Moldovan territory. It did not name a country responsible.
Italy's government says it sees no sign of a Russian link to the explosion at the Colleferro munitions plant, pushing back on speculation about sabotage.
A Russian court jails a prominent anti-war opposition politician for 11 years over comments about the war, the independent outlet Mediazona reports.
Moscow warns of 'consequences' after reports that British-made drones were used in strikes on Russian territory. London has not confirmed the reports.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin says 620 Ukrainian drones headed for the Moscow region between Monday evening and 5am and that 180 were downed over the region, in one of the largest attacks on the capital region of the war. Regional governor Andrei Vorobyov says drones hit a Wildberries warehouse and other sites and that three people, including a 10-year-old girl, were injured; Moscow's airports temporarily restricted flights. The figures are Russian officials' account and Kyiv has not commented.

Russia's foreign ministry says the United Kingdom 'will pay' for supplying drones used in strikes on Russian territory, hardening the earlier warning of 'consequences'. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Russia summons Japan's ambassador over the disputed Kuril Islands, which Tokyo calls the Northern Territories. Japan has not detailed its response.
Myanmar's leader Min Aung Hlaing is due in Moscow to meet President Vladimir Putin on his first trip there as president, one of a small number of leaders visiting Russia during the war.

A Russian missile attack kills 10 people in a village in Ukraine's north-eastern Kharkiv region, President Volodymyr Zelensky says, adding that Kyiv will respond. The figure is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified; Moscow has not commented.

A court in Stuttgart convicts a Ukrainian man over what German prosecutors describe as a Russian intelligence-linked plot to detonate parcels in Europe. Moscow has denied involvement in previous parcel-bomb cases.

The IAEA says a drone exploded at a bus stop used by staff of the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant, killing one person and injuring several others. Russian officials blame Ukraine and call it one of the most serious incidents at the plant; Kyiv has not commented. The IAEA reports no nuclear safety or security damage.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia has the right to treat British involvement in strikes on Russian territory as participation in the war, according to Interfax. London has not confirmed that British-made drones were used.
Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham says the United Kingdom 'supports Ukraine 100%' in response to Russia's warning over drones used against Russian territory.

Estonia's prime minister says the country is investigating whether Russia was involved in an arson attack last week on a building housing a defence contractor. No conclusion has been announced and Moscow has not commented.
Ukraine's new defence minister takes office after a parliamentary vote, which the country's anti-corruption agencies had opened a probe ahead of.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, publicly calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky since the 2022 invasion. Ukraine has not held elections under martial law.

German federal prosecutors say a second suspect in the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage investigation has been arrested in Croatia. Prosecutors have not published the suspect's identity or alleged role.
The Straits Times reports that Russia's 'pivot to Asia' is prioritising ties with isolated states over larger economies, as Moscow's options for trade and diplomacy narrow.
Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denies President Volodymyr Zelensky's claim that Pyongyang is deploying additional troops to support Russia. Kyiv has not withdrawn the claim.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine grind to a virtual halt, The Straits Times reports, after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.
A suspected sabotage attack fails to disrupt deliveries by Estonian defence manufacturer Milrem to Ukraine, according to the company. Investigators have not publicly attributed the attempt.

Protests in Kyiv back former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a wartime presidential election, Al Jazeera reports, turning his statement into the first visible street mobilisation on the question since 2022.
Russia and Ukraine each hand over 103 prisoners of war in an exchange, one of the few channels between the two sides still operating.

Ukrainian officials say at least 15 people were killed and dozens injured in an overnight ballistic-missile and drone attack on Kyiv, with a nine-storey residential block destroyed in Solomianskyi district and a children's hospital, a school and warehouses damaged. The toll was revised upward through the day from an initial five. Moscow has not commented on the toll.

Ukraine's air force says Russia launched dozens of missiles and 168 drones overnight and that most cruise missiles and nearly 90% of the drones were downed, without specifying how many ballistic missiles were fired or intercepted. Officials say Kyiv is effectively defenceless against ballistic missiles because of an acute shortage of interceptors.
timeline.source: Ukrainian Air Force via BBC, NBC News

timeline.event: German prosecutors say a Ukrainian man has been arrested in Croatia over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage, the second arrest in the investigation. Prosecutors have not detailed his alleged role.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, calls for a presidential election to be held during the war - the most direct domestic challenge yet to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The Kremlin says the call shows splits in Kyiv.
Poland says it has arrested a man over an alleged plot to assassinate an official in Ukraine's arms industry. Warsaw has not named the suspect or the intended target.
Romania's defence minister says the country destroyed a marine drone near the Neptun Deep gas project in the Black Sea. Bucharest has not attributed the drone to a party.
Black Sea grain exports from both Russia and Ukraine remain at a virtual halt after weeks of strikes on port and terminal infrastructure on both sides.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least 17 people were killed and more than 40 injured in the overnight attack on Kyiv, which struck blocks of flats and warehouses and damaged a children's hospital and a school. CNA's earlier count was 16. The figures are Ukrainian and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Ukraine State Emergency Service)

timeline.event: Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko tells the BBC that critical infrastructure was 'purposefully attacked' for the first time in several months, disrupting hot water supply in parts of the city.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine urgently needs more Patriot interceptors and that the shortage is costing lives.

A senior Russian diplomat says Moscow is ready to consider new ideas on a Ukraine peace settlement but only on its own conditions, repeating that any talks must recognise the 'new realities on the ground'.
Russia holds a rare missile test near the disputed islands north of Japan that Tokyo calls the Northern Territories.

Australia charges a 27-year-old Russian-Australian citizen with foreign interference, alleging he joined Ukraine's armed forces to gather information on their military activities for Russia. The allegations have not been tested in court.

Russia's FSB says nine people have been arrested for planned attacks and espionage on behalf of Ukraine, according to Russian state agencies. Kyiv has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.
A Ukrainian man wanted over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline sabotage is detained in Croatia, the second arrest in the German-led investigation.

Mykhailo Fedorov, removed as defence minister, plans a trip to the United States to raise funding for his projects, The Straits Times reports - a sign his domestic challenge to Zelensky has shifted abroad after the wartime-election protests ended.

The BBC's Steve Rosenberg reports petrol shortages spreading in Russia as the cumulative effect of Ukrainian strikes on refineries and export infrastructure reaches ordinary consumers, though he finds little erosion of public support for the war.
Japan lodges a formal protest over Russia's missile test near the disputed Kuril Islands, held days ahead of an expected Putin visit.

Russian drones strike a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, President Zelensky's home city, with a second drone hitting about half an hour after the first. Regional military head Oleksandr Hanzha says 16 people were killed and 130 injured, among them 23 children. Zelensky calls the two-wave attack 'cynical and despicable' and says the second strike targeted emergency workers at the scene; the BBC says it verified footage of the second drone hitting the already burning mall. Russia's military has not commented on the mall.
A separate Russian drone strike in the southern Mykolaiv region kills at least four people, three of them children, and wounds a woman, Ukrainian state media report.
The leaders of France, Britain and Germany announce they will co-chair a meeting on Ukraine on Monday.

Russian state agencies report that nine people have been arrested on suspicion of planning attacks and conducting espionage on Ukraine's behalf. The claim comes from Russian authorities and has not been independently verified.
Russia designates the independent news outlet Mediazona a 'foreign agent'.

German authorities are investigating possible Russian links to a weapons cache discovered in woodland, according to reports cited by the BBC. The investigation is unconfirmed by German officials on the record.

Rescuers work through the night in the wreckage of the Kryvyi Rih shopping centre; Hanzha says the death toll reached 16 after another body was recovered overnight, with nine people reported still missing and 29 in a serious condition. Local officials say at least two more people were killed in further Russian strikes early on Saturday. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted transport infrastructure and warehouses.

Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia kill at least 10 people according to Russian regional officials and halt work at a warehouse of the online retailer Ozon in the Samara region. Russia's figures are not independently verified.

The death toll from Friday's double-tap drone strike on a shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih rises to 16, with 130 injured and four people still missing, says Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha. Rescue work may run for two more days.
President Vladimir Putin says Ukraine has opened a 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia will hit back at Ukraine's 'most sensitive economic sectors'.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, visiting Ukraine, condemns what he calls Russia's escalating attacks on civilian areas.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says French President Emmanuel Macron agreed to accelerate deliveries of French air-defence equipment, after Kyiv said a shortage of interceptors was costing lives. Paris has not published a delivery schedule.

Norway's government says it will give Ukraine another 85 billion Norwegian crowns (about US$9.2 billion) in financial support in the 2027 fiscal year, matching its 2026 contribution and split between military and humanitarian spending. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Stoere announced it while visiting Kyiv with Nordic and Baltic leaders.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine believes Russia plans to draft an additional 300,000 troops after Russian parliamentary elections in mid-September, working towards 500,000 overall by 2027, and that Moscow is raising missile production to about 1,300 a year. These are Ukrainian assessments and have not been independently verified; the Kremlin has not confirmed them.

Zelensky rejects holding a wartime election, saying a vote during this kind of war would 'destroy' the country by splitting Ukrainians. It is his first response to ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov's call for a poll. Elections in war are prohibited by Ukrainian law and the country has been under martial law since 2022.

Sacked defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov tells the BBC that Zelensky should be asked what he knew about corruption in his government, following a money-laundering investigation announced last week, while saying he never saw the president act corruptly and never received an improper instruction from him. He repeats his call for a wartime vote.

Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store says Norway will give Ukraine US$9 billion (about S$11.4 billion) in 2027, matching this year's record level, with most of it going to the military. Baltic and Nordic leaders gather in Kyiv for a summit with President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Zelensky says Ukraine's army faces a US$27 billion deficit and urges the European Union to advance payments on part of a 90 billion euro loan, warning that without about US$10 billion by the end of the year his soldiers will not have enough weapons. He did not give a detailed breakdown.

Ozon reports a fire at its logistics hub in Russia's central Orenburg region after a drone attack and suspends warehouse operations, a day after an Ozon centre in the neighbouring Samara region was hit and an unspecified number of workers wounded.
A Russian attack on the outskirts of the north-eastern city of Kharkiv kills three people, the regional governor says on Telegram.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev says drone debris hit a private childcare centre overnight, killing two children and injuring nine people including seven children, and that debris fell on apartment buildings. The Russian account is not independently verified.

Ozon says a 'major fire' is burning at one of its logistics centres in the Krasnodar region after a drone attack, the second consecutive day one of its hubs has been hit. The company says staff were evacuated and there are preliminarily no casualties. Ukraine's defence ministry said on 22 Aug it was extending to Ozon a campaign that has already struck the 15 largest Wildberries logistics hubs.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ozon, Ukrainian defence ministry)

timeline.event: A drone attack on an industrial area in Nevinnomysk, a chemical production centre in the Stavropol region, is repelled, Governor Vladimir Vladimirov says on Telegram.
Zelensky says Ukraine was not behind the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts and that Kyiv is cooperating with the German-led investigation, after two arrests in the case.

Kyiv hosts a meeting of the French- and British-led Coalition of the Willing to discuss stepping up support for Ukraine and pressure on Russia ahead of winter, as Ukraine marks 35 years of independence.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is due to urge US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to take a more active role on Ukraine, The Straits Times reports.
President Volodymyr Zelensky marks 35 years of Ukrainian independence, saying Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russian terms.
BBC reports that President Vladimir Putin said on Saturday Ukraine had opened 'Pandora's box' by striking economic targets and that Russia would hit back at Kyiv's most sensitive economic sectors.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says measures are being taken to minimise the impact of Ukrainian strikes on Russia's grain exports, telling reporters that 'all grain intended for export' will be shipped on time and in full. Tit-for-tat attacks on ports and vessels have shuttered grain terminals and forced dozens of cargoes to be delayed or cancelled in peak export season.

Zelensky says Russia is 'not ready' for a ceasefire limited to attacks on Black Sea ships carrying agricultural produce, because Moscow wants any deal extended to cover strikes on Russian refineries and pipelines.

Ukrainian drone strikes set fire to logistics centres belonging to Ozon, Russia's second-largest online retailer, in Krasnodar, Dagestan, Stavropol and Adygea. The BBC verified video of the attacks. Ozon said several people were injured; Russia's defence ministry said three children aged 13, 15 and 16 were killed in Krasnodar. Neither account has been independently verified. Ozon shares fell as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange and those of its main shareholder AFK Sistema by almost 13%.

Andy Burnham, on his first overseas trip as UK prime minister, met Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the British- and French-led coalition of the willing. Britain agreed to hand over blueprints for UK-made components of the Scalp missile, the French version of the Storm Shadow cruise missile, so Ukraine can build the weapon domestically. Burnham urged the US Congress to 'ratchet up' economic pressure on Russia.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the British missile transfer prevented 'even the slightest progress' towards peace and that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate and destroy any Ukrainian missile production sites. Asked about the charge that Britain was adding fuel to the fire, Burnham replied: 'Who started the fire?'
Ukrainian strikes hit Russia's second-biggest online retailer, extending Kyiv's campaign against Russian commercial and logistics infrastructure.
Britain and Ukraine signed an artificial-intelligence defence partnership covering battlefield technology, extending the industrial cooperation announced during Burnham's visit.

President Vladimir Putin granted the Russian state the right to take control of infrastructure it judges inadequately protected against drone attacks, a response to Ukraine's deepening campaign against Russian economic targets.
Britain and France pledged stronger support as Ukraine marked 35 years of independence, with Burnham saying allies were digging into their own stocks of air defences to help protect Ukrainian skies.

Krasnodar governor Veniamin Kondratyev said the Afipsky oil refinery was on fire after a drone attack, and that two people were killed and two injured by falling drone debris at the Afipsky railway station. The account is from Russian regional officials and is not independently verified. The export-focused plant processed about 144,000 barrels a day in 2024, and follows the halt of the Perm refinery after a Ukrainian drone strike on 21 August.

Andrei Fedorov, an adviser to the Kremlin, told BBC Newsnight there might be a 'semi-military' response against UK drone factories by 'unknown sources' over Britain sharing blueprints for Scalp/Storm Shadow missile components. The remark is one adviser's and not a stated Russian government position.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, returning from Kyiv, said he will 'likely' travel to the United States next month with European leaders to lobby President Trump on Ukraine's defence needs, though he said the details were not fully confirmed. It would be his first US trip since taking office in July.

Archbishop Paul Gallagher, the Vatican's foreign minister, met Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in Moscow — the first in-person Vatican-Russia talks in five years. Gallagher said it was 'urgent and necessary' to end the war, and the two agreed to cooperate on humanitarian matters including children affected by the fighting.

A US Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster, tail number 07-7181, flew direct from Riga and landed at Moscow's Vnukovo airport at about 0700 GMT, per Flightradar24 data. It is the first direct flight of a US-registered jet to Russia from Europe since January. The Kremlin said it had no information on the plane; its cargo and passengers could not be verified.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine sees a window for US-led mediation until the end of next summer, and that a one-page set of ideas drafted with US and European officials — a ceasefire as the main point, plus a US-proposed free economic zone in Donbas administered by a third party — will be put to Moscow.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Finnish President Alexander Stubb's approval of Ukrainian long-range strikes inside Russia showed he belonged, alongside Britain's Andy Burnham, to the 'party of war', and accused Western leaders of misleading voters about Russia being strategically defeated.

German investigators found a third drone west of Leipzig/Halle Airport on 14 August, 10 days after the attempted attack, along with about 50g of a substance suspected to be the military explosive hexogen, according to NDR, WDR and the Sueddeutsche Zeitung. Security sources cited in the reports suspect Russian intelligence involvement; Moscow denies it. The prosecutor-general's office did not comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (NDR, WDR, Sueddeutsche Zeitung)

timeline.event: Sweden's military said it was seeking to take over a Russian-owned estate close to a Swedish naval base, citing security concerns.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that whoever was behind a drone incident over Germany would 'pay a price'. No party has been formally identified.
Slovak police said they had thwarted a planned arson attack on a drone factory.

German magazine Der Spiegel reported that a man detained over a Berlin gun stash is suspected of being part of a Russian network. The claim comes from the magazine's reporting and has not been confirmed by prosecutors.
Mykhailo Fedorov, recently ousted as defence minister, said Ukraine needs to change how it is fighting to avoid losing the war.

The United States asked Ukraine not to launch air strikes around Moscow, St Petersburg and some northern Russian territories on 24, 25 and 26 August, because a plane carrying a senior US official would be in the area.

CIA Director John Ratcliffe travelled to Moscow for meetings with Russian officials, CBS News and Axios reported citing unnamed sources — the first known Moscow visit by a US intelligence chief since William Burns met Vladimir Putin in November 2021. The CIA declined to comment; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov neither confirmed nor denied the visit and said Putin had no plans to meet Ratcliffe.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, CNA (CBS News, Axios)

timeline.event: Switzerland will hold a referendum next month on adopting a more restrictive form of neutrality that would bar it from imposing economic sanctions or cooperating with NATO in peacetime.

The BBC reports the CIA director's Moscow trip would be the first known visit by a US spy chief since 2021. The CIA declined to comment and the Kremlin said President Vladimir Putin had no plans to meet him.

The Kremlin said CIA director John Ratcliffe held talks with Russian intelligence counterparts during his Moscow visit, while stating that President Vladimir Putin did not meet him. Neither side described what was discussed.
A Wildberries warehouse in Russia's Tambov region was destroyed by fire after being hit by a drone, the regional governor said. Ukraine did not claim the strike.
The BBC reported that as Ukraine keeps striking Russian oil refineries, Russia has shifted to targeting Ukraine's fuel distribution network, including petrol stations.
Ukraine awarded Elon Musk a high state honour as Kyiv seeks to expand its use of Starlink.
The Kremlin said remarks by ousted Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov showed Kyiv was consumed by infighting. The characterisation is Moscow's; Kyiv has not responded.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned that those behind a drone incident over German territory would 'pay a price'. Berlin has not publicly attributed the incident.

Ukraine's military named prominent commanders to lead the defence of the eastern region that Russia is demanding be ceded in any settlement, signalling it intends to hold the ground rather than trade it.

President Donald Trump described CIA director John Ratcliffe's unannounced Moscow trip as a 'semi-routine' mission and said 'something may come out of' it. Neither Washington nor Moscow has said what was discussed.
A US senator said he hoped a 'sledgehammer' package of Russian sanctions would pass Congress next month. The bill has not been scheduled for a vote.
A Pentagon official is to brief NATO allies as a US force-posture review raises questions among European members about the scale of the American commitment to the continent.
France's security chief said he sees new threats following the drone attack at Leipzig. No attribution for that incident has been made public by German or French authorities.

The Wall Street Journal and CBS News reported that CIA director John Ratcliffe used his Moscow visit to warn Russia against attacking NATO members, following US intelligence assessments that Moscow could seek to test the alliance. Neither the White House nor the Kremlin has confirmed the content of the talks.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (WSJ, CBS News)

timeline.event: US officials said the Pentagon's global posture review is preparing options on American troop levels in Europe for Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth by 6 November. No decision has been announced.

Russia launched a large overnight missile and drone attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities. Ukraine's air force said the barrage included two Oniks anti-ship cruise missiles, 258 drones and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles, and that nearly 90 per cent of the drones were downed along with one Oniks and seven ballistic missiles. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said ports, grain storage, energy and industrial infrastructure were targeted.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ukrainian Air Force, Ukrainian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: President Volodymyr Zelensky said European allies had made 'important decisions' this week to strengthen Ukrainian air defence and that Ukraine had recently received a small batch of Patriot interceptors, renewing his call for further packages. Kyiv has been short of the US-made interceptors capable of downing ballistic missiles.
Russia said it could strike British military targets in response to Ukraine's use of British-supplied missiles against Russian territory.
A senior aide to President Volodymyr Zelensky said talks between Ukraine and Russia may be possible in September.
Russia's foreign intelligence chief confirmed that he held talks with CIA director John Ratcliffe during the American's unannounced visit to Moscow. Neither government has said what was discussed.

US Defense Under Secretary Elbridge Colby, visiting NATO headquarters in Brussels, pressed European allies to set out how they are taking primary responsibility for the continent's conventional defence, as Washington's six-month review of its force posture in Europe continues.
Slovak prosecutors said suspects had planned an arson attack on Skyeton, a Ukrainian drone manufacturer.
Bulgaria will receive seven minehunter ships from Belgium and the Netherlands to help protect the Black Sea.
An EU official said there were no signs Russia is preparing a military attack on NATO countries, pushing back on warnings circulating in allied capitals.

The Netherlands, Poland, Spain and Sweden called for the European Union to reopen discussion next week on using Russia's frozen assets for Ukraine, arguing Moscow shows no sign of wanting to end the war. Belgium, which holds most of the assets, has previously blocked the idea.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Dutch, Polish, Spanish and Swedish governments)

timeline.event: Poland's deputy defence minister said Poland does not want nuclear warheads stationed on its territory.
A car bomb killed a Russian army officer outside Saint Petersburg, Russian media reported. No one has claimed responsibility and investigators have not publicly attributed the attack.

President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin will not attack NATO territory and played down reports that CIA director John Ratcliffe had warned Russian officials against doing so during his unannounced Moscow visit.
