Authorities in Ukraine's Kherson told residents to leave the city, the strongest evacuation message from the regional administration in recent weeks.

Ukrainian courier company Nova Poshta said Russian attacks destroyed its sorting centres near Kyiv and in the northern city of Sumy. It said four guided aerial bombs hit the Sumy terminal and damaged three trucks, that all employees were unharmed, and that it continued to operate.
Sweden's military will help survey and protect Finnish territory with Gripen fighter jets and a corvette, at least until the end of 2026, Finland's defence forces said.
Countries bordering the Baltic Sea plan a joint task force for drone defence so they can react quickly to hybrid attacks, German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said in Flensburg.

The Straits Times reported, citing officials, that CIA director John Ratcliffe's 25 August trip to Moscow was an attempt to persuade the Russian leadership against fresh provocations in Europe. The account is single-sourced reporting and has not been confirmed by either government.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said the United States had passed Kyiv information about a number of meetings held in Moscow over the previous few days, following CIA director John Ratcliffe's trip to the Russian capital on 25 August.
Ukraine's top presidential adviser said technical talks on the war would likely take place in the near future, while cautioning that he did not expect a swift agreement.
Mykhailo Fedorov, dismissed as Ukraine's defence chief six weeks earlier, agreed to become adviser on defence innovation to Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto.

Ukrainian officials said Russian attacks across the country killed 16 people and injured 50 over the previous day, with strikes reported on a gas station in Kharkiv, a supermarket in Pavlohrad and warehouses in the Kyiv region. The tallies come from Ukrainian regional authorities and have not been independently verified; Russia's defence ministry says it targets military and military-linked infrastructure.

Zelensky said Ukraine's security service struck a Tu-95MS missile carrier at Engels airbase and that Ukrainian forces hit an oil refinery in Russia's Yaroslavl region. Both are Ukrainian claims; Moscow has not confirmed the damage.
Ukraine's military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov said Ukraine needs to mobilise at least 30,000 people a month, and separately that ending the war now is unrealistic.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says the United States passed Kyiv information about a number of meetings held in Moscow over recent days, thanking Washington for the information and for "the necessary tone of the conversation with Russia", without saying who took part.

Western officials told the BBC that Russia is sharpening its rhetoric towards NATO but wants to avoid a direct war with the alliance, while remaining likely to continue hybrid activity against member states short of open military action.

Ukraine's Air Force said air defences neutralised 233 of 267 attack drones launched from the evening of 28 August, in a barrage that also included an Oniks anti-ship missile and an Iskander-M ballistic missile fired from occupied Crimea. The figures are Ukrainian military claims and have not been independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said after a Commander-in-Chief's Headquarters meeting that Ukraine's goal is 1,000 long-range strike drones a day against Russia, against an average of 300 or more now.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service said a Russian strike in the Odesa region killed one person and injured three, setting eight lorries carrying food on fire; an overnight attack on the Izmail district damaged transport infrastructure. Both accounts come from Ukrainian authorities.

Ukraine's General Staff reported 242 combat clashes along the front over the previous day, the largest number of them on the Pokrovsk axis. Russia's defence ministry gives its own, differing accounts of front-line activity.
The leaders of Russia, China and Iran are due to attend a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Kyrgyzstan, a bloc that presents itself as a counterweight to Western influence.

A Russian drone struck an enterprise in the town of Myla, in Kyiv region's Bucha district, at about 8.10pm on 28 August, causing a large fire and sustained detonations. Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko reported 27 dead and more than 40 wounded during the afternoon; Ukrinform reported the toll had risen to 37 by evening and the BBC reported hundreds of residents evacuated. Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community, was among the dead. All figures are Ukrainian officials' and are not independently verified.

Ukraine's prosecutor general opened a criminal negligence investigation into the Myla site, saying it would examine the legality of storing explosive objects and materials on the enterprise's grounds and whether the company held the necessary permits. Officials did not describe the nature of the facility.
A mass drone attack caused a local blackout in Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, leaving about 300,000 customers without power, Ukrinform reported citing Ukrainian authorities.

Ukraine's Defence Forces said they struck launch sites used for Russian attack drones in Donetsk region and occupied Crimea, and separately that drones hit an Ozon logistics centre in Russia's Rostov region. Both are Ukrainian claims; Moscow has not confirmed the damage.
Estonia's foreign minister called for increased pressure on Russia following the overnight attack on Ukraine.

The death toll from the Russian drone strike on a weapons store at Myla, in Kyiv region's Bucha district, reaches 37 with 42 injured, four of them children. Regional head Tymur Tkachenko says around 80 sites were damaged and about 130 homes hit; police say four people are still missing. Russia's defence ministry says it targeted an ammunition depot holding components for long-range drones.

Zelensky says the store "definitely shouldn't have been there" and orders an investigation into "terrible negligence" by whoever kept explosives beside houses; Ukraine's defence ministry separately calls on defence-industry leaders to audit how they store weapons and ammunition.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 224 attack drones between 6.30am and 6pm, most of them jet-powered and the majority aimed at Kyiv, and that 199 were shot down or jammed. The figures are Ukrainian and not independently verified.

A two-year-old girl dies in hospital of shrapnel wounds after drone debris falls in a park in Kyiv's Obolon district, and eight people are injured in the capital during the day, Mayor Vitali Klitschko says. A second strike hits a non-residential building in the Podil district.

The IAEA says the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has been without off-site power for more than a week and is running its cooling on emergency diesel generators with only a 10-day fuel supply, after military activity on the northern side of the Dnipro. Director General Rafael Grossi calls reliable external power "indispensable"; the agency is seeking a local ceasefire to repair the lines and reports three drone incidents at the site this week that injured two employees.

Finland's President Alexander Stubb tells Germany's Bild he sees "neither evidence nor facts" behind assessments that Russia could attack a NATO country by 2029, saying it would "make no sense" for Moscow to test the alliance. German officials have made that 2029 assessment.
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk says after talks with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that Ukraine needs greater air support amid Russian escalation.
Kyiv region declares 30 August a day of mourning for the victims of the Myla blast, with flags at half-mast and entertainment venues restricted, regional administration head Tymur Tkachenko says.
Putin and Xi Jinping are due in Bishkek on 31 August for a two-day Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit marking the bloc's 25 years, also attended by the leaders of Iran and India.

Ukraine's General Staff says 221 combat engagements were recorded along the front in the previous 24 hours, with the heaviest fighting in the Kostiantynivka sector (31 Russian attacks) and the Pokrovsk sector (30). Russian figures are not available and the tallies are not independently verified.

Ukraine's State Emergency Service says at least three people were injured in a drone attack on Kyiv, with a fire running from the second to the fifth floor of a 12-storey residential block in Obolonskyi district and damage in three other districts. The service says eight people were injured in the capital across the wider attack, three of them hospitalised. Not independently verified.

The head of the Kherson regional military administration, Oleksandr Prokudin, says Russian attacks killed three people and wounded 17 across the region in 24 hours, damaging six high-rise buildings and 14 private homes. Not independently verified.
Russian forces struck warehouses in the city of Zaporizhzhia in a morning attack, starting a fire, regional officials say.

Ukraine's General Staff issues a public warning against siting ammunition depots near civilian areas, a day after the Myla blast, and the defence ministry asks defence-industry leaders to audit how they store weapons and ammunition.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian General Staff, Ukraine's defence ministry)

timeline.event: President Volodymyr Zelensky says the death toll from the 28 August strike on the ammunition depot at Myla in Kyiv region has risen to 38, with four people still missing; Ukrinform reports 20 injured. Zelensky says most fires have been put out but contamination of the site is significant. It is the deadliest Russian strike in the Kyiv area this year.

Zelensky says Russia launched nearly 2,000 strike drones, more than 1,600 aerial bombs and 31 missiles at Ukraine over the past week, including North Korean ballistic missiles. The figures are Ukrainian and are not independently verified.
Ukraine's air defence forces say they shot down 125 Russian drones overnight. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.

Ukraine's Defence Forces say they struck the Kirishi oil refinery and the Yeysk airfield inside Russia, and separately claim the destruction of five Russian air defence assets at the Yeysk and Millerovo airfields. Ukrainian claims; Russia has not confirmed them.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian Defence Forces, Unmanned Systems Forces)

timeline.event: Ukrainian forces deny Russian claims to have captured Velykyi Prykil and Sadky in the Sumy region. Both sides' battlefield claims remain unverified.

A Russian attack on the Odesa region injures at least three people overnight, and drones and 'Banderole' missiles strike port infrastructure in the Mykolaiv region, Ukrainian regional authorities say.
Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces say they destroyed five Russian air-defence assets at the Yeysk and Millerovo airfields inside Russia. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.
Two people, including a minor, are killed in a Russian guided-bomb strike on the Donetsk region, regional authorities say.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says Berlin is finalising a response, coordinated with European and NATO partners, to the suspected drone attack on a Ukrainian Antonov cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport on 4 August. Germany has not officially attributed the incident.
A NATO official says the alliance sees no imminent threat of an attack, The Straits Times reports.
Ukraine's defence chief pledges to set out a clear war plan as Kyiv seeks the early release of loan funding, The Straits Times reports.

Kyiv regional authorities raise the number of casualties from the 28 August strike on the ammunition depot at Myla to 52, including five children; 38 of them have died. Ukrainian figures, not independently verified.
President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia launched nearly 1,500 drones of all types at Ukraine over four days, about 800 of them jet-powered. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 186 combat clashes along the front over the past day, with more than 40 Russian attacks repelled in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors combined - down from 221 clashes the day before. Ukrainian claim.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says a trilateral meeting between Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelensky and Vladimir Putin would be possible "only to formalize agreements".
Russian attacks injure four people in the Dnipropetrovsk region over the course of a day, with the region struck nearly 50 times, regional authorities say.

Russia attacked overnight with one Kh-59 guided missile and 121 Shahed-type attack, Gerbera and Parodiya decoy drones, the Ukrainian Air Force Command says; air defences shot down or suppressed 96 drones and the missile did not reach its target, with hits recorded at 11 locations. Ukrainian military claim.
Ukraine's General Staff reports 225 combat clashes over the past 24 hours, the most in the Pokrovsk sector, alongside 91 Russian airstrikes dropping 288 guided bombs. Ukrainian military claim.
Two people were killed and three injured as Russian forces carried out 923 strikes on the Zaporizhzhia region over the past day, regional authorities say. Ukrainian regional claim.

A missile attack on the Russian city of Belgorod killed two people and injured 16, acting governor Alexander Shuvayev says, after a Ukrainian strike on a commercial facility set seven warehouses ablaze; Russian retailer Ozon says a logistics hub and a sorting facility were hit. Russian official claim.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Belgorod acting governor, Ozon)

timeline.event: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says NATO's moves in the Arctic pose a "direct threat" to Russia; NATO said separately it sees no imminent threat of attack.

Russian drone attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region stretch into a fifth day, with near round-the-clock air raid sirens disrupting daily life; attacks early on Monday injure four people and damage warehouses, an apartment block and a retail outlet, regional governor Tymur Tkachenko says. Ukrainian official account.

Six people are injured in drone attacks on Kyiv and the village of Pohreby, Mayor Vitali Klitschko says; three are hospitalised in serious condition and warehouse facilities in Pohreby catch fire. Ukrainian official claim.

Energy company DTEK says Russian forces have attacked its Dnipropetrovsk region facilities three times in recent days; power was restored to 40,000 customers over two days but another 30,000 remain without electricity. Company statement.
Ukraine's Defence Forces say they struck a Russian radar, an S-400 command-and-staff vehicle and supply depots. Ukrainian military claim, not independently verified.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the oil tanker MV Sun, suspected of sailing under a false flag, was boarded on 30 August in the Mediterranean by EUNAVFOR MED IRINI forces for flag verification — the sixth suspected Russian shadow-fleet vessel boarded by EU operations in recent months. Shadow-fleet action is on the agenda when EU defence ministers meet in Ireland on Tuesday.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz pledges a "swift response" to Russian hybrid attacks; separately, Polish authorities are investigating possible sabotage after a fire at a Polish drone manufacturer.

Ukraine's General Staff reports 173 combat clashes along the front on 31 August, with 66 Russian airstrikes dropping 218 guided glide bombs, 6,542 kamikaze drones deployed and 2,049 attacks on settlements and positions. The heaviest fighting was again in the Pokrovsk sector, where 32 assaults were repelled and, by preliminary Ukrainian estimates, 53 Russian troops were killed and 18 wounded. Ukrainian military claim, not independently verified.

The Kherson Regional Prosecutor's Office says three civilians were killed and seven injured, including an 11-year-old boy, in Russian artillery and drone attacks across the region during the day. A 65-year-old woman in Kostyrka was killed by a drone strike; a Russian drone also hit a supermarket roof in Kherson, injuring a child. War-crimes investigations have been opened. Ukrainian official account.

The Kyiv Regional Military Administration says nine people were injured in Russian air attacks in the Kyiv region during the day, eight of them in the village of Pohreby, with warehouses damaged in three districts and two houses damaged in Bucha district. Ukrainian official account.

Polish prosecutors open a terrorism investigation into a fire at the WB Electronics drone factory in Skarzysko-Kamienna, saying it was started deliberately with a device containing flammable materials, and also investigating “participation in the activities of a foreign intelligence service directed against the Republic of Poland”. No suspect has been named; Poland has repeatedly accused Russia of sabotage since 2022 and Moscow has denied it.

Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attends a G20 finance ministers' meeting in Asheville, North Carolina in person — his first since the 2022 invasion — after a US invitation, and holds a bilateral meeting with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent that a US official says focused on President Trump's Ukraine peace plan. German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil calls the presence a “quite troubling” signal and says Europe is preparing a further sanctions package; European officials refuse to appear in the family photo, which is taken without Siluanov.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (G20 delegations, German finance ministry, US Treasury)

timeline.event: Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping hold talks in Bishkek as the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit opens. Xi says Russia–China ties have become “more solid”; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says the pair discussed the Ukraine war only “in passing”.

Russian strikes have destroyed some 12 million books as Ukraine returns to school, the BBC reports, after missiles hit publishing warehouses, printing presses nationwide and a well-known second-hand book market in Kyiv. One plant on the edge of Kyiv was hit overnight as it ramped up to deliver 1.3 million books — about 10 per cent of Ukraine's schoolbooks.
Debris from Russian drones falls in two districts of Kyiv overnight, sparking fires, according to Ukrainian authorities.

Nine people are killed and more than a dozen injured in Russian air attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region, the sixth consecutive day of strikes on the capital, Ukrainian authorities say. The State Emergency Service says eight were killed and five wounded in Kyiv itself, three of them children, with fires in several districts; in Boryspil, Kyiv regional governor Tymur Tkachenko says one person was killed and nine injured, including a child, after missiles and drones damaged an apartment building and a business facility. Air raid alerts covered most of Ukraine in the early hours. The figures are Ukrainian officials' account; Moscow has not commented.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Ukrainian State Emergency Service, Kyiv regional administration)

timeline.event: A fresh Russian strike halts border crossings into Romania, a member of the EU and NATO, at Orlivka on the Danube, CNA reports, as Russia widens attacks on Ukraine's borders alongside energy and logistics facilities. Separately, CNA reports a drone attack caused a fire in the port area of Ust-Luga, a major Russian export outlet in the north-west.

Ukraine's sanctions commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk is in Washington to lobby members of the US House to back the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which passed the Senate with bipartisan support but faces opposition in the House over its tariff powers and political risk ahead of the midterms. If enacted it would let the president impose steep tariffs on countries dependent on Russian energy, with discretion to lift them.

Ukraine's air force says air defences neutralised 10 missiles and 187 drones in the overnight attack, and a spokesperson says all cruise missiles launched at Ukraine were shot down. The tallies are Ukrainian military claims and are not independently verified.

The toll from the overnight strikes on Kyiv and the surrounding region rises to at least 12 killed and 20 injured, including two children, Ukrainian officials say. Eight died in Kyiv — six of them workers at a state railway depot hit in the city — and four in Boryspil, where a residential building was struck. President Volodymyr Zelensky said nearly 350 rescue workers were deployed overnight. Russia's defence ministry said its “massive strike using high-precision weapons” targeted Ukrainian military and energy facilities and said one person was killed by Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Belgorod region. All figures are the claims of parties to the war.

Russia attacks port export infrastructure in the Odesa region and damages the Orlivka ferry checkpoint on the Romanian border — the fourth strike on that crossing, Ukraine's border service says — suspending processing of people and vehicles. Zelensky said the strike “deliberately damaged a border crossing point on the border with Romania, as well as export infrastructure”; the emergency service said energy infrastructure was also targeted and one person was hurt in a fire at a residential building. Odesa recorded more than 300 air-raid alerts in August, lasting a combined 238 hours, according to a monitoring service.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, Ukrinform (Zelensky, State Border Guard Service)

timeline.event: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly urges Vladimir Putin at a regional security summit in Kyrgyzstan to end the war, saying “every day spent in war pushes humanity back”. India buys heavily discounted Russian oil and has stayed broadly neutral; BBC correspondents read the remarks as continuity rather than a policy shift.

Ukraine's General Staff says Russian forces lost more than 124,000 troops over the summer, about 25 per cent more than in spring, and another 1,440 personnel in the past 24 hours. These are Ukrainian military claims and are not independently verified; Russia does not publish comparable figures.
Ukraine's parliament fails to pass a parcel tax law tied to IMF and EU funding, leaving a condition of external financing unmet.

Ukraine's military intelligence directorate (DIU) says its operators, in a joint deep-strike operation with Ukrainian Defence Forces, hit the Novatek-Ust-Luga complex in Russia's Leningrad region overnight, reporting damage to key refinery components and a large fire. This is a Ukrainian military claim and has not been independently verified; Russian authorities have not confirmed the damage.

Ukraine's Air Force Command says Russia launched 99 strike drones between 06:30 and 18:00 on 1 September, 72 of them jet-powered, and that air defences shot down or suppressed 82 of them, 57 jet-powered. It says around 10 jet-powered drones were still in Ukrainian airspace at 18:30 with new groups entering. These are Ukrainian military claims and are not independently verified.

Zelensky warns airlines that Russian airspace is becoming dangerous, saying Ukrainian drones have effectively closed it, and threatens to keep it that way through mass drone deployment. Putin later says Russia would respond if Ukraine closes Russian airspace to commercial flights.

Germany says Russia was behind the 4 August drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport, where an explosive-carrying drone was found near Ukrainian cargo planes and failed to detonate. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says equipment analysis and intelligence proved Russian involvement; Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul orders the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn, terminates the Russian House Berlin contract, tightens entry controls for Russian nationals and summons Moscow's ambassador. Russia's embassy calls the allegation 'absurd' and an 'unprecedented escalation', and foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova says Moscow will respond in 'mirror-image' fashion.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (German interior and foreign ministries, Russian embassy)

timeline.event: Explosives are used in a sabotage attack on power lines at a Brandenburg substation in Germany, with rockets carrying conductive material triggering short circuits. Grid operator 50Hertz says general electricity supply was unaffected. No party has been formally blamed.

Putin, speaking to reporters after the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, says Ukraine's 40-day strike campaign caused damage of about 1 per cent of Russia's GDP - 'real damage' but 'not critical' - and claims Ukraine damaged about 100 Russian ships, roughly 40 of them in the first two weeks. He says only about 10 per cent of Russia's refineries are still to be repaired, and separately says Russia is winning on the battlefield and will not negotiate with 'terrorists'. These are Russian presidential claims; Ukraine has not confirmed the figures.

Russian drones strike the Brovary and Bucha districts of the Kyiv region overnight, the regional administration says: a woman born in 1971 is hospitalised with a thigh wound in Brovary, and warehouse facilities are damaged and burning in Bucha. Regional head Tymur Tkachenko says drone attacks on the region have now run six days.

Russia's embassy in Germany calls Berlin's attribution of the Leipzig/Halle airport drone attack to Moscow an 'absurd and baseless provocation' and an unprecedented escalation, saying it benefits Ukraine and arms makers.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Russian embassy in Germany)

timeline.event: Putin responds to Zelensky's airspace warning by calling it 'a declaration of state terrorism', says Russia will continue its attacks and that its military is preparing 'massive' strikes on Ukrainian power stations, and acknowledges Ukrainian strikes damaged Russian infrastructure while insisting 'only 10%' of oil refineries are left to repair.

Aviation risk firm Osprey Flight Solutions tells clients that while most Ukrainian drone and missile strikes are likely to fall within 300km of the border, daily attacks deeper inside Russia are almost certain to continue this year, and that misidentification in the conflict zone is likely.
Putin says Ukraine's 40-day strike campaign, which began in June, damaged about 100 Russian ships, and repeats that Russia is winning on the battlefield and will not negotiate with 'terrorists'.

German police say they are investigating a second sabotage attack on the country's electricity grid, at a substation near Bergheim in the west, a day after explosives were used against power lines at a Brandenburg substation.

Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov says dialogue between Russia and the United States should continue to find common ground in economics, which he argues would make political discussions easier, according to Interfax. Canada's finance minister says Siluanov's presence at the G-20 'created discomfort'.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Interfax, Anton Siluanov, Canadian finance ministry)

timeline.event: Mykhailo Fedorov says Palantir chief executive Alex Karp will be the first major investor in his new defence company, and Ukrainian experts are to advise European governments on plugging their defence gaps.
The Kremlin says Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin may hold a trilateral meeting at the next APEC summit.

Russian drones tear into central Kyiv on the seventh day of near round-the-clock attacks, wounding nine people and damaging residential and university buildings. Zelensky says about 160 students had to shelter during a strike on a downtown university while classes were in progress.

Russian missiles and drones hit power facilities in the Odesa region, knocking out electricity to more than 350,000 homes, while two people are killed and eight wounded in Dnipro, where food warehouses and educational buildings were damaged, the regional governor says.

Ursula von der Leyen says the EU will increase pressure on Russia, including with new sanctions, after the Leipzig/Halle airport drone plot; Kaja Kallas says the attack had the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism and that measures are being prepared against Russia's military-industrial complex. Germany says it will close Russia's consulate general in Bonn and terminate its agreement with the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin, and the EU and several member states summon Russian embassy officials. Russia denies involvement.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte says more drones and missiles have crossed into alliance airspace on the eastern flank and that malign activity, including the Leipzig attack, is increasing.
Zelensky tells airlines, insurers and anyone using Russian airports that Russian skies are not safe, because Ukrainian drone operations over Russia are being scaled up.
Merchant ships in the Black Sea are fitting makeshift anti-drone defences as attacks on shipping intensify.
German officials say a test of an Israeli-made ballistic missile was successful, part of Berlin's build-out of layered air defence.

Ukraine formally notifies the International Civil Aviation Organization that Russian airspace is not safe for civil aviation, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha says, after Zelensky told airlines and insurers that 'the Russian sky is becoming completely dangerous'. Putin calls the warning a 'declaration of state terrorism'. FlightRadar24 still showed aircraft over Russia on Wednesday afternoon.
timeline.source: BBC (Andrii Sybiha, Volodymyr Zelensky, Vladimir Putin)

timeline.event: ICAO reiterates calls for stronger commitments to protect civilian aircraft from risks arising in conflict zones, responding to Ukraine's notification.

Ursula von der Leyen says 'Leipzig marks a new escalation on European Union soil directly attributed to Russia' and that the EU must respond 'faster and better'; Mark Rutte says NATO stands in full solidarity with Germany. Germany's interior minister says the drone's configuration, components, explosives and detonator are all known from other Russian hybrid operations, and two suspects have reportedly been identified, including a Belarusian holding a Russian passport who entered on a tourist visa. Russia rejects the German accusation.
timeline.source: BBC (Ursula von der Leyen, Mark Rutte, German interior ministry)

timeline.event: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blames high energy prices on Ukraine's strikes inside Russia; The Straits Times describes the remarks as consistent with the administration's willingness to pressure Kyiv while courting Moscow.

Norway seizes the Russian-owned vessel Professor Molchanov off Svalbard after a 24-hour standoff with its coast guard, to enforce a US$4.22 billion award won by Ukraine's Naftogaz over Russia's expropriation of its Crimean assets. A Hague tribunal ordered the payment in April 2023 and Moscow has not complied. Russia's foreign ministry, quoted by TASS, calls the seizure 'piracy'.

Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Russia will close Germany's Goethe-Institut cultural centres in Moscow, St Petersburg and Yekaterinburg, retaliating for Berlin's closure of a Russian cultural centre in Berlin and a consulate in Bonn over the Leipzig drone incident. Lavrov says further measures will follow. Putin said on 1 September that Germany planted the evidence.

EU foreign ministers meeting in Ireland summon Russia's envoys and discuss sanctions on some 1,600 Russian individuals and entities, plus a possible visa ban on Russians involved in the war. Foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas says the Leipzig incident has 'all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism'. Germany says it has identified two suspects. Russia denies involvement.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (Kaja Kallas, German government)

timeline.event: Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service says it has documents on at least eight Indonesian citizens recruited into Russia's army under false promises of high-paying jobs, publishing Russian visa and migration papers. Indonesia's foreign ministry says it must verify their identities, citizenship and the nature of their involvement; a deputy speaker of parliament confirmed on 1 September that the information had been shared. Russia has not commented.
timeline.source: CNA (Foreign Intelligence Service of Ukraine, Indonesian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: Britain summons Russia's charge d'affaires to condemn last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport, after the German government said Russia was responsible. Moscow denies involvement.

President Vladimir Putin says there is a chance of a peace settlement and that several countries, including the United States and China, are ready to support one, while arguing that Ukraine's warning to airlines about Russian airspace makes a deal harder; Kyiv says it sees a 'new dynamic'. No terms have been published and both characterisations come from parties to the war.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Vladimir Putin, Ukrainian officials)

timeline.event: Russia's Transport Ministry says it has given foreign airlines clarifications about the safety measures at Russian airports and in Russian airspace, after Volodymyr Zelensky warned carriers that flying over Russia had become unsafe.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Russian Transport Ministry, via Interfax)

timeline.event: German police investigate a suspected arson attack outside a defence-technology firm in Munich, days after two sabotage attempts on the power grid and a month after the Leipzig airport drone attack. No attribution has been made for the Munich fire.
Denmark's national security and intelligence service PET says Russia is recruiting Danish citizens to help plan sabotage against Danish defence companies with ties to Ukraine.

President Donald Trump says the United States will seek back payment from European governments for aid provided to Ukraine. He gives no figure, mechanism or timeframe; European capitals have not responded publicly.
Ukrainian authorities say an overnight Russian attack on Kyiv injured 10 people, started a fire and damaged a high-rise building. The account is Ukrainian and has not been independently verified.

President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russian drones struck a Coca-Cola bottling plant outside Kyiv. Moscow says it targets military and military-industrial sites; the claim is not independently verified.
Zelensky says he expects to host US envoys in Kyiv in the 'coming days'. Neither side has named the officials or set a date.
Zelensky says an investigation is under way after a clash between two Ukrainian security agencies, without naming the bodies involved.

Russia demands the 'immediate release' of the research vessel Professor Molchanov, seized by Norway off Svalbard to enforce a US$4.22 billion arbitration award won by Ukraine's Naftogaz. Moscow calls the seizure piracy; Oslo says it is enforcing a court award.
A Russian court imposes restrictions on the head of a children's hospice charged over posts about the war, the latest in a run of prosecutions over wartime speech.

German police respond to two more suspected attacks on the electricity grid, Bild reports: an attempt to short-circuit a grid installation in Dormagen, where a letter claiming responsibility was received, and a cordoned-off transformer station in Ganderkesee. A police spokesperson told NDR an overnight discovery prompted the response and there was no danger to the public. The incidents are unattributed; Berlin has separately blamed Russia for last month's Leipzig airport drone attempt, which Moscow denies.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Bild, NDR, German police)

timeline.event: Finland's Border Guard says it is investigating whether a surveillance drone found on the shore of its southern coast violated Finnish territory. A preliminary examination identifies it as a Geoscan 701, a survey and mapping model used by both state and civilian operators. The Border Guard says it cannot confirm the drone's origin, operator or purpose; the defence ministry says it posed no danger to the public.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Finnish Border Guard, Finnish defence ministry)

timeline.event: WHO says a warehouse storing medical supplies in the Kyiv region was attacked overnight. The agency has not attributed the strike beyond describing it as part of the ongoing attacks on Ukraine.

Russian state agency TASS reports that envoys of President Donald Trump will visit Russia and Ukraine at the weekend. The Kremlin declined to comment and Washington has not confirmed the trip; the report is a Russian state-media claim.

A BBC survey of August incidents describes a spiralling sabotage campaign against European defence and military sites - fires at Bulgaria's EMCO plant on 10 August, at KNDS Ammo Italy outside Rome on 13 August and at Estonia's Milrem Robotics in Tallinn on 15 August, where two suspects were arrested - following the discovery of explosive-laden drones at Leipzig airport on 4 August. Germany's interior minister says 'Russia is responsible' for the Leipzig attack; the Kremlin calls the accusation 'absurd' and demands proof. Some fires remain under investigation and may yet be ruled accidental.
timeline.source: BBC (German interior ministry, Polish interior minister Marcin Kierwinski, Kremlin, La Repubblica, Kyiv Post)

timeline.event: A Russian drone strikes the Kyiv headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service, one of the most high-profile targets hit in more than four years of war. Kyiv's mayor says at least 12 people are wounded. President Volodymyr Zelensky says the drone was aimed directly at the office of the SBU's head and that he has ordered a response that will 'mirror' the strike; SBU head Oleksandr Poklad briefed him on preparations. It is the 10th consecutive day of Russian air attacks on the capital. Moscow has not publicly commented on the target and the Ukrainian account has not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC, CNA (Volodymyr Zelensky, Kyiv city authorities)

timeline.event: A senior Ukrainian official says there is growing appetite among partners for negotiations on the use of frozen Russian assets. No decision or mechanism has been agreed and the characterisation is Kyiv's.

German police respond to a third suspected sabotage attempt against the electricity grid as a state election approaches. German officials have blamed Russia for some recent incidents; the Kremlin calls the accusations absurd and investigators have not ruled out other causes in every case.
The Kremlin says the position President Vladimir Putin set out two years ago - that Ukraine should cede the whole of four regions Russia claims and abandon its bid to join NATO - is 'unshakeable'.

President Donald Trump says his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are travelling abroad over the weekend to discuss a Ukraine peace settlement, confirming trips to Moscow and Kyiv that Russian state agency TASS had trailed a day earlier and the Kremlin had declined to comment on. No agenda or meeting list has been published.

Zelensky says he will meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on Sunday, after the pair meet President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday. Trump says the envoys are 'bringing with them a proposal to end the war'; no terms have been made public and the two sides remain far apart.

Oleksandr Ganzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration, says four people were killed and five wounded in a Russian strike on the south-eastern city of Kamianske. Russia has not commented.

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner land in Moscow and are met by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev, two people familiar with the visit told The Straits Times. Dmitriev took part in all their previous meetings with Putin. Zelensky says the pair will fly to Ukraine on 6 September.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (sources familiar with the visit)

timeline.event: Zelensky says in a post on X that Russia struck two Ukrainian airports ahead of the US envoys' visit to Kyiv. The claim is Ukraine's and has not been independently confirmed; Russia has not commented.

A local ceasefire brokered by the International Atomic Energy Agency takes effect around the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant so Ukrainian technicians can demine and repair the damaged Ferosplavna power line. The plant has had no external power since 20 August and is running its safety systems on emergency diesel generators, which the IAEA says are running low. Rosatom chief Alexei Likhachev says the truce is expected to last about a week and that repairing the line would not necessarily restore supply; Ukraine has not publicly commented on his account. Both sides have repeatedly accused each other of endangering nuclear safety.

President Vladimir Putin meets US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow for more than three hours. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov calls the talks 'highly useful' and says the pair 'outlined a number of ideas regarding possible avenues for a settlement' without saying what they were, adding that economic projects were also discussed. Ushakov says Putin told the envoys Russia was making 'real progress' on the battlefield and stressed addressing 'all the root causes of the conflict' - positions Moscow has stated repeatedly. There was no comment from Witkoff or Kushner, who flew out soon afterwards; no breakthrough was announced.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov)

timeline.event: Witkoff thanks Putin for agreeing with Ukraine to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days. President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow from Saturday through Monday and expects Russia to do the same regarding Kyiv, and that plans for the envoys' Kyiv talks on 6 September have been approved. The Straits Times reports Russia continued missile strikes on Kyiv despite the pause around the talks.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Volodymyr Zelensky, Steve Witkoff)

timeline.event: Regional authorities in eastern Germany say 12 improvised explosive devices were found on Friday near high-voltage lines close to the Baerwalde and Graustein electricity substations in Saxony. Bomb disposal units disabled them and police are investigating a 'possible link' to this week's other substation attacks, which authorities describe as likely 'climate extremism' after a 48-year-old man sent letters claiming responsibility. These incidents are attributed to a domestic suspect, not to Russia.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, AFP (German regional police)

timeline.event: US ambassador to NATO Matthew Whitaker says alliance members should not tolerate deliberate hybrid warfare and that Washington will stand by countries dealing with such incidents. He describes last month's attempted drone attack on Germany's Leipzig/Halle airport, which Berlin blames on Russia and Moscow denies, as more concerning than Russian drones that stray off course while targeting Ukraine.

Berlin's state government sets up a central crisis unit to review a trove of data published by the Rhysida ransomware group after a cyberattack on two city departments. The 5.79 terabytes of data were released on Friday when an auction starting at 30 bitcoin ended; Berlin had said it would not submit to extortion. The city calls the incident 'an extremely serious crime' and an attack on the state itself, less than a month before city elections on 20 September.

The Straits Times reports from Kyiv that near-constant drone attacks have become the city's daily reality, with commuters stranded, children moved underground during the school day and festivals cancelled.

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to travel to Kyiv, their first trip there, after meeting President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. The Kremlin said the envoys outlined a number of ideas on possible avenues for a settlement but gave no details and reported no breakthrough.
Odesa, Ukraine's third-biggest city and majority Russian-speaking, is due to decide this week whether to ban Russian-language content in music and literature in public.

US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrive in Kyiv and meet President Volodymyr Zelensky, their first visit to the Ukrainian capital. The White House says the pair 'discussed substantive plans for next steps' with President Vladimir Putin in Moscow the previous day.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Western accusations that Moscow was involved in the drone incident at Germany's Leipzig airport are 'by and large, the start of a real war', state news agency TASS reports. Germany blames Russia for the attempt; Moscow denies involvement.

Moscow says it has not ruled out a trilateral meeting between the presidents of Russia, the United States and China, TASS reports. No date or venue was given and neither Washington nor Beijing has confirmed such a meeting.

Germany is drawing up a broad package of measures against drone attacks, cyber intrusions and other sabotage after last month's failed drone attack on Leipzig airport, Bild am Sonntag reports, as explosive devices are found at two more electricity substations.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Bild am Sonntag, German authorities)

timeline.event: Zelensky says after several hours of closed-door talks with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Kyiv that he expects the war to continue into the winter, and that officials from Ukraine, Europe and the United States will meet again soon. He calls for a trilateral meeting with Russia and the US and says he wants a just peace that leaves no opening for renewed Russian aggression. Witkoff says he is 'encouraged' by talks he calls substantive; no breakthrough was announced.

Jordan Bardella, president of France's far-right National Rally, says France should demand guarantees from Ukraine in return for military and financial support, arguing Kyiv should buy defence equipment from the European countries backing it. He cites France's economic difficulties and praises US demands for a return on aid.

BBC Verify's analysis of Ukrainian government figures finds Kyiv recorded 76 air raid alerts in the seven days from 27 August, above the previous peak of about 66 in the week beginning 27 February 2022, with residents sheltering as many as 13 times a day. Ukraine's air force says Russia launched 2,800 jet-powered attack drones in August, almost twice July's total.
timeline.source: BBC Verify (Ukrainian government figures, Ukrainian Air Force)

timeline.event: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov says Moscow does not rule out resuming trilateral talks with Ukraine and the United States but that it is 'too early to speak of the venue and exact dates', and that a Putin-Trump phone call about the envoys' trip is possible.

UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk tells the Human Rights Council he is 'horrified by reports that fully autonomous drones launched by the Russian Federation killed three Ukrainians last month', notes reports that Ukraine has field-tested such weapons, and calls for an urgent ban on weapons that kill without human involvement.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, AFP (UN Human Rights Council)

timeline.event: Russia's foreign ministry condemns the US deployment of an Mk-41-based missile system to Norway, saying it 'resets to zero' conditions for strategic stability talks and that such deployment sites would become targets in the event of a military conflict.

Prosecutors in Saxony say nine more homemade explosive devices were found over the weekend near high-voltage lines south of the Graustein substation, taking the total recovered to 21, as Germany stays on alert after a run of grid sabotage. A separate Berlin transformer fire on the same day is attributed to a technical fault.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Saxony police and prosecutors)

timeline.event: Russia and North Korea open the first road bridge across their border, adding a permanent overland link after two years of deepening military and economic cooperation.

Russia closes Germany's consulate in St Petersburg, deepening a diplomatic rupture that widened last week when Berlin accused Moscow of orchestrating a drone attack on Leipzig airport. Moscow has denied involvement in previous incidents.
Latvia bans the import of books from Russia and Belarus, saying the material amounts to war propaganda.

Downing Street says British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and President Donald Trump discussed working towards a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in a call. The readout is the British government's; the White House has not issued its own account.

A US envoy says there is 'movement' towards three-way talks involving Washington, Moscow and Kyiv, a day after the Kremlin said it did not rule out resuming trilateral talks but called it too early to name a venue or dates.

An air raid alert is declared over Kyiv early on 8 September because of a threatened drone attack, ending a three-day pause in strikes on the capital. Damage and casualty figures had not been published at the time of reporting.

Ukraine's prosecutor-general submits his resignation, citing political conflict - the latest sign of disunity in the senior ranks of the Ukrainian leadership after the removal of the defence minister and his call for a wartime election.

Russian drones and missiles hit Kyiv overnight, killing two people and wounding at least 10, ending a three-day pause that Moscow declared while US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff visited the city. Ukraine's air force says it shot down or suppressed two ballistic missiles, 31 cruise missiles and 142 drones; the tallies are Kyiv's and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, AP (Ukrainian air force)

timeline.event: President Volodymyr Zelensky tells Axios that Russia is 'ready to negotiate', a day after a US envoy said there was 'movement' towards three-way talks. Moscow has not publicly confirmed the characterisation.
Russia says it will strip contract soldiers of their one-off enlistment payment if they break the law at home, tightening terms for a recruitment drive that has leaned on large signing bonuses.
Hungary expels 10 Russian diplomats, saying they acted in ways incompatible with their diplomatic status.
Ukraine braces for months of fighting over key strongholds in the eastern Donetsk region, the first major test for incoming top general Mykhailo Drapatyi and his new commanders.

Zelensky says US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner presented several 'decent ideas' for ending the war, and that a Russia-Ukraine meeting could take place as early as September if all sides agree. Moscow has not confirmed a date.

A daytime Russian drone attack on Kyiv hits a building housing a television channel; Ukrainian officials say five people were killed in the capital. President Volodymyr Zelensky calls it 'a new page in Russian degradation'. Casualty figures are those reported by Ukrainian authorities.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov says President Donald Trump told President Vladimir Putin in a call that he wants the conflict brought to an end as soon as possible and US-Russia ties restored. The account is the Kremlin's; the call was described as 'extremely frank'.
German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius says Germany will send Patriot air-defence missiles to Ukraine from national stocks, warning Russia is likely to intensify its air campaign over the winter.
Ukraine's defence chief Yevhenii Khmara says Kyiv is contracting around 1,000 Patriot missiles from allies, but that most would only be shipped in the coming years.

Romania says it detained a 40-year-old Russian who filmed and photographed military sites and was preparing an act of sabotage on Moscow's orders. The accusation is Bucharest's; Russia has not publicly responded.
Norway says it assisted 69 Russian citizens in returning home from an Arctic island after the small cruise ship they arrived on was seized.
A monitoring report released ahead of a treaty conference says cluster munitions killed or wounded at least 1,063 people in 2025, most of them in Ukraine - the third-highest annual toll on record.
Zelensky arrives in Oslo for the funeral of Norway's King Harald V and defence talks with Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store.

Ukraine's allies expect the war to run into 2027 following Putin's meeting with US envoys, assessing that he intends to step up attacks through the winter. The assessment is that of allied officials cited by The Straits Times, not a public Russian statement.

Russian drones hit a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova in the southern Odesa region, killing two people, and struck Kyiv overnight, Ukrainian authorities say. The casualty figures are Kyiv's and have not been independently verified.

Four people including a child are killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on the Black Sea port of Novorossiysk, the governor of Russia's Krasnodar region Veniamin Kondratyev says. The claim is Moscow's; Kyiv did not immediately comment.
Russia's foreign ministry says it hopes US-mediated talks with Ukraine will resume soon, a day after the Kremlin said President Donald Trump pressed President Vladimir Putin to end the war quickly.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says disaster was narrowly averted in a drone attack on an airport that Berlin says was prepared by Russia. The attribution is the German government's; Moscow has not publicly responded.
Finland concludes that GNSS jamming and wind, rather than deliberate action, caused Ukrainian drones to enter Finnish airspace in the spring.
President Vladimir Putin hosts Vietnamese leader To Lam at the Kremlin, praising deepening ties as Hanoi looks to diversify its defence partners.
Russia's state arms exporter Rosoboronexport markets drone-like missiles for the Su-57 stealth fighter at an Egyptian air show, the aircraft's African debut.

A British man is charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service and preparing an act of sabotage after alleged contact with a group linked to Russian military intelligence, UK prosecutors say. The man has not entered a plea.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UK Crown Prosecution Service)

timeline.event: President Donald Trump says he had a 'great' conversation with President Vladimir Putin earlier in the week and that the Russian leader wants a deal to end the war. The characterisation is Trump's; the Kremlin has separately said it hopes US-mediated talks resume soon.

A Russian drone strike on a shopping centre in Sumy kills two people and injures 20, four of them seriously, regional governor Oleh Hryhorov says. The figures are Ukraine's and are not independently verified.
Norway's prime minister says President Volodymyr Zelensky's aircraft was almost hit by a drone as it took off from Moldova on 8 September en route to King Harald V's funeral in Oslo.

A Ukrainian drone strikes Russia's Arctic region almost 3,000km from the border - reportedly the longest-range attack on Russian territory since the 2022 invasion, according to The Straits Times. Moscow has not published a damage assessment.

The BBC reports five deaths in Ukraine and four in Russia from the latest exchange of drone strikes, including two people killed at a Ukraine-Moldova border crossing. All tolls come from the respective national or regional authorities.

BBC Verify analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data finds Russia launched its new jet-powered Geran drones against Ukraine on every day of August, the first month daily use appears in the data. Ukraine's military says jet-drone attacks rose from 350 in June to 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August. The figures are Ukrainian military data.

Sea drones injure eight people and damage beach infrastructure at Russia's Black Sea resort of Sochi late on 9 September, authorities in the Krasnodar region say. Ukraine has not claimed the attack and the casualty figures are Russian officials' own.

Britain, Norway and the United States disclose that they tracked and confronted Russian vessels near Svalbard this spring which two Western officials say were rehearsing the deployment of technology designed to disable undersea cables without leaving traces. The operation is attributed to Moscow's GUGI undersea warfare directorate. The account comes from two officials speaking anonymously; Moscow has not commented publicly.
President Vladimir Putin hosts Vietnam's leader To Lam at the Kremlin and praises deepening ties between the two countries.

Russian forces strike a petrol station complex in south-western Kyiv for the first time, injuring four people, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko and the oil company Ukrnafta. Ukraine's emergencies service says the attack destroyed at least one vehicle and set a neighbouring building alight. The account is Ukraine's and has not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Kyiv mayor, Ukrnafta, Ukrainian emergencies service)

timeline.event: Kyiv has been under an almost continuous barrage of jet-powered drones aimed at warehouses and industrial sites for nearly two weeks, The Straits Times reports.

Joshua Cammidge, 31, appears at Westminster Magistrates' Court in London charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service and preparing an act of sabotage. Prosecutors say he supplied details of four drone factories near Swindon and offered to sabotage them after contact with the GRU Volunteer Corps, which they say Russian military intelligence controls.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UK Crown Prosecution Service)

timeline.event: Russia sends the bones of a medieval warrior prince to the Ukrainian front in an effort to raise the morale of its troops.
With Russians preparing to vote, The Straits Times reports that anxiety over the war is deepening among the electorate.

A BBC analysis of Ukrainian Air Force data finds Russia is launching its new jet-powered Geran drones every day and that Ukraine's interception rate against them is falling, leaving the fast drones increasingly able to reach their targets. The underlying counts come from the Ukrainian Air Force, a party to the war.

Amnesty International says Russia has recruited foreign nationals under false pretences to fight in Ukraine and describes the practice as trafficking. Moscow rejects that characterisation of its foreign recruitment.
Poland says it expects Russia to target its border crossings with Ukraine, the main routes for Western military and humanitarian supplies. The assessment is Warsaw's; Moscow has not commented.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says Canada has agreed a C$350 million air defence package for Ukraine during a visit by President Volodymyr Zelensky. CNA and The Straits Times differ slightly in converting the figure to US dollars; both attribute the Canadian dollar amount to Carney.

Ukrainian officials say at least five people were killed when a Russian strike hit a shopping centre. Russia's defence ministry maintains it strikes military infrastructure; the toll comes from Ukrainian authorities and is not independently verified.

Russia's Belgorod regional governor says Ukrainian drone attacks killed two people and injured seven in the region overnight. Kyiv does not usually confirm individual strikes inside Russia and the toll comes from Russian regional authorities.
President Vladimir Putin arrives in India for the BRICS leaders' summit, which India hosts on 12-13 September with the Iran war straining the bloc's unity.

Ukrainian authorities say eight people were injured and a nine-storey apartment block caught fire in Russian air strikes on Kyiv, ending a brief pause that coincided with a visit by US negotiators. Tula's governor Dmitry Milyayev says Ukrainian drones killed two people and injured three in his region overnight, and officials in Saratov and Volgograd report damage to civilian and industrial sites. All figures come from officials on their own side of the war and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ukrainian authorities, Russian regional governors)

timeline.event: Donetsk police spokesman Pavlo Dyachenko tells the BBC that forced evacuations of families with children have begun in the worst-hit parts of Slovyansk, where glide-bomb strikes have gone from roughly weekly to almost daily. Slovyansk and Kramatorsk are the largest cities still fully under Ukrainian control in Donbas and form part of Ukraine's 'fortress belt' with Kostyantynivka, which Russia claims to hold in full. The BBC reports Russia controls almost all of Luhansk region and close to 80 per cent of Donetsk.

The Straits Times reports on the rapid expansion of Ukrainian uncrewed ground vehicles used for resupply, casualty evacuation and direct attack, which commanders describe as a shift in how the war is fought along contested stretches of front line.
The International Energy Agency again cuts its forecast for Russian oil production, citing continuing Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian energy infrastructure.

A Latvian man suspected of an attempted arson attack on a drone factory in Slovakia tells investigators he was recruited via Telegram and instructed by several people, one of whom spoke Russian, a Slovak news website reports. Slovak authorities have not published their own findings.
Vladimir Putin holds talks with Narendra Modi in New Delhi on trade and defence as the BRICS summit opens, with Xi Jinping also attending. No movement on ending the war is announced.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko says the toll from the morning's Russian strikes on two gas stations rises to two dead and 12 injured, including a 12-year-old boy; two of the injured died in hospital. The figures are the city's own.

Ukraine's General Staff says its forces struck the Saratov oil refinery, a roughly 7-million-tonne-a-year plant it says supplies the Russian military; President Zelensky says long-range strikes also hit an oil facility in Volgograd and targets in Dagestan, Udmurtia, Tula, Nizhny Novgorod, Perm and Samara and in the Black Sea. Damage is not independently verified.

Vladimir Putin says events in Europe, including the far-right AfD's win in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt state election, are caused by 'Western globalists'. The claim is Putin's characterisation and was made without supporting evidence.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia attacked overnight with six Kalibr cruise missiles, two air-launched missiles and 101 drones, mainly at the Odesa region, and that 110 targets were shot down or suppressed with hits recorded at 20 locations. Odesa's military administration reports six injured and a damaged high-rise; regional officials report one killed in Kryvyi Rih, two in Zaporizhzhia and one in Kharkiv. All figures are Ukrainian claims.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian Air Force, regional military administrations)

timeline.event: UNDP chief Alexander De Croo tells the BBC Ukraine faces its 'toughest winter' since 2022 and risks a humanitarian catastrophe if Russian strikes cut power and water, accusing Russia of systematically targeting energy infrastructure; both sides deny targeting civilians.

Russia's defence ministry says its forces struck the Zaporizhstal steelworks, an Interpipe complex in Dnipro, plants in Kryvyi Rih and two cargo vessels in the port of Chornomorsk. ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih says two subcontractor employees were killed and four injured and production facilities damaged. Both accounts are the parties' own.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Russian defence ministry via Interfax; ArcelorMittal Kryvyi Rih), Ukrinform

timeline.event: Odesa regional head Oleh Kipper says the number injured in the overnight missile-and-drone strike has risen to 23, with seven adults and a five-month-old infant in hospital. Ukrainian claim.

Ukraine's General Staff says it struck the Tolyattikauchuk synthetic-rubber plant in Samara region, whose output feeds solid rocket propellant, plus drone command posts at Polohy and Zaliznyi Port and drone depots in occupied Donetsk and Luhansk regions. Russia's defence ministry says it downed 230 Ukrainian drones overnight; Togliatti's mayor reports one person injured. All claims from the parties.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Ukrainian General Staff), Al Jazeera (Russian defence ministry, Interfax)

timeline.event: Zelensky tells Deutsche Welle he would 'of course' meet Putin at the G20 summit in Miami in December if both are invited, saying only results matter, after US envoys visited Moscow and Trump and Putin spoke by phone this week. A Russian diplomat says Moscow will send officials to a G20 energy meeting in Houston next week.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP; Deutsche Welle), The Straits Times

timeline.event: Ukrainian officials say Russian strikes on Sept 12 killed nine civilians, including three people in private cars in Kramatorsk and two at a grocery store in Zviahel, Zhytomyr region; Zelensky says Russia launched nearly 500 drones since early morning. Odesa governor Oleh Kiper raises the region's injured to 37, including an infant, with two missing. Ukrainian claims, not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ukrainian regional officials, Volodymyr Zelensky), Ukrinform, BBC

timeline.event: Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov is quoted by Ukrainian media as saying Kyiv is preparing for three-sided talks with Russia and the US to resume in October. No date or venue has been confirmed.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Kyrylo Budanov via Ukrainian media)

timeline.event: Ukraine's SBU says its drones struck FPV-drone production and UAV storage sites near Taganrog in Russia's Rostov region, causing fires. Ukrainian claim; Russia has not commented.

Prime Minister Koretskyi convenes an emergency meeting over what the government calls a significant intensification of Russian attacks on petrol stations, including in Kyiv and along international highways, and announces protective structures and drone-approach alerts for stations.

Ukraine's Navy says its Sargan 3000 unmanned surface vessel destroyed a Russian unmanned surface vessel in the Black Sea, calling it the first-ever battle between naval drones. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 453 strike drones and four S8000 Banderol missile drones from 18:00 on Saturday; by 08:00 Sunday 405 drones and all four missile drones were shot down or suppressed, with hits at 13 locations and debris at seven. Ukrainian claim.

Odesa regional head Oleh Kiper says an overnight missile and drone attack damaged an apartment block, private houses, warehouses and cars, with no casualties, a day after a strike on the region injured 35.
The General Staff reports 249 combat clashes over the past day with Pokrovsk the most active sector, and says Russia used 11,357 kamikaze drones and dropped 348 guided bombs. Ukrainian claim.
Ukraine's 47th Mechanised Brigade says it killed about ten Russian assault troops who tried to enter Sumy region from Kursk region through a pipeline. Ukrainian claim; not independently verified.

Ukrainian media, citing the Telegram channel Astra and local residents, report overnight drone attacks on the Slavyansk refinery in Kuban and a fire at a Nizhnekamsk enterprise in Tatarstan, reportedly the Tatneft refinery; Nizhnekamsk's mayor confirmed a fire at 'one of the city's enterprises'. No official confirmation that refineries were hit.
Odesa's military administration raises the toll from the overnight missile and drone attack to two dead at an apartment block and 20 injured, including two children. Ukrainian claim.

Ukraine's General Staff confirms overnight strikes on the Slavyansk refinery in Krasnodar Krai and the Taneco refinery in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, reporting fires at both, plus a drone storage and launch site in Millerovo, Rostov region. Russia has not confirmed the damage.

The head of Russia's Rosatom accuses Ukraine of attacking diesel fuel trucks near the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant, killing two Russian servicemen; the plant relies on diesel generators for reactor cooling during outages. Russian claim; Ukraine has not responded and the IAEA has not confirmed it.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov tells AFP a Putin–Zelensky meeting at the G20 summit in Miami in December is 'impossible' and that Putin will meet Zelensky only in Moscow, after Zelensky said he would attend if the US invited Putin.

President Zelensky says Russia launched about 2,100 attack drones, 78 missiles and nearly 1,700 guided aerial bombs at Ukraine this week, with Sunday's strikes hitting energy, rail, businesses and homes. Ukrainian claim, not independently verified.

Ukraine's railway operator says a Russian drone hit the locomotive of a Kyiv–Warsaw passenger train a few kilometres from the Polish border in Volyn, with no injuries; Lithuania closes Vilnius airport for about an hour and NATO scrambles a jet over a possible drone. Poland's deputy defence minister says its air force flies almost nightly over its eastern regions.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Ukrzaliznytsia, Lithuanian National Crisis Management Centre), Ukrinform (Polish deputy defence minister)

timeline.event: Poland and Ukraine call the Yahodyn strike an escalation. Ukrzaliznytsia says a diplomatic train carrying former UK PM Boris Johnson and European security advisers left the station shortly before a jet-powered drone hit the Kyiv–Warsaw train's locomotive, and that former CIA director David Petraeus was on another train there; the evacuation order came about 15 minutes before impact and no casualties were reported. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha calls it 'Putin's terror knocking directly on the doors of the EU and NATO'.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AFP, AP), Ukrinform (Ukrzaliznytsia), The Straits Times (Ukrainian foreign ministry, Polish border guard)

timeline.event: US President Trump, in Ireland, tells Zelensky to 'stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia', saying the shortages are 'hurting the world'; US diesel topped US$6 a gallon on Sept 10 (GasBuddy). Kyiv says refineries are legitimate military targets.

Odesa's regional emergency service puts the toll from Russian strikes on Odesa and the surrounding region at 24 injured, including two children, with apartment blocks, warehouses and a car-service centre damaged and more than 120 rescuers deployed (Ukrainian figures).

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 323 attack drones between 06:30 and 18:00 on Sunday, 14 of them jet-powered, and that 310 were shot down or suppressed with hits recorded at ten sites; about ten Banderol/Dan-T loitering munitions were also used (Ukrainian claim, preliminary).

Poland's Border Guard tells an emergency meeting of the Government Security Centre, attended by PM Donald Tusk, that more than 600 people were evacuated from two crossings with Ukraine overnight and vehicle processing suspended over the threat of Russian drone attacks; Ukraine had warned for several days that crossings could be hit.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Polish Border Guard, Polish Government Security Centre)

timeline.event: Ukraine's military intelligence chief Oleh Ivashchenko tells The Times that Russia has recruited more than 28,000 foreign mercenaries and that about 8,000 North Korean troops are in Russia's Kursk region, a number he says could rise to about 50,000 (Ukrainian intelligence claim, not independently verified).
timeline.source: Ukrinform (The Times; Defence Intelligence of Ukraine)

timeline.event: Ukraine's Air Force says Russia attacked with 108 drones from the evening of Sept 13 and that air defences shot down or suppressed 85 of them.

Regional officials say a Russian drone struck an energy repair crew's vehicle in Sumy region, killing one worker and injuring another, and that Russian forces launched 876 attacks on 54 settlements in Zaporizhzhia region over the past day, killing one person.
Ukraine's General Staff reports 208 combat engagements along the front on Sept 13.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine)

timeline.event: Chernihiv regional prosecutors say Russian Banderol-type cruise missiles struck warehouses of an agricultural company in central Pryluky around 10:00, killing three people and injuring 12.

Ukraine's General Staff claims its forces hit a 92N6 radar of an S-400 air-defence system in Sochi, plus drone storage and launch sites in Kursk region and occupied Donetsk; Russia has not confirmed the damage.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine)

timeline.event: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius calls Sunday's drone strike on a train near the Polish border a 'calculated escalation' by Putin; Poland's defence minister says a drone retrieved from the Baltic near Jarosławiec appears to be a Russian military UAV.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy), Ukrinform (Polish defence ministry)

timeline.event: Trump says Ukraine and Russia have agreed not to hit each other's energy targets; Zelensky says Kyiv will support such a de-escalation step only if the US secures Russia's genuine readiness to end the war. Moscow has not publicly confirmed the arrangement.

Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha says Russian attacks killed one person and injured seven over the day, including a strike that set fire to part of Pavlohrad; Kharkiv regional officials say a missile strike on Izium injured four, including three teenagers.
timeline.source: Ukrinform (Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regional military administrations)

timeline.event: A NATO Baltic Air Defence fighter shoots down a drone near Kaunas in southern Lithuania shortly after midnight; Lithuania's crisis centre says it likely entered from Belarus and its origin is undetermined.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Lithuanian crisis management centre)

timeline.event: Zelensky fires Prosecutor-General Ruslan Kravchenko, who is accused of taking bribes; Kravchenko, now outside Ukraine, denies the allegations.

Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko says a drone hit a petrol station, injuring one person, and warehouse facilities were struck elsewhere in the city, a day after Trump announced a pause on energy strikes; Poland briefly scrambled aircraft as a precaution and says its airspace was not violated.

Brigadier-General Andrii Biletskyi says Ukraine's Third Army Corps has launched an offensive, 'Vivaldi', north of the Sloviansk–Kramatorsk belt in Donetsk, clearing 75 sq km of Russian infiltration groups and recapturing 10 sq km including Serednie; the claims are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Third Army Corps)

timeline.event: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov calls Trump's energy-strike moratorium a 'very good idea' but says safe shipping for tankers and lifting sanctions are also needed; Zelensky says Kyiv will pause attacks on Russian territory if the US secures a Russian commitment to spare Ukrainian infrastructure.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Denmark summons Russia's ambassador, saying a Russian frigate fired two flares at a Danish military helicopter monitoring it in the Baltic on Monday; Russia's ambassador, quoted by RIA, accuses Danish helicopters of dangerous manoeuvres near Russian warships.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (RIA via wire copy)

timeline.event: Poland's Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz says Poland is reinforcing the infrastructure at its border crossings with Ukraine after Russian drones struck a passenger train and a truck at a petrol station near the frontier at the weekend, forcing border guards to suspend crossings and take shelter.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Polish defence ministry)

timeline.event: UN Humanitarian Coordinator in Ukraine Matthias Schmale says Russian strikes have hit 10 UN warehouses in 2026, including one of the WHO's main medical-supply stores earlier this month, and that the UN is weighing moving aid stocks into underground bunkers and delaying purchases until the last minute.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; UN OCHA)

timeline.event: Zelensky says in his nightly address that a new Ukrainian-developed drone interceptor scored a hit overnight, destroying a Shahed-type drone, but still needs refinement. Ukraine's military says it downed 187 airborne targets overnight and Zelensky puts the interception rate at 93 per cent; the figures are Ukrainian claims and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Zelensky, Ukrainian military)

timeline.event: Zelensky tells CBS that Russian drones entered Moldovan airspace twice while his presidential jet was in transit at Chisinau, once outbound and once on the return leg. Moldovan authorities say two drones crossed for about 10 minutes each on Sept 14, and two more entered on Sept 9, when Moldova closed its airspace and delayed his departure for Norway.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Zelensky via CBS, Moldovan authorities)

timeline.event: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko says one person was killed and 12 injured in Russian attacks on the capital over the course of Sept 15, with six still in hospital.

Lithuania says Nato fighters flown by Italian pilots on the alliance's air-policing mission destroyed a drone that entered its airspace near Kaunas shortly after midnight, in what is thought to be the first such shoot-down over Lithuania; the crisis management centre says it likely came from Belarus and its origin is undetermined.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, Al Jazeera (Lithuanian presidency and crisis management centre)

timeline.event: A Russian drone strikes a passenger minibus near Nikopol in Dnipropetrovsk region, killing five people and wounding at least seven, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha says on Telegram; there is no immediate comment from Russia.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Dnipropetrovsk regional administration)

timeline.event: Zelensky says Ukraine will take 'difficult' measures to cut its budget deficit, as war spending continues to outrun revenue.
US prosecutors charge five people over alleged Russian-backed murder plots.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; US Department of Justice)

timeline.event: European governments are driving demand for larger, cheaper missile stockpiles as the war reshapes procurement priorities across the continent.

Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched 80 strike and decoy drones from 18:00 on Sept 15 and that 63 had been shot down or suppressed by 08:00, with impacts recorded at seven locations — a Ukrainian claim not independently verified.
Ukrzaliznytsia says the Kyiv–Mykolaiv passenger train No. 122 came under Russian attack; passengers and crew were evacuated after an advance warning and moved on by bus.

Ukraine's General Staff claims strikes on a Su-24 at Saky airfield in Crimea, a drone storage and launch site near occupied Donetsk, UAV command posts in Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia regions and fuel and ammunition depots in Luhansk and Berdiansk; damage is 'being assessed' and the claims are not independently confirmed.

Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda says the drone destroyed by an Italian NATO jet near Kaunas was a Russian Gerbera most likely aimed at Ukraine and diverted by Ukrainian electronic warfare; Polish prosecutors say a drone found on a Baltic beach on Monday was a warhead-carrying Gerbera 2. Russia has not commented.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; Lithuanian presidency, Polish prosecutors), Ukrinform
