US Central Command says it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on 8 September, calling it a response to the Revolutionary Guards targeting a US Navy warship twice with ballistic missiles; Washington says no Americans were harmed. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Iran will 'lose tankers' each time it tries to hit US ships.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (US Central Command)

timeline.event: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it fired ballistic missiles at a base used by US forces near Al Azraq in Jordan and attacked 10 ships, including two US vessels and eight oil tankers. Tehran says the missiles caused heavy damage; Jordan says its air defences intercepted 18 of 20 missiles, with two falling in unpopulated areas and no casualties.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, BBC (IRGC statement; Jordanian government)

timeline.event: CNA reports the heaviest single day of attacks on merchant shipping since the war began, with US and Iranian forces both striking tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz. All strike claims are those of the parties involved.
A merchant oil tanker is hit in Iraqi waters as commercial vessels are caught in the exchange of US and Iranian attacks, The Straits Times reports.
Brent crude rises above US$100 a barrel for the first time since July, which the BBC attributes to the US and Houthi strikes and the widening conflict.
Saudi Arabia lifts the alert in a southern city a day after Houthi strikes that Saudi authorities say injured 73 people and disrupted energy facilities.
A Sunni Kurdish cleric is killed in north-west Iran; the Revolutionary Guards blame 'separatists'. The attribution is the Guards' own and no independent account has been published.
Protesters in South Korea urge Seoul to stay out of the Iran war, days after the government sent a team to assess conditions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, visiting Syria, says 'the main task is to bring down the terror regime in Iran' and that Israel is 'very close' to that. The assessment is his own; Iran's government remains in place.
The Straits Times reports Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi faces a credibility test as Iran-backed Shi'ite militias resist his call to hand their weapons to the state.
Protesters in South Korea urge their government to stay out of the Iran war, CNA reports.

The IAEA's 35-nation Board of Governors passes a resolution reporting Iran to the UN Security Council for breaching its Non-Proliferation Treaty obligations - the first such referral in 20 years. Tehran condemns the resolution and blames US and Israeli strikes on its nuclear facilities for disrupting inspections.
Iran strikes further ships and announces an expanded no-go zone outside the Strait of Hormuz, saying exact coordinates will be published later. The claims are Tehran's.
Brent crude passes US$100 a barrel, the first time since July, on the Middle East flare-up; CNA reports the move is stoking inflation fears.

The Straits Times reports Iran is likely to try to reverse-engineer the unmanned US underwater vehicle its Revolutionary Guards say they seized in the strait. Washington has not publicly confirmed the loss.
Advisers to President Donald Trump warn the conflict with Iran may last through the end of his term, the Wall Street Journal reports - a contrast with the president's own public remarks.

Iran says it attacked more than a dozen vessels attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz in a single day, and the Revolutionary Guards expand the declared no-go zone into the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea, warning vessels to seek permission. Brent crude is quoted at US$101.28 a barrel in early Asian trade. The attack claims are Tehran's and are not independently verified.

President Donald Trump says he does not expect the Iran war to end until after November's US midterm elections and that oil prices will not come down until then: "I think the war's going to end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer." The assessment is the president's own.
President Donald Trump says activity has been seen at Iran's Pickaxe Mountain site, threatens to attack it and urges Tehran "not to get cute". Iran has not publicly responded to the specific claim.

The Straits Times reports Yemen's Houthis are closing in on a stranglehold over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern chokepoint of the Red Sea shipping route, after clashes near Khamis Mushait in Saudi Arabia. Riyadh says there is no danger following the alert.

Four Yemeni government military sources say Iran-aligned Houthi forces have seized the port city of Mocha, a shift that could let them threaten the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The group has also attacked the Hanish islands and pushed government forces south towards Dhubab. The account comes from one party to the conflict.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Yemeni government military sources)

timeline.event: Saudi Arabia says there is no danger after an alert at Khamis Mushait, amid intensifying clashes with the Houthis.

Brent crude closes above US$100 a barrel for the first time since late July, rising more than 3 per cent to US$101.21, dragging equity markets down and pushing European gas above 80 euros per megawatt hour, its highest since early 2023.
India prepares to host the BRICS leaders' summit in New Delhi on 12-13 September with the bloc split by the war: Iran, a member since 2024, and the UAE sit on opposing sides of the conflict.

US President Donald Trump says the war with Iran will not end until after the November US midterm elections, and threatens to strike the underground site known as Pickaxe Mountain. Iran has not responded publicly to the specific threat.

A US official says an Iranian attack on a base in Jordan damaged American military aircraft. The Pentagon has not released a damage assessment and Iran has not confirmed the strike, so the account rests on a single unnamed US official.

Houthi forces advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast after taking Mokha, in a push Saudi and Western officials say threatens Saudi oil exports routed through the Red Sea. Accounts of the advance come from Yemeni government military sources and regional officials and are not independently verified.

Four sources tell The Straits Times that Iranian-supplied weapons and military advice were central to the Houthi capture of Mokha. The sourcing is anonymous and Iran has not commented, so this is a claim rather than an established fact.
The US Treasury sanctions networks it accuses of financing and supplying Iran-aligned armed groups across the Middle East. Tehran rejects the designations as economic pressure without legal basis.

Axios reports that President Donald Trump declined a request from Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for US strikes on Houthi forces in Yemen. The report rests on unnamed sources and neither Washington nor Riyadh has confirmed it.

South Korea says its foreign minister discussed the Strait of Hormuz with his Iranian counterpart, one of the few open channels between Tehran and a US ally since the war began. Much of North-east Asia's crude oil transits the strait.

Four Yemeni government sources say Houthi forces have reached the strategic island of Perim (Mayyun) in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, days after taking the port of Mokha. The Houthis have not publicly commented and the account is not independently verified.
Iran's and Saudi Arabia's foreign ministers discuss what both sides describe as regional 'insecurity' as fighting in Yemen flares. Neither released details of what was agreed.
The International Energy Agency warns the 2026 oil supply gap will widen because normal Gulf flows have not resumed. Brent remains above US$100 a barrel.

Six people familiar with the matter say the UAE is revising plans for a 5-gigawatt AI data centre project after Iranian attacks prompted a rethink of where critical infrastructure should be built. The UAE has not confirmed the changes.

Yemeni government officials say Houthi forces completed their takeover of the Bab al-Mandab area and Mayyun (Perim) island, then seized Greater and Lesser Hanish and the remainder of Yemen's Red Sea coastline. 'Everything that was under our control on the western coast has fallen,' a government military official told AFP. The Houthis have made no detailed public statement on the seizures and the accounts have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA, BBC (Yemeni government officials, AFP)

timeline.event: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree says navigation through the Bab al-Mandab strait is 'safe' for all shipping except Saudi Arabia's. The Houthis have been targeting Saudi tankers since July.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Houthi military spokesman, AFP)

timeline.event: AFP reports the week-long Houthi offensive has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides, and displaced about 46,000 people. The tolls come from parties to the fighting and are not independently verified.

Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry says drones launched from Iraq struck the East-West oil pipeline in the Riyadh and Medina regions on the morning of 10 September, causing injuries and damage, and that the line was halted as a precaution. Riyadh says it has chosen not to respond 'at this stage' at the request of the Iraqi prime minister, while reserving the right to protect its sovereignty and facilities. The pipeline runs from Abqaiq near the Gulf to Yanbu on the Red Sea and has carried more Saudi crude since Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Saudi foreign and energy ministries, SPA, AFP)

timeline.event: Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, congratulates the Houthis on their 'resounding victory'.

Oil trades above US$100 a barrel and average US diesel prices top US$6 a gallon for the first time, according to figures cited by The Straits Times. The IEA separately warns the 2026 supply gap will widen because normal Gulf flows have not resumed.
Iran says it will discuss the Strait of Hormuz with Gulf states in Oman on Monday, one of the few open channels with its neighbours since the war began.
President Donald Trump links the 25th anniversary of the 11 September attacks to the current conflict with Iran in public remarks, saying 'that's why we fight'.

The office of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi confirms the drones that struck Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline were launched from Iraqi territory, dismisses the commander responsible for Maysan province on the Iranian border and opens an investigation. Saudi Arabia keeps the line shut as a precaution and says it will not retaliate at this stage; the BBC cites analysts putting the pipeline's recent throughput at 4–5 per cent of global oil supply.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Iraqi prime minister's office, Saudi foreign ministry)

timeline.event: Xi Jinping arrives in New Delhi for the BRICS summit, which Iran's leadership is also attending; the Middle East war and energy security are expected to dominate the two-day meeting.

Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces say they destroyed Houthi vehicles and weapons and killed fighters near Mocha's port and on the Mocha–Dhubab road, a day after the Houthis completed their hold on the Red Sea coast; the UN migration agency puts the displaced at about 46,000. Claims from parties to the fighting, not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Saba), Al Jazeera (IOM)

timeline.event: In Dublin, Trump says Iran was 'probably' responsible for the drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline and that the Houthis have told his administration they do not want the US directly involved and are 'letting most ships go through'. He offered no evidence; Baghdad's finding is that the drones were launched from its Maysan province.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters copy; Donald Trump), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: BRICS leaders unanimously adopt a New Delhi declaration that, per Al Jazeera, stresses keeping trade, supply chains and energy flowing; CNA cites sources saying it condemns unilateral aggression without naming any country. Xi Jinping says the Middle East war 'does not serve the common interests of the international community'.

A senior Iranian official says Monday's Oman-initiated meeting with Gulf states will discuss Hormuz but is not expected to yield a signed agreement, and that Iran still wants to charge ships fees, which Oman rejects. Bahrain's foreign ministry says it will not attend any collective meeting with Iran before diplomatic ties are restored.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Iranian official), Al Jazeera (AFP; Bahraini foreign ministry)

timeline.event: The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed US officials, reports that Chinese entities gave Iran satellite images of the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan before and after the July 17 strike that killed three US soldiers; Chinese officials asked for proof and did not acknowledge involvement.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (The Wall Street Journal)

timeline.event: Iraq temporarily closes the Shalamcheh, al-Shib and Mandali crossings into Iran after drone launch sites are found, an Iraqi security source says, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi approves an Iranian request for a joint investigation into the launch platforms. No group has claimed the pipeline attack.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Iraqi security source, Iraqi armed forces spokesman)

timeline.event: Saudi Civil Defence says a Houthi projectile wounded two people and damaged a mosque, buildings and vehicles in Jazan's al-Tuwal governorate; the Houthis say they targeted a Saudi base in Sharurah and accuse Saudi Arabia of 129 strikes on them in 48 hours. Claims from both sides are not independently verified.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Saudi Civil Defence, Houthi statements)

timeline.event: UKMTO says it received a report of a projectile hitting a vessel transiting the Strait of Hormuz, with damage and crew status unknown; Al Jazeera reports an Iranian commercial vessel was attacked near Qeshm Island, killing one and wounding three, and quotes an Iranian official blaming the 'US terrorist enemy'. Not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UKMTO), Al Jazeera (Iranian official)

timeline.event: Al Jazeera reports the Houthis have seized Mayun (Perim) Island in the Bab al-Mandeb strait along with US-made military hardware left there; Djibouti's finance minister says about 1,400 Yemenis arrived in Obock within 24 hours. Houthi claims not independently verified.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AFP; Djibouti finance ministry, Houthi statements)

timeline.event: Iraq says security forces located and seized a drone-launching platform in Maysan province near the Iranian border, which Saudi authorities had traced as the launch site of the East–West pipeline attack.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian says Tehran is 'not at war with Saudi Arabia' and that the Houthis have 'their own issues', calling on regional countries to work together on peace and security.

Al Jazeera reports Yemeni government forces and Saudi Arabia carrying out air attacks to stop the Houthi advance around Mocha and the Bab al-Mandeb, with the humanitarian situation deteriorating; claims from both sides are not independently verified.

The BRICS summit in New Delhi closes with a declaration that avoids condemning the US-Israel war on Iran; analysts say Iran leaves without strong backing, though its delegation met the UAE's crown prince.

CNA reports the continued shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East–West pipeline threatens the loss of about 4 per cent of global oil supply as the Houthis tighten their grip on Red Sea shipping. CNA's estimate, not independently confirmed; Saudi Arabia has given no restart date.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree says Saudi Arabia carried out 58 air strikes on Houthi positions in 24 hours, after the group claimed a rare drone and missile attack on a military base in the kingdom; Almasirah reports strikes on Saada and a market in Al-Jawf. The Houthis have claimed more than 100 Saudi strikes since Sept 8; Riyadh has confirmed none.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Houthi military spokesman, Almasirah TV)

timeline.event: The IOM says displacement in Yemen has reached 85,818 people, up 10,000 in a day, with more than 82,000 displaced since the Houthi offensive began in early September; Taiz is worst hit with nearly 56,000 displaced, and more than 2,000 people have reached Djibouti.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; International Organization for Migration)

timeline.event: Trump says the US could stay in Iran and 'keep the oil', comparing it with the US push for a fifth of Venezuela's reserves, while repeating that he expects the war to end this year, possibly after the November midterms, and that Iran is 'calling constantly' for talks — a claim Tehran has previously dismissed.

Oman postpones the Sept 14 Salalah meeting at which Iran was to present an Omani-brokered plan for the Strait of Hormuz, citing 'the interests of consensus'; Fars says the delay was requested by some regional states and agreed jointly by Tehran and Muscat. It came hours after an attack on an Iranian cargo vessel in the strait that Iranian media said killed one person. No new date has been set.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP), The Straits Times, Al Jazeera (AP; Omani foreign ministry, Fars)

timeline.event: Oil prices jump as markets reopen with Saudi Arabia's 1,200km East–West pipeline still shut after the Sept 11 drone strikes; traders warn Riyadh will run out of export stocks within days without a restart, a loss of up to 4 per cent of global supply.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (wire copy; Saudi traders)

timeline.event: Al Jazeera reports from Sanaa that Houthi fighters are advancing toward government-held Marib, the oil and gas province, and the city of Taiz, as fighting intensifies (Al Jazeera reporting; no independent confirmation of front-line positions).

Trump dismisses a Wall Street Journal report, citing unnamed US officials, that Iran obtained satellite images of a Jordan base from Chinese entities before July's attack that killed three US troops, saying 'we spy on them too'.
The Houthis say they fired dozens of missiles and drones at Saudi military targets; Saudi Civil Defence issues alerts in Khamis Mushait and Abha, and Iran denies involvement in Yemen's war.

The US blocks Iranian nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami from attending the IAEA General Conference by opposing a snapback-sanctions exemption; Iran says Austria revoked his visa and protests the 'politicisation' of the agency.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Iranian state TV)

timeline.event: The US Defense Department inspector general tells Congress the Iran campaign cost an estimated US$33.4 billion from 28 Feb to 30 Jun, including US$22.3 billion in munitions, and caused strategic inventory shortfalls.

US Central Command disputes the IRGC's claim that the tanker El Gaia struck a mine in the Strait of Hormuz, saying it was hit by an Iranian missile last month and a drone this weekend off Oman; Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei says there will be no talks with the US until Iran's demands are met.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (CENTCOM and IRGC claims attributed)

timeline.event: Yemeni officials say the Houthis launched a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia and are digging into positions on the Red Sea coast as Riyadh deliberates its response; the Gulf–Iran talks remain postponed.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (wire copy; Yemeni officials)

timeline.event: Saudi Arabia warns it will react “firmly” to the Houthis after ballistic-missile and drone attacks wound 13 civilians in the kingdom’s south.

China's foreign ministry says Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi will hold talks with Wang Yi in Beijing on Wednesday, as China seeks to mediate and a week before Xi Jinping is expected to meet Trump in Washington.

The Congressional Budget Office reports the six-month US war against Iran has cost US$38 billion through Aug 1 and projects it to rise about US$3 billion a month, adding roughly 0.5 per cent to inflation in the first quarter of 2027, with munitions stockpiles possibly taking five years to replenish. The CBO says the Defence Department did not cooperate with its auditors.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; CBO), CNA (AFP), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Oman's Maritime Security Centre says two sailors are missing and 23 were rescued after the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia was attacked about 1.3 nautical miles north of the Musandam peninsula and caught fire in its engine room. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say the vessel struck naval mines; US Central Command says it was hit by an Iranian missile last month and by a drone at the weekend. The competing accounts are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC (Oman Maritime Security Centre; IRGC and CENTCOM claims attributed)

timeline.event: The UN refugee agency says more than 100,000 people have been internally displaced by the renewed fighting in Yemen, with thousands more crossing by sea to Djibouti, after Houthi forces routed Saudi-backed government troops along the Red Sea coast and tightened their hold on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; UNHCR, IOM)

timeline.event: BBC Verify satellite imagery shows the most significant damage from last week's strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline is at a pumping station, with experts saying repairs could take more than a month; Saudi Arabia blames Iran-backed militias in Iraq. The US energy secretary says separately the pipeline should be back online within days.
timeline.source: BBC Verify, The Straits Times (wire copy)

timeline.event: A US official, speaking anonymously, says US Central Command has a task force in place to enhance intelligence sharing and planning support for Saudi forces facing Houthi attacks.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; unnamed US official)

timeline.event: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi backs Saudi calls for secure navigation in the Red Sea at a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Cairo, according to the Egyptian presidency; Suez Canal revenues have fallen by about US$7 billion over two years.

Republican Representative Thomas Massie reads articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on the floor of the US House, seeking to force a long-shot vote over the conduct of the Iran war.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Reuters copy), The Straits Times

timeline.event: Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki says air defences destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca on Tuesday before it entered prohibited airspace, calling the security of the holy sites a 'red line'. A Houthi military source, quoted by the group's SABA agency, denies threatening Mecca or other holy sites.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Saudi-led coalition and Houthi claims attributed)

timeline.event: Oman's Maritime Security Centre says two sailors are missing and 23 were rescued from the Panama-flagged tanker El Gaia, which was being towed to an Omani port after a fire in its engine room; the IMO says at least 22 seafarers have been killed in 79 confirmed incidents in the Strait and the wider Middle East since the war began in late February.
timeline.source: BBC (Oman Maritime Security Centre, International Maritime Organization)

timeline.event: The Congressional Budget Office reports the Iran war cost the US Defence Department about US$38 billion as of 1 Aug, with monthly costs of US$2-3 billion or more; munitions replacement accounts for US$21.7 billion and the CBO estimates the US has used between half and two-thirds of its missile-defence interceptor inventory since June 2025. The Pentagon disputes the shortfall finding.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy), CNA (Congressional Budget Office)

timeline.event: BBC Verify publishes satellite imagery showing major damage to a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline; Kpler estimates repairs could take four to six weeks and that the closure could remove up to 3.6 million barrels a day from supply. Brent traded as high as US$108 a barrel.

Trading sources say Saudi Arabia has cancelled some September-loading crude cargoes to European customers and suspended loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu, sending Poland's Orlen to seek North Sea alternatives; Riyadh separately offers Asian refiners additional crude routed via Oman.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy), CNA (trading sources)

timeline.event: The Pentagon's inspector general confirms to Congress that the Iran war has left the US with munitions shortfalls.
timeline.source: BBC (US Department of Defense inspector general)

timeline.event: US officials tout American energy power at a G-20 energy meeting while avoiding discussion of the Iran war.

The US House passes a war powers resolution to end the Iran war for a third time; AP puts the vote at 220-204 with seven Republicans in favour. None of the resolutions has reached Trump, who is expected to veto.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AP), The Guardian, The Hill

timeline.event: Five sources tell Reuters that US embassy staff met Houthi representatives in Muscat over the weekend, with the Houthis reportedly saying they will not attack US vessels and will spare all commercial shipping except Saudi ships; Vice-President Vance said on Monday the US is in direct contact with the group. Not independently confirmed.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree says Saudi warplanes carried out as many as 450 strikes on Yemen this week and claims a Saudi F-15 was shot down, offering no evidence; Saudi officials did not respond. The US bans its government employees from travelling within 20 miles of the Yemen border.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; Houthi military media, US State Department)

timeline.event: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi, hosting Iran's Abbas Araghchi in Beijing, urges Iran and the US to return to their June interim deal and take 'effective measures' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The Guardian reports the weekend Muscat meeting between US officials and Houthi leaders as confirmed, and says it led Washington to decide against militarily backing Saudi Arabia against the Houthi advance; the Houthis told the US only Saudi-linked shipping is a target.

CBS publishes leaked, undated photos from service members showing a destroyed E-3 surveillance aircraft at Prince Sultan Air Base and heavy damage at Camps Buehring and Arifjan in Kuwait from Iranian strikes; the BBC has not independently verified them.

CENTCOM spokesman Capt. Tim Hawkins tells Al Jazeera the strait is open, that US forces have helped move more than 900 million barrels of crude since May and redirected over 100 blockade-running ships, and denies targeting civilians; Trump says the war is 'hopefully toward the end' and claims direct contact with Tehran, which Iran has not confirmed.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (US Central Command, Trump remarks)

timeline.event: Two officials tell AP that Saudi Arabia, short of interceptors, has asked France, Pakistan, Egypt and the UK for air-defence support as the coalition strikes Houthi positions around Mocha; the Houthis claim to have downed a Saudi F-15 over Marib and hit Khamis Mushait air base, claims not independently confirmed. The US bars government staff from within 30km of the Yemen border.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (AP; Houthi and Yemeni government statements), The Straits Times (Reuters)

timeline.event: Axios reports Trump will meet leaders or foreign ministers of the six Gulf Cooperation Council states on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly on Sept 22 to discuss the war's next steps; the White House did not comment.

A UN fact-finding mission says it has found grounds to believe the US committed war crimes in Iran and that Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity; US officials say operations are conducted in line with the law of armed conflict.

The US State Department approves a US$24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth jets to Saudi Arabia and notifies Congress, saying it will not alter the regional military balance. Israel, the only current Middle East operator of the aircraft, has objected to the sale; congressional approval is still required and no delivery timeframe was given.
timeline.source: CNA (AFP; US State Department), The Straits Times

timeline.event: Five people are killed as Yemen's Houthis, the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia trade strikes; Saudi Arabia says one person died as it intercepted a Houthi drone. The BBC verifies video showing the wreckage of a Saudi fighter jet shot down over Yemen.
Sources tell CNA that satellite imagery shows three pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline were hit in the recent attack — one more than previously thought.
timeline.source: CNA (Reuters; sources familiar with the assessment)

timeline.event: Russia and China vote down a resolution extending the mandate of the UN Security Council's independent panel of experts monitoring Iran sanctions; 11 members vote in favour and Pakistan and Somalia abstain. Moscow and Beijing argue all UN measures lapsed under the 2015 nuclear deal.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; UN Security Council)

timeline.event: Italy prepares to deploy its navy to protect Italian-linked shipping amid tensions in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, and US Democrats move to block Trump's Saudi nuclear cooperation deal.
A US official says Washington will allow an Iranian delegation, including President Masoud Pezeshkian, to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, as the war passes the half-year mark.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says it struck a Togo-flagged tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming the vessel attempted 'illegal passage'. The claim has not been independently verified and no casualty details were given.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (IRGC claim, not independently verified)

timeline.event: Trump tells Axios he is weighing a major decision on Iran, saying he is considering whether to 'annihilate' Iranian adversaries and that 'anything could happen'.

South Korean President Lee Jae-myung rules out any South Korean military involvement in the Middle East conflict, explicitly excluding a deployment to the Strait of Hormuz, and says US-North Korea talks remain possible.
Iran expels a Swedish diplomat in what it describes as a retaliatory move, and Al Jazeera reports Iran's nuclear chief was blocked from attending an IAEA conference in Vienna over US objections.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards say via IRNA that the Togo-flagged tanker Trend was targeted and detained after a fire broke out on board late on Thursday, calling it an attempted 'illegal passage'. UKMTO separately reports a vessel hit by an unknown projectile early on Friday. The IRGC account is not independently verified.

Aid agencies say about 115,000 people are on the move after a rapid Houthi advance, and the UN migration agency puts internal displacement at 112,000 with thousands crossing to Djibouti, as a civil war largely paused since the 2022 truce reignites.
Italy's minister calls for more warships to protect navigation in the Red Sea as attacks on shipping widen.

Sources tell CNA that three pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline were hit in the recent attack that shut the line, a fuller picture of damage that satellite imagery had already suggested.
Saudi Aramco tells European refiners it will not supply them with crude in October, sources say, after a drone attack shut the East-West pipeline last week.
The Washington Post reports at least 22 US military fatalities in the Iran war, exceeding the Pentagon's published count by at least four.
The US warns allies that deliveries of key missile and air-defence capabilities could be delayed by as much as five years because of munitions shortages.
Houthi authorities accuse Saudi Arabia of launching 26 strikes in 24 hours. The claim has not been independently verified and Riyadh has not confirmed it.
President Trump extends US sanctions on Iran, Al Jazeera reports.
The Straits Times reports Yemenis fleeing on foot from the advancing Houthi front, as displacement from the offensive continues.
JP Morgan tells the BBC it cannot reliably forecast oil prices because of the war, saying 'we simply don't know' how the conflict will move the market.
The UN Security Council condemns 'in the strongest terms' continued Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia.
South Korea and the United States discuss Seoul's role in the Middle East alongside an investment pact, days after President Lee Jae-myung ruled out any South Korean military deployment.
Saudi Arabia issues air-raid alerts for Riyadh, the first for the capital since the Houthis escalated their attacks, the BBC reports. Saudi authorities have not said what was intercepted.

A large plume of black smoke is seen near Riyadh's main airport after booms are heard in the city, hours after Saudi civil defence sent overnight alerts warning of potential aerial attack over Riyadh and Al-Kharj and then issued an all-clear. The Saudi government media office does not immediately comment. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree had said on Friday that the group foiled unspecified 'criminal attempts' in Sanaa, blaming Saudi Arabia and vowing a response.
A Saudi-led naval coalition prepares to secure Red Sea waterways, Al Jazeera reports, as attacks on shipping widen.
Turkiye revokes the operating licence of Iran's Bank Mellat in Istanbul.
Iran stages a show of force in Tehran during a mobilisation campaign, Al Jazeera reports.

Admiral Brad Cooper, head of US Central Command, says oil and liquefied natural gas shipments through the Strait of Hormuz over the past two weeks reached their highest level in six months, that the strait's main transit lanes are clear of mines, and that US naval protection and mine clearance are 'paying off'.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan tells broadcaster NTV that Saudi Arabia may have unmet military needs because of the Houthi attacks and that Turkiye would consider how to help under the trilateral Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, adding that it is unacceptable for Riyadh to be dragged into the US-Iran war and that proposals to end the fighting have been passed to all sides.

The Houthis say they fired ballistic missiles and drones at Riyadh and at energy sites on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast. The Saudi-led coalition says air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired at the capital at dawn and thwarted attempts on Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu; Riyadh has not confirmed any further strikes or casualties. A column of black smoke was seen rising from fuel tanks near King Khalid International Airport and flights were briefly disrupted. The US State Department urged Americans in the region to expect possible flight cancellations.
timeline.source: BBC, Al Jazeera, CNA, The Straits Times (Saudi-led coalition, Houthi claims)

timeline.event: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, tells Al Jazeera that Tehran has conveyed conditions to Washington through Qatari mediators for ending the war - an end to the fighting on all fronts, release of Iran's frozen funds and an end to the naval blockade - and is awaiting President Trump's response. Washington has not publicly responded.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera (Iran's Supreme National Security Council)

timeline.event: The US State Department warns that the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis 'has the potential to escalate rapidly' and tells Americans to seriously reconsider travel to and through the region, after the first missile attack aimed at Riyadh since Yemen's war resumed. President Trump returns early from Camp David on Sept 19; the White House gives no explanation. The Houthis say they carried out two operations with ballistic and cruise missiles and drones against sites in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu; the Saudi-led coalition says the missile was intercepted and the other attempts thwarted. The UN says the Houthis' recent offensive in Yemen has displaced more than 110,000 people.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; US State Department, Saudi-led coalition, Houthi claims)

timeline.event: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf says the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed and there will be no return to negotiations until Tehran's conditions are met and US commitments fulfilled. Al Jazeera lists the conditions security chief Mohsen Rezaei sent through Qatar: an end to the war on all fronts including Lebanon, release of frozen funds, an end to the US naval blockade, and an end to US attacks and interference. Washington has not publicly responded.

Iran's military central command says on state media that it has information a new attack by the US and its allies is being prepared, and warns any such strike would bring sustained retaliation against US bases and interests, with Washington's regional allies treated as parties to the conflict. It gives no details; the statement is an Iranian claim.

Fox News reports President Trump saying the Houthis 'have agreed not to fight the United States', that he is in 'deciding mode' on Iran and that 'big things will be happening in the not-so-distant future'. The remarks are relayed second-hand by a Fox reporter; the Houthis, who continue to attack Saudi Arabia, have not confirmed any understanding.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP, citing Fox News)

timeline.event: Qatar's prime minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, speaking in New York, calls the fallout of the war an 'earthquake', urges a regional security framework based on respect for sovereignty and says Doha is working to revive Iran-US talks.

The Statistical Center of Iran reports that the economy contracted 10.1 per cent year-on-year between late March and late June, the first full quarter of the war. The figure is the Iranian government's own.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Statistical Center of Iran)

timeline.event: Al Jazeera reports that Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has left Tehran for the UN General Assembly with a stopover in Qatar, and that Trump told Fox News his options on Iran include further military action, economic pressure or a deal and that he would be open to meeting President Pezeshkian in New York. Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf says the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until Washington meets what Iran calls its commitments under an earlier agreement; Qatar's foreign ministry says it is carrying proposals between the two sides.

A spokesman for Iran's Revolutionary Guards says any new US attack would be met with 'new weapons with new capabilities' and that Iran's targets 'will not necessarily be the same as before'. This is a statement by a party to the conflict; no new military action by either side was reported.

Houthi fighters push to seize strategic heights in Yemen that would cut the Red Sea coast off from areas held by Saudi-backed forces, following a media report that Trump called off US strikes on the group at the last minute. The Houthis said on Sept 19 they had fired on Riyadh; Saudi Arabia has not commented and the claims are not independently verified.

theatres.name: Israel-Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Palestinian medical sources told Al Jazeera that Israeli fire killed three people in Gaza on Sept 21, including a child, despite the October ceasefire (not independently verified; no Israeli account reported). In the West Bank, Israeli forces detained at least 53 people in a raid on Biddu following the Sept 20 shooting of an Israeli man. Children in Gaza have returned to in-person classes for the first time in nearly three years.

timeline.event: A Hamas delegation led by Khalil al-Hayya holds talks with Egypt's intelligence chief in Cairo on a plan for Gaza.
US envoy Jared Kushner meets Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Cairo - a rare direct meeting between a senior US official and the group's leadership - while Israel carries out fresh strikes on Gaza.
The Pope calls for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
Kushner meets Netanyahu in Jerusalem to push Trump's Gaza plan, a day after the Cairo meeting. Israel rejected the plan on 9 August and has not said whether its position has changed.
UNIFIL says Israeli flags placed along a road in southern Lebanon violate UN Security Council Resolution 1701. Israel has not responded publicly.

Kushner's round of talks with Israel and Hamas ends without a breakthrough on Trump's Gaza plan. US officials say Netanyahu and Kushner discussed Hamas handing over weapons under the supervision of an American general, with disarmament possibly beginning within 30 days; Hamas has not publicly accepted disarmament.

An Israeli settler walks onto the land of Loui Ridi, a Palestinian American whose West Bank home in Qusra has been besieged by settlers, in a tense face-to-face confrontation. The Israeli authorities have not commented on the incident.

An Israeli airstrike kills at least six Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials say, a day after Jared Kushner's regional trip ended without advancing Trump's plan to end the war. Israel has not commented on the strike.
A US envoy says Washington is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria to avoid clashes as all three operate in Syrian territory.

The United States sanctions ICC president Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, extending a campaign that began with the court's warrants against Israeli officials over alleged war crimes in Gaza. The ICC says the measures undermine the rule of law.

Syrian state television reports eight Israeli airstrikes on the disused Abu al-Duhur military airfield in Idlib province, saying there were no casualties. Damascus calls the attack an unjustified act of aggression.
US envoy Tom Barrack says Washington is deeply concerned by Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase and calls them an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Turkey rejects as untenable Israel's claim that it struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase to prevent Turkish forces deploying there. Washington says it is working on a deconfliction mechanism between Turkey, Israel and Syria.

The Israeli military says it has ordered criminal investigations into the January 2024 killing of five-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza City and into the killings of Palestinian paramedics and rescue workers. Israel had previously said its forces were unaware of the vehicle Hind Rajab was in.

The International Criminal Court calls the US sanctions on its president, Tomoko Akane, and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye a 'flagrant attack' on the tribunal's independence. Japan separately calls the designations 'unfortunate'.
The BBC reports that thousands of people remain missing in Gaza, with recovery and identification work far behind the scale of the task and families still searching for answers.
Syria arrests an Assad-era officer who had fled Austria after being convicted there.

An Israeli airstrike on a Gaza police station kills nine Palestinians, medics say; Al Jazeera reports the strike hit the Gaza City police headquarters and killed the head of the women's police. Israel has not published its account of the target.

Sources tell The Straits Times that the Mossad chief and Syria's foreign minister discussed Turkish military deployments before Israel's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase. Neither government has confirmed the meeting.
Lebanon hands a former Assad-era Syrian army general to Damascus after an arrest warrant, the first such transfer since Assad's fall.

The Israeli military confirms its soldiers fired at the car in which five-year-old Hind Rajab was killed in Gaza City in January 2024, reversing its earlier account, and opens a criminal investigation. Her family says it does not trust the Israeli judiciary.
The United States commits US$206 million towards an international stabilisation force for Gaza, despite its 15-point peace plan remaining deadlocked.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decides not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian World Central Kitchen aid worker in Gaza.

Israel opens bidding for construction in a highly sensitive area of the occupied West Bank; critics say the project would sever the northern West Bank from the south. Britain's foreign minister says he plans sanctions over settlement expansion.
US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee warns Israeli settlers not to take land belonging to Palestinian Americans.
The BBC reports multiple deadly Israeli strikes across Gaza in under 24 hours. Casualty figures are from Gaza health officials and have not been independently verified.

Israel and Turkey step up warnings over Syria after Israel's bombing of the Abu al-Duhur airbase; Syria says no Turkish military build-up is planned there. The Straits Times reports Netanyahu is putting Turkey in Israel's crosshairs as an election approaches.

An Assad-era officer is extradited to Syria to face war crimes charges, the first such extradition since Assad's fall, after Lebanon handed a former Assad-era general to Damascus under an arrest warrant.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times, Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada issue a joint statement demanding Israel withdraw plans for more than 1,200 homes in the E1 area of the occupied West Bank, a day after Israel opened bidding. The UN has said the E1 plan poses an 'existential threat' to a contiguous Palestinian state; Israel rejects the criticism.
Australia says it is 'outraged' after Israel decided not to open a criminal investigation into the killing of an Australian aid worker in Gaza.

Thirty settler families move into Kadim, outside Jenin in the occupied West Bank, 21 years after a previous Israeli government evacuated it under the 2005 Disengagement Plan; the current government has overturned a 20-year ban on settlement around Jenin. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, the Justice Minister and the Knesset Speaker attend the ceremony. All settlements are illegal under international law; Israel disputes this.
ICC president Tomoko Akane, sanctioned by Washington on Aug 18, warns the measures point towards the 'demise of international rule of law'.

The UK, Canada and Australia issue a joint statement calling 'shameful' Israel's decision not to open a criminal investigation into the April 2024 strikes on a World Central Kitchen convoy that killed seven aid workers. Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, says there was 'no criminal intention' and therefore no criminal responsibility.
Israeli forces shoot dead a Palestinian teenager after settlers entered a West Bank village, according to Palestinian officials. The Israeli military's account has not been reported alongside it.

Israel rejects Turkey's move to seek an Interpol red notice for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the Gaza aid flotilla case, calling it a 'pathetic attempt' to intimidate its leaders and soldiers. Netanyahu calls President Recep Tayyip Erdogan an 'antisemitic dictator'.
Former French and British ambassadors urge Paris and London to take joint action on the Palestinian territories, where violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank has surged since the Gaza war began.

Israel says it fired at a 'terrorist' in southern Syria; Syria's foreign ministry says an Israeli drone hit a civilian car near Beit Jinn, west of Damascus, calling it a 'blatant violation' of Syrian sovereignty. Syrian state TV reports one person injured. It is the second Israeli strike in Syria in a week, after the Abu al-Duhur airbase attack the US called an 'unnecessary escalation'.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Israeli military, Syrian foreign ministry)

timeline.event: The Straits Times reports that the widening confrontation between Israel and Turkey could reshape the region, with Syria - which physically separates the two - bearing the brunt of their rivalry.

Syria's government condemns the Israeli strike on the village of Beit Jinn, south-west of Damascus, as a violation of its sovereignty and of international law; officials say it hit a civilian vehicle and injured several people. The Israeli military says it targeted a 'terrorist' in the 'final stages' of preparing attacks posing an immediate threat to its soldiers.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, The Straits Times (Syrian officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: US ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack says the earlier Israeli strike on the Abu al-Duhur airbase could be 'the Israelis baiting the Turks' in an attempt to draw Ankara into a conflict. Washington had already called that strike an 'unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability'.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani says he expects security talks with Israel to resume soon despite an absence of trust, with Damascus seeking an Israeli withdrawal from Syrian land and an end to strikes. He says the US is pressing Israel to return to negotiations, and denies Syria allowed Turkish forces at the airbase Israel bombed this week.

Syria and Israel hold high-level US-mediated talks in Jordan, focused on practical mechanisms to halt Israeli strikes, arrests and targeted operations and on reviving negotiations towards a security agreement, Syria's state news agency SANA reports citing a diplomatic source. Israel's prime minister's office did not comment.

At the Jordan talks, Damascus says its immediate priorities remain an Israeli withdrawal to positions held before Bashar al-Assad's overthrow on 8 Dec 2024 and full restoration of the 1974 disengagement agreement, and that it will not accept limits on rebuilding its armed forces, according to SANA.

Syrian state news agency SANA reports that Syria and Israel held further US-mediated talks aimed at easing tensions, following the round held in Jordan on 23 August. Israel's prime minister's office has not commented.

Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz warned of 'forceful actions' after four kites were found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, about 800m from the Gaza boundary, and several more elsewhere in southern Israel. The Israeli military said the kites carried no suspicious materials and posed no threat. Hamas denied responsibility, called them 'basically children's toys from displacement camps', and accused Israel of using them as a pretext for continued strikes despite the ceasefire agreed last October.
Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked a ship off Saudi Arabia's Yanbu. There was no Saudi confirmation of the claim.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli fire killed two young children. The account comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

The United States removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism after 47 years, and removed Hayat Tahrir al-Sham from its list of global terrorist organisations. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it recognised Damascus distancing itself from international terrorism; Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani called it a 'historic step'. Syria remains at the centre of tension between Israel and Turkey.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa said Syria 'shakes off a dark stain and tears away a painful chapter of its past' after the US removed the country from its state-sponsors-of-terrorism list, thanking President Trump. The Treasury announced corresponding sanctions relief; Hayat Tahrir al-Sham was also delisted as a global terrorist organisation.

Far-right Israeli lawmaker and settler activist Zvi Sukkot took a sledgehammer to a Palestinian memorial in Madama in the northern occupied West Bank while under military escort. The army said the demolition was unauthorised and a misuse of security protection, that soldiers stopped it and removed him, and that it viewed the incident with 'utmost severity'; Foreign Minister Gideon Saar and opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot also criticised him.

Parents in Gaza were urged to stop children flying kites after Israel's warning to Hamas over kites found near the boundary. Israel's defence minister had threatened 'forceful actions'; the Israeli military says the kites carried nothing dangerous and Hamas calls them children's toys.

Medics in Gaza said Israeli attacks killed five people including two children. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented on the specific incident.

An official on President Trump's US-led 'Board of Peace' said all militant activity in Gaza must stop, including the flying of kites, and added that 'Israel, too, must comply with the ceasefire' and that military action cannot extend beyond genuine and imminent threats. The UN and Hamas called the kite warnings outrageous.

Israeli forces took control of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training centre between Kafr Aqab in east Jerusalem and the Qalandia refugee camp. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said the evacuation followed the law Israel passed severing ties with the agency; UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the raid. The centre, opened in 1952, trains about 340 West Bank Palestinians a year.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UNRWA, Israeli PM's office)

timeline.event: Syria's Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announced their dissolution as part of an agreed integration into the Damascus government's structures.
President Trump sent a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress, while saying Riyadh must recognise Israel.
Israeli forces have taken control of a UN training centre for Palestinians, The Straits Times reports. UNRWA has not said whether courses there will continue.

Israel's seizure of UNRWA's Qalandia vocational training college in East Jerusalem drew international condemnation. Israel's government says the site was evacuated lawfully; UNRWA disputes the basis for the takeover.
A far-right Israeli lawmaker damaged a Palestinian memorial with a sledgehammer, footage of the incident showed.
Lebanon accused Israel of setting fire to forest and farmland in the south of the country. Israel has not commented on the accusation.
US Senate Democrats urged Israel to rein in settler violence in the West Bank.
Turkey said the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces would help Syrian unity, a day after the SDF announced it was integrating into Damascus government structures.

The United States designated the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation and imposed sanctions on it. The group has previously said its actions target arms manufacturing sites.
An Israeli court acquitted, on grounds of mental health, the man filmed on CCTV attacking a nun in Jerusalem.
A funeral was held in the West Bank for Sliman Mansour, one of the best-known Palestinian artists of his generation.

Israeli strikes killed at least three Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, health officials in Gaza said. The figure comes from Gazan medical sources and has not been independently verified; the Israeli military has not commented.

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's envoy for Gaza, criticised both Israeli strikes and Hamas's actions and warned that a collapse of last October's ceasefire would be 'a point of no return' for the region.

The UN human rights office condemned the United States' designation of the UK-based group Palestine Action as a foreign terrorist organisation, saying the label risks criminalising protest. The State Department announced the designation, with sanctions, on 26 August.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights)

timeline.event: A former British-Israeli hostage held by Hamas married in Tel Aviv, in one of the more visible personal milestones since last October's ceasefire.
An Israeli air strike killed a Hamas operative and two other people near Jenin in the occupied West Bank, the Israeli military said, in a rare use of air power in the territory.
The BBC published the results of a week spent tracking settler violence in the occupied West Bank, documenting incidents against Palestinian communities.

Druze factions blocked students from sitting examinations in a dispute with the Syrian government, The Straits Times reported, the latest friction between Damascus and communities in the south as the new government consolidates control.

Dozens of Israeli settlers attack the Palestinian village of Qusra near Nablus in the northern occupied West Bank, residents and the Israeli military say. A resident tells AFP a small group approached villagers working on a house, then returned with dozens more, surrounded them and threw stones. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the attack, a rare step; Israeli forces deploy to the site.

Israel's military says it struck a Hamas commander "hiding within the compound" of Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, saying medical facilities must not be used for militant activity. Gaza health officials say Israeli strikes elsewhere in the territory killed four people. Both accounts are contested and not independently verified.
Druze factions in southern Syria block students from sitting state examinations in a dispute with the Damascus government, The Straits Times reports.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemns the settler attack on the West Bank village of Qusra, calling it a criminal act that does not represent Israeli society; the Israeli military says it has opened an investigation. Palestinian residents say the village had been under a supply blockade for weeks before the attack.

The Straits Times reports that killings of Palestinian children and teenagers by Israeli forces and settlers have risen sharply in the occupied West Bank this year. Israel says its forces operate against militants; the two accounts of individual incidents frequently diverge and are rarely independently adjudicated.

An Israeli air strike near a bakery in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza kills a man and a three-year-old boy and wounds several others, Gaza health officials say; the Israeli military says it attacked a Hamas militant. Gazan health officials say more than 1,300 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect, while the Israeli military says four Israeli soldiers have been killed. Both tallies come from parties to the conflict.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: An AFP investigation reports that Israeli forces and settlers have killed Palestinian children and teenagers in the occupied West Bank at an average of about seven a month since October 2023, against roughly one a month before. Families say Israeli military investigations rarely produce accountability; the Israeli military says it investigates such deaths.
Israel's far-right national security minister publicly boasts of having worsened prison conditions for Palestinian security prisoners.

The Straits Times publishes an analysis of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's position on settler violence, noting he condemned the Qusra attack while continuing to back far-right coalition partners. No new strikes or casualties were reported in Gaza or Lebanon in the preceding 24 hours.

The UK Foreign Office says it has raised with Israeli authorities the detention of Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old British student activist forcibly detained by Israeli settlers in Umm al-Kheir in the occupied West Bank on Saturday before being arrested.

An Israeli strike killed at least five Palestinians in Gaza on Monday, health officials say: two killed and several wounded when a strike hit a crowd near the municipal public park in Gaza City, an area densely populated with displaced families, and at least three more killed later when a strike hit a vehicle in the Tel Al-Hawa neighbourhood. The Israeli military said it targeted Hamas militants in the first strike and did not immediately comment on the second. Casualty figures come from Gaza health officials.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Israel and Greece sign a EUR 3 billion (S$4.43 billion) agreement under which Israel will build a multi-layered air defence system for Greece, named "Achilles Shield", to be delivered by 2036. Israel's defence ministry confirmed the signing.

Raam leader Mansour Abbas announces that Yoav Segalovitz, a former Israeli police official and until recently a Yesh Atid member of the Knesset, will run on the moderate Islamist party's list in the 27 October election — the first Jewish Israeli to stand for an explicitly Arab party. Raam will campaign on an anti-crime platform. Segalovitz said there is “a difficult history between Arabs and Jews in this country, but there is also a shared future”.

An Israeli-backed raid to detain a Hamas figure in Gaza City is discovered mid-operation. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz says a senior Hamas member was captured, and an Israeli security official says the man detained heads Hamas's internal security service. Gaza officials and medics say air strikes launched to cover the force's withdrawal killed at least four people near the Katiba area of western Gaza City — two children and a woman among them — with another child killed in central Gaza; witnesses described at least 12 missiles fired into an area crowded with displaced families. Hamas government media office director Ismail al-Thawabta says the Israeli unit was detected before it could finish. Casualty figures come from Gaza medical sources and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (Israeli defence ministry, Gaza medics, Hamas media office)

timeline.event: Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar warns Israel will retaliate if the UK imposes sanctions over the potential expansion of West Bank settlements. The warning came shortly after British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband told Parliament he would introduce a 'comprehensive reset' of policy on Israel in the coming weeks, including examining how to stop UK companies financing, constructing or advertising new settlements.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accuses security officials of deliberately failing to wake him on the morning of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack, insisting the assault would have been contained had he intervened earlier - a day after his wife claimed an opposition figure knew of the attack in advance, prompting a threatened lawsuit. Netanyahu faces close-fought elections later in 2026. The 7 October attack killed more than 1,200 people in Israel and saw 251 taken hostage; Gaza authorities report more than 73,000 Palestinians killed in the offensive that followed.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli and Gaza authorities)

timeline.event: Unifil says the Israeli military has established four new bases in the areas of southern Lebanon it invaded, bringing the number of Israeli positions to nine, and reports consolidation and fortification of those positions along with demolition and engineering work. The strip under Israeli control is about 5 per cent of Lebanese territory and extends up to 10km from the border in places. A Lebanese intelligence official says Lebanon's military has recorded more than 5,000 violations of the June deal by Israel; the Israeli military says the buildings destroyed were used by Hezbollah for military purposes and that it acts in accordance with international law.
timeline.source: BBC (Unifil, Lebanese intelligence official, Israeli military)

timeline.event: More than 10 EU countries say they are willing to contribute to a planned European mission to train the Lebanese army.

Israel says a Hamas security chief was captured during a raid in Gaza City in which strikes killed four people, according to Gaza medics. Hezbollah's leader Naim Qassem last week called the US-brokered framework for the group's disarmament 'surrender with humiliation'.

Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry says Israeli attacks have killed more than 900 people in the territory so far in 2026 despite the ceasefire, taking the total since the 10 October truce past 1,300, including 301 children. The ministry does not separate civilians from combatants. The UN considers the figures reliable and BBC Verify says independent analysis is consistent with them; the Israeli military disputes the count, saying there is no basis to assume all those listed were killed by its activity, and says five of its soldiers have been killed in combat since the ceasefire.

A BBC team travelling with Unifil inside the part of southern Lebanon under Israeli control reports entire villages flattened, with air strikes and demolitions continuing after the ceasefire announced in June. Lebanese officials say Israel is expanding its positions in the zone.

Two Palestinian teenagers are killed in an attack by Israeli settler militants and army troops on their village in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday, local officials and the Palestinian health ministry say, amid an uptick in settler violence in the territory. Israel has not published its own account.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Palestinian health ministry, local officials)

timeline.event: The Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, named after a Shi'ite scholar whose shrine sits at its summit, has become one of the most contested pieces of ground in the Israel-Hezbollah war, according to a Straits Times explainer from Beirut.

Netanyahu visits Israeli forces inside the Gaza Strip, his first trip there since the October 2025 ceasefire, and rejects mediators' push for a US-backed plan requiring withdrawal. 'We control the area. We are not retreating. We are staying on this line,' he says near the Yellow Line, adding that Israel controls 60 per cent of the strip. Hamas has not responded publicly to the visit.
Rights groups urge US lawmakers to drop a provision that would deepen American defence ties with Israel.
Lebanon receives the first of five Lebanese detainees Israel has agreed to free as part of continuing talks between the two governments.
The US House of Representatives passes a bill to penalise university boycotts of Israel. It still requires Senate action.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (US House of Representatives)

timeline.event: Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir, campaigning ahead of close-fought elections, sets out a plan to remove Palestinians from Gaza: 250,000 in the first year and the remaining roughly two million over the following six. He claims unnamed countries are 'ready' to take them and says the plan does not amount to forcing anyone out. No government decision has been announced. Forced displacement of civilians in occupied territory is a war crime under the Geneva Conventions.

The Israeli military says it has cleared Hezbollah fighters from tunnels beneath the Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, one of the most contested positions of the conflict. Hezbollah has not confirmed the account and the claim has not been independently verified.

With Israeli elections approaching, more of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition partners publicly back removing Palestinians from Gaza, after National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir set out a staged plan earlier in the day. Such proposals are opposed by Palestinian officials and by Israel's main mediators.
Thousands of Lebanese students remain displaced as the school year approaches, with schools in the south destroyed or occupied and families still unable to return home.

The Israeli military says it struck southern Lebanon after Hezbollah launched a drone towards Israeli soldiers. Lebanon's health ministry says three people were killed and 23 wounded, including medics, women and children, and Lebanon's state National News Agency reports strikes across the south. Hezbollah did not immediately comment. Both accounts come from parties to the conflict and are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Israeli military, Lebanese health ministry, Lebanese NNA)

timeline.event: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee, visiting the West Bank town of Turmus Ayya, says categorically that there is no Israeli plan to displace Palestinians out of Gaza against their will, after Defence Minister Israel Katz and far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir floated mass removal this week.

Huckabee meets relatives of US citizens killed by Israeli settlers in Turmus Ayya, calling the attackers a 'tiny group' who damage Israel's reputation and urging prosecutions. Palestinian Americans and local officials dispute his characterisation and press for stronger US pressure on Israel.

The Israeli military says it is striking southern Lebanon early on Sunday in retaliation for Hezbollah firing two drones at Israeli soldiers stationed in an area Israel has declared a security zone. Hezbollah has not publicly commented on the launches.

Lebanon's health ministry says Israeli strikes killed at least seven people in southern Lebanon on Sunday - two men near the zone occupied by Israeli troops, two women in Arab Salim and three in a separate drone strike on Nabatieh al-Tahta - with six others wounded, including two girls. Israel says it struck Hezbollah weapons storage sites and a command centre inside a building formerly used as a hospital, in retaliation for Hezbollah drone attacks, and says it used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to limit civilian harm. Figures are the Lebanese ministry's and the targeting account is Israel's; neither has been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (Lebanese health ministry, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Muslim-majority nations warn that Israeli plans to remove Palestinians from Gaza threaten the US-brokered peace framework. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said on 2 September that the government had such plans.

An Israeli strike on a vehicle in western Gaza City kills Youssef Akila and his eight-year-old daughter Wafaa and wounds six others, says Mohamed Abu Selmia, head of Al Shifa Hospital. An Israeli military spokesperson says forces targeted a Hamas militant and were still reviewing the results. Two further Israeli strikes later on Sunday killed two more people, including a child, medics say. The casualty accounts are from Gaza medical officials and have not been independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Gaza health officials, Israeli military)

timeline.event: President Joseph Aoun's office calls the day's Israeli strikes 'a dangerous escalation' that hit 'purely civilian administrations and health centres', saying they destroyed an out-of-service hospital and damaged a finance ministry building, and urges the United States and the international community to act. Israel says its targets were Hezbollah weapons stores and a command centre.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Lebanese presidency, Israeli military)

timeline.event: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu orders unauthorised settler outposts in the occupied West Bank to be dismantled, two people familiar with the matter say, amid US pressure over settler attacks on Palestinians. No start date was given. UN bodies and most governments consider all Israeli settlements illegal under international law; Israel argues the territory is disputed rather than occupied.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, CNA (sources familiar with the matter)

timeline.event: Israeli warplanes strike a residential building in Kfar Rumman in southern Lebanon just after midnight, killing nine people including two children and wounding five, and a separate drone strike on a civilian vehicle in the town kills two medics, Lebanon's National News Agency says - at least 11 dead. The agency says no online evacuation warning was issued; the Israeli military did not immediately respond to questions about the strikes. A warning was issued just after 2am for areas around a building in another southern town where it said it would hit Hezbollah facilities.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Lebanon's National News Agency, Israeli military)

timeline.event: A separate Israeli drone strike on a civilian vehicle in Kfar Rumman kills two medics, taking the town's toll for the night to at least 11 including two children, Lebanon's National News Agency says. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to questions on the strikes or the absence of an evacuation warning.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Lebanon's National News Agency)

timeline.event: Israel says its strikes in Lebanon respond to Hezbollah violations of the June truce, saying they hit weapons stores and a command centre after drone attacks on its troops.

Defence Minister Israel Katz says he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have instructed the military to prepare for 'full-scale war' against the Palestinian Authority if its security bodies initiate an Oct 7-style attack, including targeted killings of senior figures and a permanent military presence in evacuated areas. The statement follows a stabbing attack in the northern West Bank.

Nickolay Mladenov, high representative for Gaza under the US-backed Board of Peace, says at the Hili Forum that a two-state solution is becoming 'practically impossible', citing West Bank violence and a Gaza now more than half under Israeli army control with the remainder held by Hamas.
Germany asks the International Court of Justice to throw out a case brought over its arms exports to Israel.

Israeli troops shoot dead a Palestinian during a village raid by settlers from a nearby outpost in the occupied West Bank, and kill another Palestinian who entered an outpost and stabbed a settler, officials say. Both accounts come from Israeli and Palestinian officials and have not been independently verified.

Two Israeli air strikes on the southern Lebanese village of Kfar Rumman kill at least 12 people, including two children and four women, Lebanon's health ministry says; one strike hit a building and another a car, killing a paramedic with the Islamic Risala Scout Association. The Israeli military says the strikes retaliated for two Hezbollah drone attacks on its troops and targeted a militant moving weapons. The toll is the Lebanese health ministry's.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA, AP (Lebanese health ministry; Israeli military)

timeline.event: A UN expert says Israel's clearing of Gaza rubble could destroy evidence of possible atrocity crimes, noting the assault has generated around 61 million tons of wreckage that could take seven years to clear.

Britain prepares to impose a trade ban on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, a measure that goes beyond its previous settlement sanctions though its direct trade impact is expected to be limited.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main political challenger accuses him of prioritising his own survival over Israel's security, as domestic argument over the widening fronts sharpens.
The BBC reports that Palestinian parents in the occupied West Bank fear for their children's safety on the way to school as settler attacks increase.
Britain says it will announce a trade ban on goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, going beyond its earlier sanctions on individual settlers.
France's foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot says Paris will launch a process to ban products from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, citing rising settler violence.
Netanyahu comes under fire over a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Israel ahead of the October 2023 Hamas attack; the Prime Minister's Office calls the report 'an absolute lie'.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Haaretz; Israeli PM's office)

timeline.event: Netanyahu moves to consolidate Israel's fractious right-wing parties before a Tuesday registration deadline, with opinion polls forecasting an election defeat.

Britain announces sanctions and a trade ban covering goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank; the foreign secretary accuses settlers of carrying out the 'ethnic cleansing' of Palestinians. Israel rejects the characterisation.
Israel's foreign minister says Israel is closing the British consulate in East Jerusalem in response, and accuses Britain of interfering in Israel's upcoming elections.
timeline.source: CNA, The Straits Times (Israeli foreign ministry)

timeline.event: Ministers from a dozen countries say they will back or consider curbs on trade in goods from Israeli settlements in the West Bank, saying Israel's actions there are undermining the possibility of a two-state solution. Israel's government calls the move a 'big mistake'.
timeline.source: CNA, BBC (joint ministerial statement; Israeli government)

timeline.event: A UN commission investigating Syria says it is deeply alarmed by Israeli military activity inside Syrian territory and warns that some actions, including detentions, may amount to war crimes. Israel disputes the commission's mandate.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (UN commission of inquiry)

timeline.event: The BBC assesses British-Israeli relations to be at their lowest ebb in decades following the settlement trade ban and the consulate closure.

Israel tells the British consulate in East Jerusalem that it must close and that diplomats assigned there will lose their accreditation within 30 days, an Israeli official and two other sources say. The move follows Britain's settlement trade ban.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Israeli official and sources familiar with the matter)

timeline.event: Israel says it will open an embassy in Slovenia as relations thaw, a rare warming on the same day its rift with Britain deepened.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar says the government has no plans to deport Palestinians from Gaza, after two Israeli ministers floated mass-removal proposals earlier this month.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham defends the ban on imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank in parliament, saying Britain has to 'stand for something'. Israel rejects the policy.
The BBC reports from Khan al-Ahmar, a Palestinian community in the West Bank's E1 area that Israel has earmarked for settlement construction and Britain opposes.

An Israeli airstrike kills a man, his wife and their daughters aged eight and 12 in a house in Beit Lahiya in northern Gaza, health officials say, as the military escalates strikes on houses over two days. The Israeli military did not immediately comment. Casualty figures come from Gaza health authorities.

Medics in Gaza say shortages of engine oil and spare parts are causing hospital generators to seize up, with power cuts cascading through one of the territory's largest functioning hospitals. Gaza has had no grid electricity since the start of Israel's offensive, and neighbourhood generator power is becoming unaffordable for families.
A film premiered at the Venice festival features Israeli whistleblowers giving accounts of the civilian toll in Gaza.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says he will sue a newspaper over a report claiming the UAE warned him ahead of the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack. The newspaper stands by its reporting.
The Israeli military says it destroyed a Hezbollah underground complex at Ali al-Taher in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah has not confirmed the loss and the claim has not been independently verified.
