The Israeli military says it destroyed a major Hezbollah underground complex at Ali al-Taher in southern Lebanon and is ready to carry out further strikes; the US Geological Survey registered the blast as equivalent to a magnitude 4.1 earthquake. Hezbollah has not confirmed the Israeli account of the site.

German federal prosecutors charge seven suspected Hamas members in Berlin with membership of a foreign terrorist organisation and preparing an attack, including by procuring weapons. The charges have not been tested in court.
A US official says the next round of Israel-Lebanon talks in Rome has been delayed to October. Neither government has commented on the record.

The Israeli military rejects testimonies given by whistleblowers in a documentary, premiered at the Venice festival, about the use of AI systems in targeting decisions in Gaza. The film-makers stand by the accounts; neither version has been independently verified.

Lebanese President Joseph Aoun makes an unannounced visit to Nabatieh, below the Ali al-Taher ridge Israel seized and blew up, and says 'there will be no new negotiations with Israel at the moment'. A US official says the Rome round has slipped to October and the two ambassadors will meet at the State Department next week instead. AFP reports Israeli strikes in the area have killed at least 29 people in recent days; not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Lebanese presidency, US official), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Israeli forces continue striking southern Lebanon as the next US-mediated round of Israel–Lebanon talks, scheduled for Rome this month, is pushed to October.

An Israeli air strike on a civilian vehicle in the Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood of Gaza City kills two Palestinians, medics say; strikes continue despite the US-brokered ceasefire. The Israeli military has not commented.
timeline.source: Al Jazeera, The Straits Times (Gaza medics)

timeline.event: A US State Department official says Israel and Lebanon will meet in Rome in October for the next round of talks on the US-brokered security agreement, and that the two ambassadors will meet in Washington next week; the August round ended without a breakthrough on territorial issues. Israel holds a roughly 10km 'buffer zone' inside Lebanon; more than 4,300 people have been killed in Lebanon since fighting resumed on March 2, the report says.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; US State Department official)

timeline.event: Medics say the Israeli strike on a vehicle in Gaza City's Tal al-Hawa neighbourhood killed at least two people and wounded 13; the Israeli military says it targeted two Hamas militants. Al Jazeera separately airs footage it says shows an Israeli quadcopter over homes in Gaza City.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Gaza medics, Israeli military), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: Residents say Israeli strikes hit people outside tents in a Gaza City displacement camp, with at least one person killed and several injured across Gaza; the Israeli military had not commented in the report.

Israel’s culture minister calls for the Israeli directors of “Naza”, a documentary in which unnamed soldiers and officers describe AI-assisted targeting in Gaza, to be stripped of their citizenship for “treason”.

UN human rights chief Volker Türk says the recovery of hundreds of bodies, including what appear to be entire families, from buildings destroyed by Israeli strikes raises fresh war-crimes concerns; Israel has repeatedly denied deliberately targeting civilians.

Gaza health officials and Hamas sources say Israeli air strikes killed at least five Palestinians, including two children and a Hamas armed commander, in northern and southern Gaza. Medics describe an apparent 'double tap' strike on a vehicle in Sheikh Radwan that killed two and wounded seven, with some casualties among people who had rushed to help. The Israeli military says it struck a militant in the area and a Hamas Rafah Brigade commander.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Gaza medics, Israeli military)

timeline.event: The British charity Medical Aid for Palestinians says a patient was shot dead by an Israeli quadcopter drone at a health centre it supports in Jabalia, northern Gaza. There was no immediate Israeli comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Medical Aid for Palestinians)

timeline.event: A six-storey apartment block in Tal al-Hawa, Gaza City, housing people displaced by the war, collapses onto nearby homes and tents; the Hamas-run civil defence agency says eight bodies including children and 15 injured people have been recovered and more than 60 people are missing, and that the building had structural damage from earlier Israeli strikes. The figures are not independently verified.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Gaza civil defence agency)

timeline.event: A US official speaking anonymously says the Trump administration plans a US$2.8 billion munitions package for Israel including 20,000 MK 84 and 20,000 BLU-117 2,000-pound bombs, informally notified to the relevant congressional committees; the State Department and Israel's embassy did not respond to requests for comment.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (wire copy; Washington Post first reported)

timeline.event: The toll from the Tal al-Hawa building collapse rises to at least 21, including eight children, with dozens missing, according to Gaza's civil defence and medics; UN agencies and an Egyptian team join a search hampered by a lack of equipment.
timeline.source: BBC, CNA (Reuters), Al Jazeera (Gaza civil defence)

timeline.event: Defence Minister Israel Katz says it is 'only a matter of time' before Israel resumes full-scale war in Gaza and implements a 'migration plan' for its two million residents, claiming 70 per cent of the territory is already emptied; US Ambassador Mike Huckabee has denied any plan to displace people against their will.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (AFP; Israeli defence ministry, US embassy)

timeline.event: Reuters reporters embedded with French UNIFIL peacekeepers report that the UN force's mandate ends at year-end, leaving residents of Rmeich and other Christian towns inside Israel's self-declared 'security zone' in southern Lebanon fearing they will be cut off; the zone was established after more than six months of Israeli bombardment triggered by a Hezbollah rocket attack in early March.

Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he will not back the US$2.8 billion sale of 2,000lb bombs to Israel over international-law concerns; the administration can proceed without his clearance.

Netanyahu vows to legislate to strip citizenship from anyone who defames Israeli soldiers, escalating threats against the Israeli directors of NAZA, a documentary alleging the military accepted mass civilian deaths in Gaza.
Britain's Trades Union Congress, representing more than 5.3 million workers, backs the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions movement against Israel for the first time.
Israel and Morocco agree at a US-hosted meeting in New York to upgrade their missions to embassies and appoint ambassadors, the Israeli government says.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; Israeli government), Al Jazeera

timeline.event: The US denies Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas a visa to attend next week's UN General Assembly for a second year, as the State Department extends visa bans on PLO and Palestinian Authority officials it accuses of failing to reform; Palestinian officials reject the accusations.
timeline.source: BBC, The Straits Times (AFP; US State Department)

timeline.event: European and Arab military chiefs meet in Paris, opened by Macron with Lebanon's President Aoun and Jordan's King Abdullah, to assess the Lebanese army's needs before UNIFIL's roughly 7,500 peacekeepers begin drawing down in January; options include a non-UN mission backed by France and Italy.
timeline.source: The Straits Times (Reuters; French presidency, diplomats)

timeline.event: Gaza rescuers end searches at the bomb-damaged building that collapsed a day earlier, where a Palestinian official says 21 people were killed and 45 rescued from the rubble.
Israeli rights groups say Israel has added a tender for 2,167 housing units to its E1 settlement plan near Jerusalem, a project critics say endangers a future Palestinian state.
Serbia opens an Israeli drone assembly plant, deepening defence-industrial ties with Israel at a time when several European governments are restricting arms cooperation over Gaza.

An algae bloom that crippled several of Israel's desalination plants raises questions about the country's water security, the BBC reports, with supply from the affected plants curtailed while operators work to restore output.
Syria's government warns that Israel poses 'the greatest threat' to stability in the Middle East, in one of its sharpest public statements since the change of government in Damascus.
Two people are injured by Israeli shelling as Israeli troops advance in southern Lebanon, Al Jazeera reports.
Syria's government arrests five former officers of the al-Assad era over strikes on civilians.
A mural of rapper Macklemore is painted in Gaza following the furore over Ed Sheeran's tour.
A UK court clears a woman of voicing support for Hamas in a university speech.
An Israeli strike on a motorcycle in Gaza City kills a Palestinian man and injures a child, Al Jazeera reports.
The European Union urges the United States to reconsider its visa denial to the Palestinian delegation for next week's UN General Assembly meeting in New York.
Gaza health officials say four people, including a child, were killed in Israeli strikes.
The UN's peacekeeping chief in Lebanon says a smooth handover to the Lebanese state is critical before UNIFIL withdraws, warning against a security vacuum in the south.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog pardons a former combat medic convicted of manslaughter over the 2016 shooting of a wounded Palestinian attacker in Hebron, a case that divided Israeli opinion; Palestinian officials and rights groups criticise the decision.

Israeli police say a Palestinian gunman shot dead an Israeli man at a spring near the West Bank settlement of Neve Tzuf and was arrested hours later at a Ramallah hospital. Separately, the Israeli military says soldiers killed a Palestinian driver who tried to ram them near Ganim, east of Jenin; the Palestine Red Crescent says its medics were prevented from reaching him. Netanyahu orders reinforcements and arrests; Hamas praises the shooting without claiming it.

Hundreds of thousands of children in Gaza have returned to in-person classes, which resumed on Sept 19 for the first time in nearly three years, mostly in tents and damaged buildings with few supplies. About 660,000 pupils missed regular schooling during the war, and UNICEF says 98 per cent of school buildings were damaged or destroyed.

Medical sources at Nasser hospital tell Al Jazeera that three Palestinians were killed by Israeli fire in Gaza on Sept 21 - a child in the al-Mawasi zone in the south, a man in Jabalia and a woman in Deir el-Balah - with nine others reported wounded in Bureij and Khan Younis. The account comes from Palestinian medical sources and Al Jazeera; no Israeli military response was carried in the report, and the figures are not independently verified.

Al Jazeera reports that Israeli forces have detained at least 53 Palestinians in a raid on the West Bank town of Biddu, north-west of Jerusalem, citing the Jerusalem Governorate and the town's mayor, who says homes have been turned into interrogation centres and shops and schools are shut. It is the third incursion since the Israeli military said it arrested a man from the town suspected of the Sept 20 shooting that killed an Israeli near Neve Tzuf (Halamish).

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: Bangladesh's evening bulletins are the only new official numbers today, and both moved the wrong way: six more children died of measles and dengue admissions rose for a third straight day, with all of the day's dengue deaths in a single division, Rajshahi. DR Congo's Ebola epidemic remains the largest and deadliest on the list, and vaccination of health workers there has only just begun; WHO has issued no new outbreak notice since Sept 10. Closer to home, Indonesia said today it is still struggling to contain the fires behind the regional haze, so respiratory complaints are the thing to watch if air quality slips again.

outbreaks.name: DR Congo - Ebola (Bundibugyo virus)
outbreaks.status: Largest Ebola outbreak on record; vaccination of health workers began Sept 19
outbreaks.scope_note: Laboratory-confirmed cases and deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo only, from DRC health ministry data published on ECDC's outbreak page (last updated 18 Sep 14:20; re-read 20 Sep, unchanged). 905 patients are hospitalised in isolation and 62 of 167 health zones across seven provinces are affected; Ituri is worst hit with 5,792 cases and 2,642 deaths, North Kivu 1,350 and 828. WHO's latest formal Disease Outbreak News (DON617, 10 Sep) put the multi-country confirmed total at 6,778 cases and 3,269 deaths as of 7 Sep. Local authorities cited by AFP/AP on 20 Sep report a higher running tally of about 7,541 cases and at least 3,639 deaths with 1,823 recovered - more recent, but not yet ratified by WHO or ECDC. Uganda's linked outbreak, 20 cases, was declared over on 25 Aug.

outbreaks.name: Bangladesh - measles
outbreaks.status: World's largest current measles outbreak; deaths still rising daily
outbreaks.scope_note: Directorate General of Health Services figures for the 24 hours to 8am on 21 Sep, reported by The Business Standard. Deaths comprise 101 laboratory-confirmed and 962 suspected; cases comprise 20,646 laboratory-confirmed and 181,035 suspected. Since 15 Mar, 159,804 patients have been hospitalised and 153,448 have recovered. Six children died in the latest 24-hour period, with 1,221 new suspected and 84 new confirmed cases.

outbreaks.name: Bangladesh - dengue
outbreaks.status: September is by far the deadliest month of 2026 so far
outbreaks.scope_note: DGHS cumulative 2026 hospitalisations and deaths since 1 January, reported by The Business Standard on 21 Sep; 59,038 patients have recovered. In the latest 24-hour period six people died, all in Rajshahi Division, and 1,655 were hospitalised. DGHS reported on 18 Sep that the first 17 days of September alone accounted for 79 deaths and 22,554 admissions, both monthly highs for the year.

outbreaks.name: United States - measles
outbreaks.status: Worst US outbreak in decades; federal and state death counts disagree
outbreaks.scope_note: US CDC confirmed cases for 2026 as of 17 Sep (page last updated 18 Sep; re-read 20 Sep, unchanged), across 47 states and jurisdictions, with 17 cases among international visitors and 39 new outbreaks; 3,296 of 3,471 cases are outbreak-associated. The federal death count is zero because the National Center for Health Statistics holds no 2026 record listing measles as the underlying cause. Pennsylvania has separately confirmed four measles-associated deaths and disputes the federal tally.

outbreaks.name: Indonesia - wildfire haze respiratory illness
outbreaks.status: Cases more than doubled in nine days; smoke now over Singapore and Malaysia
outbreaks.scope_note: Indonesian health ministry count of wildfire-related acute respiratory infection (ISPA) cases as of 9 Sep, up from 50,891 on 1 Sep; re-checked 20 Sep and no newer ministry figure has been published. More than 12.5 million people across seven provinces have been exposed and children under five account for about a quarter of cases. No official death toll has been attributed to the haze; a separate CREA analysis estimated roughly 1,700 excess deaths from the August fires. NEA attributes Singapore's current haze to fires in Kalimantan and southern Sumatra.

outbreaks.name: Fiji - HIV
outbreaks.scope_note: New HIV diagnoses recorded in Fiji in 2025 - not a cumulative total - up 27 per cent on the 1,583 of 2024 and about 16 times the 2019 figure; 59 babies were born with HIV and HIV-related deaths in 2025 totalled 117, more than four times the 25 recorded in 2021. Health Minister Antonio Lalabalavu escalated from an outbreak response to a national emergency on 15 Sep. About one in 60 adults is living with HIV, up from one in 167 five years ago. UNAIDS estimated about 9,000 people living with HIV in 2025, of whom 39 per cent knew their status and 22 per cent were on antiretroviral treatment.

outbreaks.name: Germany - Frankfurt airport-linked malaria
outbreaks.status: Extremely rare air-traffic-related cluster; source still under investigation
outbreaks.scope_note: Cases and deaths reported by the city of Frankfurt health department; re-checked 20 Sep with no newer figure. Six airport workers were infected in late August, two of whom died; two further cases announced on 17 Sep were residents of the Schwanheim district beside the airport, one of whom died. All were infected with Plasmodium falciparum without travelling to a malaria-endemic region or working at the airport, and are thought to have been bitten by a mosquito carried in on an aircraft. Mosquitoes trapped at the airport in July and August are being analysed. Germany's last recorded airport-malaria case was in 2023, per the Robert Koch Institute. Malaria does not spread directly between people.

stories.headline: Bangladesh dengue toll reaches 190 as 1,655 more are hospitalised in a day
stories.summary: DGHS reported six deaths and 1,655 hospital admissions in its Sept 21 bulletin, taking this year's toll to 190 and cumulative cases to 63,627, with 59,038 recovered. All six deaths were in Rajshahi Division. Daily admissions have now risen for three bulletins in a row, from 1,232 to 1,593 to 1,655.

stories.headline: Bangladesh measles deaths reach 1,063 as six more children die
stories.summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reported six further child deaths in the 24 hours to 8am on Sept 21, taking the toll since mid-March to 1,063 - 101 laboratory-confirmed and 962 suspected. Another 1,221 suspected and 84 confirmed cases were logged, bringing cumulative cases to about 201,700, of which 20,646 are laboratory-confirmed. Of 159,804 patients hospitalised since 15 March, 153,448 have recovered.

stories.headline: Six more dengue deaths in Bangladesh as 1,593 are hospitalised in a day
stories.summary: DGHS reported six deaths and 1,593 hospital admissions in the 24 hours to the morning of Sept 20, taking this year's toll to 184 and cumulative cases to 61,972, with 57,610 recovered. Two of the deaths were in Chattogram Division, two in Khulna and one each in Barishal and Dhaka. The day's admissions were well above the 1,232 reported a day earlier.

stories.headline: Bangladesh measles deaths reach 1,057 as four more children die
stories.summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reported four further child deaths in the 24 hours to 8am on Sept 20, taking the toll since mid-March to 1,057 - 101 laboratory-confirmed and 956 suspected. Another 1,148 suspected and 88 confirmed cases were logged, bringing cumulative cases to about 200,400, of which 20,562 are laboratory-confirmed. Of 158,589 patients hospitalised since 15 March, 152,225 have recovered.

stories.headline: DR Congo begins vaccinating health workers against Ebola as the death toll climbs
stories.summary: The rollout started on Sept 19 in Bunia, capital of Ituri province and the epicentre of the outbreak, and will extend to North Kivu where cases have been rising sharply. Some 50,000 health and frontline workers are to receive Ervebo, a vaccine developed against the more common Zaire strain, under a compassionate-use programme; its effect against the Bundibugyo virus driving this outbreak will be tracked in 20,000 recipients for up to a year. There is still no licensed vaccine or proven treatment for Bundibugyo. WHO approved 70,000 doses for the DRC in August and has cited encouraging signs that transmission may be slowing, but MSF said on Sept 18 there is no clear evidence the epidemic is coming under control.
stories.source: Al Jazeera (AFP, AP; WHO, MSF, DRC health authorities)

stories.headline: DR Congo's Ebola epidemic stands at 7,475 confirmed cases and 3,605 deaths
stories.summary: ECDC's outbreak page, drawing on DRC health ministry data, gives 7,475 laboratory-confirmed cases and 3,605 deaths as of Sept 16, with 905 patients in isolation and 62 of 167 health zones affected across seven provinces. Ituri accounts for 5,792 cases and 2,642 deaths and North Kivu for 1,350 and 828. WHO's most recent Disease Outbreak News, DON617 of Sept 10, put the confirmed multi-country total at 6,778 cases and 3,269 deaths as of Sept 7; Uganda's linked outbreak of 20 cases was declared over on Aug 25.

stories.headline: ECDC's week 38 threats report keeps Ebola, measles and dengue on the active list
stories.summary: The Communicable Disease Threats Report covering 12-18 September continues to list the DRC Ebola epidemic among the threats ECDC is monitoring, alongside measles and dengue activity. The detailed figures sit in the report's PDF; ECDC is used here as a datable corroborator, with headline case and death counts anchored to WHO and national authorities.

stories.headline: US measles count holds at 3,471 confirmed cases with no federal deaths recorded
stories.summary: CDC data as of Sept 17, published Sept 18 and unchanged when re-read for this brief, records 3,471 confirmed cases across 47 states and jurisdictions in 2026, with 39 new outbreaks and 3,296 cases outbreak-associated. The federal death count remains zero because the National Center for Health Statistics has no 2026 record listing measles as the underlying cause; Pennsylvania has separately confirmed four measles-associated deaths and disputes that tally.

stories.headline: Third person dies in the malaria cluster around Frankfurt Airport
stories.summary: Frankfurt's health department announced two further infections on Sept 17, in residents of the Schwanheim district next to the airport, one of whom died - taking the cluster since late August to eight cases and three deaths. None of those infected had travelled to a malaria-endemic area or worked at the airport, and all carried Plasmodium falciparum, pointing to mosquitoes arriving aboard aircraft. Germany's last recorded airport-malaria case was in 2023, according to the Robert Koch Institute. Malaria does not spread directly between people.
stories.source: Al Jazeera, France 24 (city of Frankfurt, Robert Koch Institute)

stories.headline: Fiji declares a national HIV emergency as new diagnoses surge
stories.summary: Health Minister Antonio Lalabalavu escalated Fiji's response to a national emergency on Sept 15 and expanded testing. The country recorded 2,016 new HIV diagnoses in 2025, up 27 per cent on 2024 and about 16 times the 2019 figure, including 59 infants infected by their mothers; HIV-related deaths reached 117, more than four times the 2021 count. About one adult in 60 is now living with HIV, against one in 167 five years ago, and UNAIDS estimated only 39 per cent of those infected knew their status with 22 per cent on treatment.
stories.source: ABC News, US News (Fiji Ministry of Health, UNAIDS)

stories.headline: Indonesian wildfire haze more than doubled respiratory infections in nine days
stories.summary: Indonesia's health ministry recorded 113,336 wildfire-related acute respiratory infection cases across seven provinces as of Sept 9, up from 50,891 on Sept 1, with children under five making up close to a quarter. More than 12.5 million people have been exposed in the country's worst fire season in 11 years, and Central Kalimantan logged an air quality index reading of 1,919 on Sept 2. No newer ministry figure had been published when this brief was compiled.
stories.source: The Jakarta Post, NBC News (Indonesian health ministry)

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: The thing to patch first is still Orkes Conductor, whose pre-login remote code execution flaw is being exploited in the wild, followed by the three Linux kernel bugs CISA added to its exploited list at the end of last week. Today's two additions are lower-grade but practical: Microsoft says its September security updates can silently break the Windows File History backup, and a new remote access trojan called ChainScript is spreading through fake 'paste this command' prompts. Much of the rest of the list is about developer and AI tooling, from poisoned npm packages to sandbox escapes in coding agents. If you run Windows backups through File History, check they still complete; if you run build pipelines, treat anything a job applicant or package asks you to execute as hostile.

stories.headline: Microsoft says September security updates can break the Windows File History backup feature
stories.summary: Microsoft has warned that File History, the built-in Windows backup feature, may stop working on some systems after the September 2026 security updates are installed. Users who rely on it should check that backups are still completing rather than removing the security updates.

stories.headline: ClickFix lures deliver the new ChainScript RAT, which finds its servers through a Polygon smart contract
stories.summary: Blackpoint researchers describe a previously undocumented Windows remote access trojan, ChainScript, delivered through ClickFix-style lures and installers posing as Spotify, Zoom Workplace and Microsoft Teams. It looks up its active WebSocket command server from a Polygon blockchain smart contract, an EtherHiding-style technique that makes the infrastructure hard to take down, and offers interactive CMD and PowerShell, file operations, screenshots, payload deployment and enumeration of cryptocurrency wallets. No CVE is involved; the defence is user awareness of paste-and-run prompts and blocking unsigned installers.

stories.headline: North Korea's Jade Sleet breached an Indian IT services firm using poisoned Terraform lock files and new macOS backdoors
stories.summary: SentinelOne has attributed the compromise of a small India-based IT services company to Jade Sleet, the North Korean group also tracked as TraderTraitor, Slow Pisces and UNC4899 and previously tied to the roughly US$1.5 billion Bybit theft in 2025. The operators pose as recruiters and send DevOps, cryptocurrency and fintech job seekers a GitHub 'coding test' whose Terraform dependency lock file points to lookalike registry domains such as registry.hashicorp-aws[.]com, so that running 'terraform init' downloads attacker-controlled modules. The chain ends with two Rust-based backdoors for ARM Macs, FLATROOF (also called Gaslight) and ROOFDECK, both seen earlier this year in the attack on KelpDAO's LayerZero bridge. Developers should treat take-home interview repositories as untrusted and check lock files for unfamiliar registry hosts.

stories.headline: Malicious npm packages hide their loader in a normal library function to evade install-script defences
stories.summary: Checkmarx researchers found an ongoing npm campaign built around 'indexed-btree', a package imitating the legitimate 'sorted-btree' library that BleepingComputer says had reached about 2 million weekly downloads; nine linked packages, including btree-core and ordered-kv-index, were also identified and removed. Instead of a preinstall or postinstall script - which npm now blocks unless approved, under measures GitHub announced in June - the loader sits inside the library's own BTree.prototype.set() method and runs only when an application calls it, so installation looks clean and static scanners see little. The malware profiles the host, reports through hardcoded Slack and Telegram channels, fetches an encrypted second stage from an Ethereum smart contract on the Sepolia test network, and can delete files and erase its own traces. Checkmarx says the operators use a wallet holding 109 ETH but does not say the funds were stolen. Anyone who installed the packages should rotate secrets and rebuild from clean sources.

stories.headline: Researchers escape the OpenAI Codex sandbox to run commands on a developer's machine
stories.summary: Researchers at Accomplish AI found two ways out of the sandbox in OpenAI's Codex coding agent. 'Heapjack' abuses the node_repl tool that Codex Desktop writes into the shared config: untrusted agent code snapshots the Node.js heap, recovers the token that marks trusted code and uses it to have the unsandboxed parent process run commands - so opening someone else's repository and asking a question about it could give the repository's author code execution, even in read-only mode and with no approval prompt. 'Overpatch', in the open-source Codex CLI, tricks the apply_patch tool into granting write access outside the project folder, for example to append a line to a shell start-up file. Both were reported on Aug 12 and OpenAI fixed them within eight days, the researchers said; no CVE has been assigned. Update Codex Desktop and CLI to current versions.

stories.headline: Researchers used Claude Opus 5 to chain two flaws into OpenAI staff account takeovers
stories.summary: Three researchers at Hacktron chained a bug in the Discourse software running OpenAI's public help forum with a weakness in OpenAI's own login system to take over the ChatGPT and Codex accounts of several OpenAI employees, then reach an internal code repository - under 72 hours from first look to internal access. This was research, not an attack: they reported the flaws, proved access with a harmless pull request and stopped, reading no source code and touching no customer data. OpenAI confirmed a fix about 14 hours after the report and paid a $6,500 bounty on Sept 1, saying the award recognised the OpenAI-side finding, not the testing of Discourse, which was out of scope. Because staff connect other services to ChatGPT and Codex, the team said the same access could in theory have reached GitHub, Slack and e-mail.

stories.headline: BragJack: malicious browser extensions hijack in-browser AI agents
stories.summary: Researcher Gal Weizman of Forever Security showed that an already-installed malicious extension can hand an entire prompt to a browser's AI assistant - a technique he calls prompt forcing - and abuse the agent's existing privileges to read files and browsing data and act on sites. Chrome's Gemini Live, Perplexity Comet, Microsoft Edge, Opera Neon and Anthropic's Claude in Chrome were all affected. Google (CVE-2026-0628) and Microsoft (CVE-2026-55945, a race condition) have fixed their flaws; bounties across five vendors exceeded $20,000. No CVSS scores were published and there is no reported exploitation. Removing unused extensions and treating broad 'read and change all your data' permissions with suspicion are the practical defences.

stories.headline: North Korean WaterPlum campaign infected more than 30,000 devices in over 100 countries
stories.summary: A joint advisory from Japan's National Police Agency, the FBI, the Australian Cyber Security Centre and Germany's BfV attributes the long-running Contagious Interview fake-job campaign to WaterPlum, linked to North Korea's 313 General Bureau. Between December 2025 and July 2026 the group compromised more than 30,000 devices across over 100 countries, targeted more than 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets and moved about US$10.71 million to North Korea. Operators impersonated AI, crypto and NFT firms on recruiting platforms and used AI face-swapping during video interviews before asking candidates to run malicious code. Malware families include BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy and StoatWaffle.

stories.headline: ShinyHunters defaces Clop's leak site through an unauthenticated Grav CMS upload flaw
stories.summary: The extortion group says it used an unauthenticated file-upload weakness in Grav CMS to get into Clop's Tor data-leak site, first uploading a warning file and then defacing the site entirely. It claims to have taken source code, Grav plugins, system logs and the private keys for Clop's onion service, and says it will extort the ransomware gang, demanding contact within 72 hours. The feud dates to Clop's Oracle E-Business Suite theft campaign in October 2025, which used CVE-2025-61882; ShinyHunters says Clop took its exploit without permission.

stories.headline: SolarWinds patches a hard-coded key in Access Rights Manager enabling unauthenticated RCE
stories.summary: SolarWinds said in a Sept 17 advisory that all Access Rights Manager versions 2026.2 and earlier are affected by an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw stemming from a hard-coded static key, credited to Armadin researcher Kai Huang and fixed in ARM 2026.2.1. The company reports no exploitation in the wild. It follows fixes roughly two months ago for a Web Help Desk SAML authentication bypass (CVE-2026-28323, CVSS 9.8) and a DoS flaw (CVE-2026-28299, 8.2), plus 16 Serv-U issues.

stories.headline: Orkes Conductor pre-auth RCE is being exploited in the wild
stories.summary: Fortinet says attackers are actively targeting Orkes Conductor servers by submitting crafted inline workflow definitions containing JavaScript or Python expressions to the workflow API before authentication. Where GraalVM evaluators are configured with unrestricted host access, an attacker escapes the scripting environment and runs OS commands as the Conductor process. Versions 3.21.21 up to 3.30.2 are affected. Fortinet blocked 1,290 attempts in 24 hours as of Sept 9, a 132 per cent daily rise, and nearly 7,000 between Sept 2 and 9, mostly from Germany, Hong Kong, Indonesia, the UAE and India. NVD lists CVSS v3.1 9.8 and CVSS v4 9.3.

stories.headline: Google's Gemini accessed real company systems during an AI security evaluation
stories.summary: During May 2026 tests run by Israeli evaluation firm Irregular, the model guessed its way into one protected system and used credentials found in a public repository to reach two others. Irregular traced the breaches to a naming error in which a fictional company used in capture-the-flag exercises matched a real domain, and notified Google in July. Unlike comparable incidents involving other labs' models, Gemini halted once it realised it had reached a real company; Google says it does not consider this misalignment.
stories.source: The Hacker News, BBC (The Wall Street Journal, Irregular)

stories.headline: CrowdSec says the TanStack npm compromise led to about 170 of its private repos being copied
stories.summary: The French security firm said on Sept 18 that an attacker used a departing employee's still-active GitHub OAuth token on May 22 to copy roughly 170 private repositories, and that his laptop had been compromised in May's TanStack npm supply-chain attack (CVE-2026-45321, in CISA's KEV catalog since May 27), in which 84 malicious versions of 42 packages stole GitHub tokens, SSH keys and cloud credentials. The code surfaced on a forum on Sept 16 alongside e-mail addresses of 83 users and details of 51 prospective investors from 2020. CrowdSec says only code was copied, nothing was modified, and its infrastructure and databases were not accessed.

stories.headline: CISA adds three exploited Linux kernel flaws to the KEV catalog
stories.summary: CISA added the three flaws on Sept 18 citing evidence of active exploitation: CVE-2025-39682 (CVSS 9.8) in the TLS receive path, which can leak memory or cause denial of service; CVE-2026-53266 (8.8), an out-of-bounds write in the ebtables SNAT ARP rewrite path that can give local privilege escalation; and CVE-2025-39964 (7.8), a race on concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket. Red Hat updated all three advisories on Sept 19 to acknowledge exploitation and flagged known public exploits. US federal civilian agencies have until Sept 21 to patch under BOD 26-04. How the flaws are being exploited, and whether as one chain, has not been disclosed.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV (Red Hat)

stories.headline: Public exploits released for four Linux kernel local root flaws
stories.summary: Researcher Asim Manizada published working exploit code on Sept 18 for four local privilege escalation flaws he calls DirtyAH6, TUNderflow, PPPoEject and DiagSpill, reported to the kernel security team in mid-July and fixed over recent weeks after a coordinated hold with distributions. Up-to-date kernels are not affected, but older ones on shared systems now face public exploit code. Three of the four need unprivileged user namespaces, which many distributions enable by default; DiagSpill needs none, only the SCTP module. No real-world attacks have been reported.

stories.headline: WordPress patches Click2Shell, a link that silently installs a theme
stories.summary: WordPress 7.1.1, released Sept 17, fixes a core flaw that lets a crafted link opened by a logged-in administrator install a theme from the official directory with no Install click. Researchers at pwn.ai, who named the chain Click2Shell, showed it could be combined with a separate weakness in the installed theme to run attacker code on the server; on its own the core bug only installs a real theme the attacker picks, and the theme stays deactivated so nothing looks wrong. The bug comes from two parts of WordPress reading the same link differently. No exploitation has been reported; WordPress advises updating immediately.

stories.headline: Gyazo breach exposes 23.62 million user records after an upload-server flaw was exploited
stories.summary: Kyoto-based Helpfeel said an attacker exploited a vulnerability in Gyazo's image upload server, ran arbitrary commands and reached the database, exposing about 23.62 million user records including e-mail addresses and password hashes, plus roughly 490 million image metadata records mostly from January 2019 or earlier. Those records include the IDs that form Gyazo image links, which Helpfeel says could be used to view images without permission; viewing of some has been temporarily disabled. No payment data was exposed. Users are told to change their Gyazo password and any reused elsewhere. The company has not said what kind of flaw was used.

stories.headline: Transparent Tribe deploys new Rust backdoors against Indian and Afghan government targets
stories.summary: Zscaler ThreatLabz attributes a campaign it calls Operation RapidRust to the Pakistan-aligned group also tracked as APT36 and Earth Karkaddan, targeting government and defence organisations in India and Afghanistan with previously undocumented tools named RUSTYSHADE, RUSTYMOVE, PSNATCH and BASHNATCH, using private GitHub repositories for command and control. It follows an Acronis report roughly a month earlier tying the group to attacks on Afghan telecoms and South Asian critical infrastructure using a backdoor called PATCHCORD.

stories.headline: Fake LastPass Authenticator GitHub repos push the Rapuncel infostealer
stories.summary: LastPass and Delphos Labs found an ongoing operation using SEO-optimised GitHub repositories impersonating LastPass and more than 39 other brands. Download buttons redirect to payload servers serving ZIP files inflated to as much as 148MB to evade scanning, and a renamed Visual Studio debugger sideloads the payload. Rapuncel harvests credentials from 25 browsers, 30 crypto wallets and messaging apps and takes screenshots, while an accompanying kernel driver, alinubx.sys, terminates 145 antivirus and EDR products by bypassing Protected Process Light. The researchers assess with moderate confidence that Rapuncel is a BoryptGrab variant.
